title: New intel on the World of Warcraft movie
content: According to the information available, the World of Warcraft movie is co-produced by Blizzard Entertainment and Legendary Pictures, and distributed by Warner Bros. The director has been confirmed as Sam Raimi, the director of Spider-Man. Earlier reports had it that the Warcraft movie would be titled The Rise of the Lich King and open in 2011, and that David Wenham might play Arthas. Other reports said the film would be set one year before World of Warcraft (isn’t that the timeframe of Cycle of Hatred? that story was pretty boring), and would tell its story from the perspective of ordinary people. That one doesn’t seem to have much to do with Arthas. And today on Tencent I saw a report that the Warcraft movie has entered the script-writing stage. Robert Tapert is a partner of Warcraft movie director Sam Raimi and currently serves as a producer and executive producer on the film. Here is what he said, in his own words: “It’s in development,” Tapert said. “Right now we’re in the outlinestoryscript stage.” The Warcraft movie has drawn attention ever since the filming plan was announced, and Tapert has now confirmed where it stands in development. He declined, however, to comment further on the relationship between the Spider-Man 4 delay and director Sam Raimi. The World of Warcraft film brings together a long list of heavyweights. It is directed by Spider-Man director Sam Raimi (Sam Raimito), and its script is being written by Robert Rodat, the screenwriter who penned Saving Private Ryan, in the hope of delivering richly drawn characters while also letting audiences experience the brutal war behind the game’s story. Live-action actors who have so far expressed interest and may later play characters from the game: Mark Hildebrandt — King Varian, Michele Morrow — Sylvanas Windrunner

title: What you need to know about developing an RTMP server using FluorineFx
content: This article is a document translated specifically for my partner to read; since it might help some folks, I’m also posting it for reference by anyone who needs it. If it doesn’t fit your situation though, I can’t take responsibility. Also, this article was exported directly from Word (page size A3), with way too much redundant code, and I can’t be bothered to clean it up; brothers with a display resolution width below 1280 may see misaligned styling when reading, so please bear with it. Overview:The FluorineFx open source library provides a set of features for the .NET framework, implementing FLEXFLASH remoting, Flex Data Services and real-time messaging. .NET frameworks supported by FluorineFxMicrosoft .NET Framework 1.1 (1.1.4322) Microsoft .NET Framework 2.0 (2.0.50727) Microsoft .NET Framework 3.5 (3.5.21022.8) Mono 1.2.4 (.NET framework support is backward compatible) FeaturesFlex, Flash Remoting (RPC) Flex Messaging (partial) Flex Data Services (partial) Supports AMF0, AMF3 and RTMP protocols (we use this one) Service Browser Template based code generator (ASP.NET like syntax) Easily integrate rich Internet applications with .NET backend Easily integrate with Adobe Integrated Runtime (Adobe AIR™) ASP.NET 2.0 Application Directory LayoutThe physical structure of an ASP.NET 2.0 application is as follows: (Only assembliestypes located under LAC (the bin directory) can be accessed by fluorineFX) Deploying with Visual StudioWe more strongly recommend referring to the FLUORINEFX VISUAL STUDIO 2005 Wizard section to create a solution with fluorineFX enabled. If you’d rather deploy a solution manually, the table below shows the minimum steps: Create your project, or open an existing solution. Use “Add Reference (R)…” to add the assemblies you need.Or, if you plan to debug fluorineFX, add the FluorineFx-2.0.csproj you downloaded earlier to your solution, then use “Add Reference” and pick a project reference. (- - ! This guy’s English isn’t that standard either, he doesn’t like adding punctuation, just like when we chat online, which easily creates ambiguity) Add the following code to your Web.config file, inside the system.web node: ... ... ... Use “Add Web Form” to create an empty file Gateway.aspx. The gateway URL will point to this file. FluorineFx Visual Studio 2005 WizardTo make creating a fluorine-enabled ASP.NET easier, the Fluorine wizard lets you create a custom new project that’s already configured to work with the gateway. (mousebomb: the gateway here is implemented by Gateway.aspx; whether it’s a remoting server side or an RTMP server side, both communicate facing this gateway) There are 2 project templates used to create a complete FluorineFx-enabled solution, and creating a new project using the options given on this page is what we recommend, this way the WebSite project automatically adds a reference to the service library project. The FluorineFx Visual Studio Wizard in Visual Studio 2005In VS, choose File\New\Project… to create an empty project. In VS2005, choose File\Add\New Project… In the Installed Templates panel, select the FluorineFx ServiceLibrary project template The wizard creates the ServiceLibrary (which is just a class library with a reference to the fluorineFx assembly). ServiceLibrary is used for two reasons: your application can run under medium trust (mousebomb: not really sure what exactly this refers to), and it makes architectural separation easier. The workspace should now look like this: Choose File\Add\New Web Site… In the “Installed Templates” selection panel, select the FluorineFx ASP.NET WebSite template At this point, you should see a structure like this in Solution Explorer: On the WebSite property panel page you can manage assembly references (if needed). With that, the solution is created; next comes running and debugging the application. Debugging with VS2005Use the Visual Studio .NET debugger to observe your program and service classes’ behavior at runtime. If this is your first time running the program, set the startup project and start page. Set the startup project Set the start page (this tutorial uses the Console.aspx page generated by the wizard, which redirects to the Service browser page). Later you can change the start page to load your client program. Set breakpoints, start debugging VS launches the default browser and starts your application, loading the start page. Set the parameter values and click the “Call” button. You can open as many browsers as you want; any client call will trigger the breakpoint. VS breakpoint triggered (Mousebomb: this part of the debugging is illustrated using remoting as an example; we’re just using it as a reference, the debugging method is known to everyone on Earth, so I won’t translate the images and text below.) Real-time Messaging ApplicationsEvery Real-time Messaging (RTMP (Real-time Messaging Protocol) is the online streaming communication protocol used by Adobe’s FMS product; a literal translation would be “real-time messaging protocol”. RTM (Real-time Messaging) literally means “real-time messaging”.) application has an Application (Application Adapter) object. The Application object can be used to manage the application’s lifecycle, and to accept or reject client connection attempts. The Application Adapter object is similar to the FCSFMS Application object. Application StructureAn ASP.NET web site can support multiple RTM applications. These applications all live in the “apps” directory under the ASP.NET web site root, and are identified by their directory names.(mousebomb: for example, HelloWorld in the sample is an RTM application ) An ASP.NET web site directory structure: WebSite –apps –SharedBall –VideoChat –VideoRecording An ASP.NET web site directory structure hosted in IIS: Inetpub –wwwroot –WebSite –apps –SharedBall -persistence –VideoChat –VideoRecording -streams In this example there are 3 RTM applications: SharedBall, VideoChat, VideoRecording. To connect to the SharedBall application from the client, you need to use an application name like this: nc new NetConnection(); nc.connect(“rtmp:localhost:1935SharedBall”) Scope ModelIn an RTM application, resources are all managed in a tree. Each node in the tree is called a scope. A scope is a stateful object, shared among the group of clients already connected to the same context path. If the scope is a leaf node, it’s called a BasicScope; if the scope has sub-scopes, it’s called a Scope. There are two predefined BasicScopes: SharedObject Scope and BroadcastStream Scope. Each application has its own scope hierarchy, and the root scope is the WebScope. There’s also a global scope, which is the parent of the WebScope. Each scope has a name. The GlobalScope is named “default”. WebScopes are named after the root level of each application context. Other scopes are named after their respective path names. SharedObject Scopes are named after each SharedObject’s name. BroadcastStream Scopes are named after each stream’s name. The GlobalScope provides cross-application resource and service sharing. Except for GlobalScope and BasicScopes, all scopes can be connected to by clients. A scope object can be created as a result of a client connection request. For example, a client might send a request trying to connect to applicationroom0, when applicationroom0 doesn’t exist yet. After the connection is established, room0 is created. If the url contains many intermediate-level scopes, all of these scopes will be created. For example, if applicationlobby0room0 is requested and neither lobby0 nor room0 exists, then both lobby0 and room0 will be created. A typical scope hierarchy would look like this: GlobalScope(default) – WebScope(application) – Scope(room0) – BroadcastStream(live0), SharedObject(so1) – Scope(room1) – SharedObject(so0) In the previous example, the code nc.connect(“rtmp:localhost:1935application”) will connect the client to the WebScope. Service HierarchyThe IServiceProvider interface defines a mechanism for retrieving service objects. Every scope object is a service provider. Services are managed in a tree (the service hierarchy). A service hierarchy consists of several ServiceContainers. A ServiceContainer is used to store instances of the corresponding class, which provides services for its own type. You can get a service instance by passing a type. A service container is usually bound to a parent. This means that when a service is requested and not found in its container, the container asks its parent, and so on. (Service containers have no concept of children, only parents.) Each scope holds a service container, and this container’s parent is the parent scope’s service container. At the GlobalScope level, you have services like IstreamableFileFactory and IBWControlService.At the WebScope level, you have services like IStreamFilenameGenerator, IsharedObjectSecurityService, and so on. Application AdapterTo write your own application code that works with client connections, handles server-side events, calls client methods, and enforces security, you must implement a custom Application Adapter. The FluorineFx.Messaging.Adapter.ApplicationAdapter class is used as the base class for new Applications. This class provides methods, shared objects and streams for working with client connections. In addition, the Application object has callback functions that can be triggered when the application starts and ends, and also when clients connect and disconnect. An Application Adapter is an application-level scope handler. Application ConfigurationEach RTM application can (optionally) contain a configuration file placed in the application’s root directory. The configuration file is named app.config. A custom Application Adapter class must be registered in the configuration file. Connecting to an RTM ApplicationFlash’s NetConnection class connects the client to the server. var nc:NetConnection new NetConnection(); var uri:String “rtmp:localhost:1935SharedBall”; nc.connect( uri ); The name SharedBall is the sample application’s relative application name under the apps directory. When the application accepts the connection request, the connection becomes available on both the client side (flash.net.NetConnection) and the server side (FluorineFx.Messaging.Api.IConnection). Application EventsApplication eventsA custom Application Adapter can override the following methods to provide access at each step in the RTM application’s lifecycle. Event Description public virtual bool AppStart(IScope application) Called when the application scope starts public virtual bool RoomStart(IScope room) Called when the room scope starts public virtual bool AppConnect(IConnection connection, object[] parameters) Called each time a new client connects. The contents of the parameters parameter are the list of parameters passed after the uri in the NetConnection.connect method. public virtual bool RoomConnect(IConnection connection, object[] parameters) Called each time a new client connects to the application (room). The contents of the parameters parameter are the list of parameters passed after the uri in the NetConnection.connect method. public virtual bool AppJoin(IClient client, IScope application) Called each time a client joins the application scope. This event is called after the connection is established. public virtual bool RoomJoin(IClient client, IScope room) Called each time a client joins the room scope. This event is called after the connection is established. public virtual bool RoomLeave(IClient client, IScope room) Called each time a client leaves the room scope. This event is called before the connection disconnects from the scope. public virtual bool AppLeave(IClient client, IScope application) Called each time a client leaves the application scope. This event is called before the connection disconnects from the scope. public virtual bool RoomDisconnect(IConnection connection) Called each time a client disconnects. public virtual bool AppDisconnect(IConnection connection) Called each time a client disconnects. public virtual bool RoomStop(IScope room) Called when the room scope stops. public virtual bool AppStop(IScope application) Called when the application scope stops. Order of Execution for Connection EventsSuppose a client is connecting to rtmp:serverapproom1room2 First, the connection is established, so the user connects to all the scopes that room2 passes through: app(- AppConnect) room1(- RoomConnect) room2 (- RoomConnect) After the connection is established, the client object is retrieved, and if this is the client’s first connection to this scope, it joins the scope: app(- AppJoin) room1(- RoomJoin) room2(- RoomJoin) If the same client establishes a second connection to the same scope, only the connect methods are called. If it connects to partially the same scopes, only some of the join methods are called; for example, rtmp:serverapproom1room3 will trigger: app(- AppConnect) room1(- RoomConnect) room3(- RoomConnect) room3(- RoomJoin) Client RPC CallsHandling RPC Calls in the Application Adapter All methods added to an Application Adapter subclass can be called from the client via the NetConnection.call method. For example, the following server-side code: public class Application : ApplicationAdapter { public string Echo(string msg) { return “Echo: “ + msg; } } can be triggered by the following as code snippet on the client: nc new NetConnection(); nc.connect(“rtmp:localhostapplication”); nc.onResult function(obj) { trace(“The result is “ + obj); } nc.call(“Echo”, nc, “Hello”); If a method has defined a parameter of type Iconnection as its first implicit parameter, then when the client calls that method, the current connection will be filled in automatically. Calling Client MethodsIf a connection implements the IserviceCapableConnection interface, then it supports calling client methods. To call methods on the client from your application, you’ll first need a reference to the current connection object. To get the active connection, use the FluorineContext.Current.Connection property. Example:IServiceCapableConnection connection FluorineContext.Current.Connection as IServiceCapableConnection; if (connection ! null) { object[] args new object[] { connection.Client.Id }; connection.invoke(“setClientId”, args); } Client code snippet: nc new NetConnection(); nc.client this; nc.connect(“rtmp:localhostapplication”); … function setClientId( id:String ):void { trace(id); } (mousebomb: you don’t need to worry about how exactly the client code is implemented; I guarantee it’s compatible in a way that matches this sample code) If you need to get the result returned by the method, you must provide a class that implements the IPendingServiceCallback interface. In the example below, the Application Adapter implements this interface, and the method call is updated and then passed to the IPendingServiceCallback interface. public class Application : ApplicationAdapter, IPendingServiceCallback { public void ResultReceived(IPendingServiceCall call) { … } private void CallClient() { IServiceCapableConnection connection FluorineContext.Current.Connection as IServiceCapableConnection; if (connection ! null) { object[] args new object[] { connection.Client.Id }; connection.invoke(“setClientId”, args, this); } } } In addition, the following ApplicationAdapter helper methods can be used to call client methods: void InvokeClients(string method, object[] arguments, IPendingServiceCallback callback)void InvokeClients(string method, object[] arguments, IPendingServiceCallback callback, bool ignoreSelf)void InvokeClients(string method, object[] arguments, IPendingServiceCallback callback, bool ignoreSelf, IScope targetScope) The targetScope parameter sets the scope that the client is connected to, on which the call will be made. (mousebomb: we don’t need sections like Shared Objects, ignore them) ExamplesFor RTMP examples see: X:\Program Files\FluorineFx\Samples\Flash\Rtm

title: FansNet! Schedule small-scale beta
content: A: Let me tell you, there’s a website called Fans! B: What Fans? A: Just Fans! Ah! B: Which team’s? A: It’s the fans of all fans! Ah! B: -.-! What’s the URL? A: http://www.qiumi.cc B: .cc is a URL too? A: Yeah, high-tech… Maybe many people feel something special about the World Cup because of that heartbreaking image of a back in a match in 1994; maybe many people stay up all night waiting for the European Cup because of a beer, a melody; maybe many people have fallen deeply in love with the NBA ever since that breathless final shot; do flair, willpower, speed, passion, and fire make you think of La Liga, Bundesliga, Premier League, Serie A, and the NBA? A fan’s love comes from and seeps back into every tournament, every match. As fans, we all surely have games we can never forget. Time goes on, the games go on, our heroes keep fighting—how can we not follow the schedule at all times? Too much clutter gradually keeps us from paying close attention to the matches of our favorite teams and players, and we even miss key games more than once—even though we weren’t really all that busy at the time. How can that not make you sigh? Fans! is not just a website; it’s a way of life! A shared lifestyle and attitude for all fans. Even in the small hours, sitting alone in front of a screen, you’ll still get wildly excited over a goal and secretly feel down after conceding one. And has forgetting match times over and over already left you annoyed? Have you ever wanted to say: I don’t want to miss xx’s matches again! Yeah, we’re fans too, and this is our voice as well. Actually, the schedule is just a tiny, tiny part of a fan’s life—so tiny that countless so-called sports portals, “No. 1 xxx” sites, and “best Chinese xxx” sites all ignore it, throwing together just a few simple tables and never seriously considering this question for fans: What kind of schedule do fans need? Accurate and timely; 2. Intuitive, low-distraction, easy to search and view; 3. Customizable (choose your favorite teams, etc.); 4. View the schedule through multiple channels and methods; 5. Schedule-related data and information; 6. … Yes! There are many more needs. These are the most genuine voices we gathered through an earlier random sample survey of more than 3,000 fans. Fans! truly starts from everyone’s needs, working steadily and quietly from the small things. Whatever fans need, no matter how small, we’ll do it! After just 2 short weeks, the Fans! schedule beta is finally live for small-scale testing. Test URL: http://www.qiumi.cc/match.html

title: Become an Avatar, lose yourself in Pandora
content: Yesterday afternoon I saw the 16:50 showing of Avatar. Although I’d already watched a ton of official videos and clips, I was still deeply blown away. The beauty of Avatar is that it made an internet-addicted otaku freelancer like me suddenly loathe modern technology and Earth, and long endlessly for Pandora. Title When I knew nothing about it, the first time I saw the name Avatar, the word that flashed through my mind was Avanti (haha). The original meaning of Avatar: Sanskrit: अवतार. In Indian philosophy it is most commonly understood as relating to the physical manifestation of gods on earth. In Sanskrit, the word for incarnation carries the sense of “descending” or “reincarnating” from a higher realm through deliberate thought and for a special purpose. After watching the film it suddenly hit me — how apt it was to use avatar as the title! Visual effects On April 26, 2005, on that long-awaited afternoon, I stepped into World of Warcraft. I’ll always remember the emotion of first walking into Darnassus, and I’ll always remember first seeing the majestic, magnificent Stormwind, and the thrill of riding a gryphon and diving past the giant dam the dwarves built. I was completely conquered by these virtual visuals. Several years later, effects as captivating as WoW’s finally showed up on film with even higher image quality — and this film, like World of Warcraft, gathers the strengths of many and carries features far beyond its predecessors. As a milestone in the industry, it will, for years to come, be “forever imitated, never surpassed.” Faced with these impeccable visuals, any verbal description is unnecessary, so I’ll say no more. Director As someone who does programming, I’m quite sensitive to how rigorous a film’s narrative is; the slightest slip makes me think much less of it. Avatar’s plot can’t be called hugely innovative, but the director really knows how to tell a story. Many details make it more coherent and its structure tighter. Not a single line of dialogue from start to finish is wasted. Well-judged shots make the main characters’ personalities full and round. A few of my favorite scenes Scene 1: When a Na’vi hunter kills his prey, before gutting it he says with gratitude, “I hear your pain, thank you, brother,” then quickly finishes the animal off, letting it feel as little pain as possible. Its spirit will return to Eywa; its body will remain and become part of the people. What a beautiful prayer — the karma of taking life is dissolved on the spot. This custom moved me deeply. On Pandora, people and nature are so intimately connected. Scene 2: Earning one’s social standing and the clan’s recognition — at Jake Sully’s coming-of-age ceremony, everyone gathers in a tight circle around Jake, hearts and hands linked with his; seen from above, they form a giant internet. On Pandora, you are so in tune with others. Scene 3: The resurrection ceremony for Dr. Grace and Jake — everyone sits on the ground, hand in hand, chanting together, swaying with the pulse of nature. The scene is so beautiful. The only thing I can think of that rivals it is last year’s Beijing Olympics opening ceremony. The wonder isn’t in the number of people but in the power of harmony it radiates — that pure, holy power that embraces all rivers. When you truly see what the director is conveying, you’re instantly filled with strength and boundless vitality, and all greed, emptiness, slander, jealousy, and pain vanish. Scene 4: The later part where all the Na’vi clans are summoned for battle — Jake asks Tsu’Tey, an Omaticaya warrior who succeeded Eytucan as clan leader after his death, to pass his words on to everyone. He wants the countless clans of all the Na’vi to unite, to fight for their brothers and sisters, to let the humans of Earth know that this is Na’vi territory and they won’t be allowed to do as they please. A thousand riders surge forth, ten thousand horses gallop — magnificent, and deeply satisfying; I’d only ever felt that kind of satisfaction watching The Lord of the Rings trilogy. Although I’d already seen tons of official videos and clips, I was still deeply blown away here. Oh no, oh no — what am I going to do if I never see a film this good again? Reflections Not to mention the many excellent and wondrous natural landscapes — while similar beautiful sights on Earth haven’t yet disappeared, we should cherish resources and eliminate ignorance. As director Lu Chuan said, what we lack isn’t technology, but a pure heart. The planet Pandora is a complete individual. The animals, plants, and people on this planet are all closely bound to nature, tightly interconnected; this inner balance keeps it durable and strong. The planet is like an organism, nurturing the flora and fauna that live on it, and they in turn take part in the planet’s metabolism. They are one whole. Here the rhythms of nature are balanced and harmonious, and pure, holy souls fly free. The spirits of the ancestors, together with the Great Mother, leave no sorrow or pain — only love and eternity. Heaven and earth and all things are one body; you are me and I am you. Humans know they carry many parasites, a great many of which are beneficial to the body, though some people carry harmful ones. Earth is the same: humans are essentially parasites on Earth. Who would allow pests to grow on their own body? Are we beneficial insects or pests to Earth? What gives Earth the right to meekly nourish us? Everything nature grants us is only borrowed; none of it is ours by right. What is given will always be taken back. One day “having” will become “not having.” While we must use Earth’s resources for the sake of social development, we should always remember gratitude. Nothing is something we’re entitled to. The biological neural network setup is just brilliant! Our Earthling technology has developed to the internet information age, yet all we’ve achieved is “fingers flying over keys, sharing this moment; the far ends of the earth as close as neighbors.” Look at their alien planet — nature and people are so in harmony there that without any “high tech” they can still see each other and hear each other across time and space. That kind of communication, free of “modern technology,” is true communication — warm communication — and Earthlings will probably have less and less of it in the future. We love sending greeting texts on holidays, but when we call, text, send QQ messages, or email, what usually gets conveyed is just a cold electronic signal — what else could there be? As Earthlings, what we can do is this: when calling or texting family and friends, smile sincerely — the other person will surely feel it. (The detailed reasons are outside this article’s scope; put simply: 1. these are psychic waves; 2. keeping a smile over the long term will definitely make you more caring toward them.) Though we can’t grow a braid like the Na’vi that lets us communicate heart-to-heart with all things, we mustn’t give up our ability to communicate with the world through the heart. That way, perhaps you’ll discover that on Earth, mountains, water, grass, trees, flowers, birds, and stones all have life. As long as you’re willing to see it, you can communicate with one another. Earlier on, the RDA wanted to bring its culture and science to the locals, hoping to build schools, hospitals, and roads, and then assimilate the Na’vi. It seems the evil RDA also wants to sow the seeds of capitalism and consumerism on other planets. They ruined one Earth and now want to ruin someone else’s planet — how stupid, how shameless! In their dealings with the alien visitors — the Earthlings — the Na’vi also tried to teach them how to “see” the rhythms of nature and the harmony of all things. But the stubborn, ignorant Earthlings have nothing in their heads but annual financial reports, money, and killing. Think carefully: who is more backward and who is more civilized, who is more worth learning from? Compared with Earth, with its highly developed material civilization, Pandora is the paradise in my heart. A decadent civilized world, a noble savage world — if you could choose, which would you pick? I’d choose to be “reincarnated” onto Pandora. Appendix: some background material not covered in detail in the film RDA: full name Resources Development Administration. It is the largest single non-governmental organization of humans in the universe, mainly engaged in mining, transport, pharmaceuticals, weapons, and communications. It has millions of shareholders and is the oldest and largest quasi-administrative entity. The RDA’s rise was like that of “Silicon Valley” in the early 21st century: starting from the two founders borrowing money from their families to start the company, in just a few short decades its status soared, and it proposed building a global rapid transit system. Through this system, large populations could be conveniently transported hundreds or even thousands of miles to wherever work was needed. But this meant the RDA had to keep mining the room-temperature superconductor Unobtanium to complete a global maglev train network. At first the RDA took huge risks exploring Pandora and, despite financial pressure, built the interstellar cargo carrier “Venture Star”. As the RDA obtained exclusive mining rights to Pandora’s precious mineral Unobtanium, along with the potential profits from biofuels and cosmetics and beauty products, the enormous investment had already paid off. Under the permanent authorization of the interstellar industry and commerce administration agreement, the RDA has monopolized the mining, processing, and transport operations of all planets beyond Earth. However, in accordance with the agreement, the RDA is also forbidden from using weapons of mass destruction, and its military strength in space is limited (mousebomb’s note: this explains why humanity’s 22nd-century interstellar demolition crew has no WMDs). But the RDA’s power already far exceeds that of the vast majority of government organizations on Earth. Exopack: The Exopack is equipment humans on Pandora must wear outdoors; it consists of a sealed transparent face mask and a backpack filtering unit. Pandora’s atmosphere is full of ammonia, methane, and chlorine; the human respiratory system can’t adapt to this toxic mixture. Yet with simple filtration, the oxygen in Pandora’s atmosphere can be breathed directly by humans. An Exopack can’t be used continuously for more than two weeks; after rinsing the filter pad with tap water it can be used again. (mousebomb’s note: this isn’t an oxygen mask, just a filter mask. This shows Pandora’s atmosphere has enough oxygen, and also explains why Earth’s missiles and incendiary bombs work normally — otherwise using incendiary bombs would be a glaring flaw.) Pandora: scientific name “Alpha Centauri B-4”, a planet in the Alpha Centauri system, roughly the same size as Earth. The Alpha Centauri system is 4.4 light-years from us, the nearest star system. Seen from space, this beautiful planet looks just like our Earth — colorful and varied. An Earth interstellar survey team discovered this vibrant, still-primitive planet 25 years ago (2129). Pandora’s atmosphere is full of ammonia, methane, and chlorine (mousebomb’s note: not that it lacks oxygen); without other equipment, Earthlings simply couldn’t survive here. But Pandora has developed a unique ecosystem based on a biochemistry completely different from Earth’s, and its strange plants and animals are breathtaking. The Na’vi: The Na’vi are the indigenous humans of Pandora; the word “Na’vi” means “the people” in the Na’vi language. The Na’vi are the only known species beyond Earth with human-like intelligence; they have language and emotions. Although Na’vi society is still at a Neolithic stage equivalent to our primitive society, they have developed a unique culture and a god called “Eywa” based on a mystical spiritual connection with the moon. The Na’vi celebrate the creative power of nature through stories, songs, dance, and crafts. The Hometree: There are hundreds of Na’vi clans on Pandora; the Omaticaya are one of them. They live in a towering ancient tree called the “Hometree” (known in the Na’vi language as Kelutral). The tree is over 150 meters tall and about 30 meters in diameter — two to three times the height of the redwoods that once covered Earth’s Pacific Northwest coast. Its honeycomb-like natural hollows and caves serve as the dwelling places where the Omaticaya live and thrive. At the coming-of-age ceremony for young Omaticaya hunters, they can carve their own bow from the branches of the “Hometree.” Unfortunately, just like the “Hallelujah Mountains,” this place the Na’vi hold sacred and inviolable sits right on top of a rich Unobtnium deposit, and the Omaticaya clan living here thus became a thorn in the RDA’s side. The Avatar Program: Called “Uniltirantokx” by the Na’vi, meaning “Dreamwalker,” it is one of the RDA’s research projects. The Avatar Program first extracts Na’vi DNA, then selects volunteers from among Earthlings, and then, in the RDA’s genetics lab on Earth, cultivates an in-vitro embryo combining Na’vi and human DNA. During the three-year journey to Pandora (equivalent to five years on Earth), the embryo is artificially grown to nearly adult size (this is because Na’vi grow faster). Once the clone has grown into a complete “Na’vi,” the human volunteer can, through a Psionic Link Unit, send his consciousness into it, merging with the clone just as if operating his own body, and transform into an “Avatar” that moves freely on the planet. However, not just anyone can control this cloned Na’vi; only someone whose DNA matches the human DNA in it has that ability. After linking, the host lives inside the “Avatar” and perceives the world through it. Originally, the Avatar Program’s goal was to create miners who could work outside without environmental protection gear. However, the very expensive Psionic Link Unit couldn’t be mass-produced. “Avatars” are mainly used to communicate with the Na’vi and to study the Na’vi and Pandora’s living systems. Polyphemis: Pandora orbits a huge, brilliant planet, named “Polyphemis” by Earthlings after the cyclops of Greek mythology. The Alpha system has three stars — Alpha A, Alpha B, and Alpha C — and Polyphemis orbits Alpha A. This gas giant is about twice the size of Jupiter in our solar system, and just like Jupiter’s “Great Red Spot,” Polyphemis’s giant halo is also lashed by persistent giant storms, so Polyphemis’s very existence is like an angry eye of god watching over Pandora. In addition, besides Pandora, Polyphemis is orbited by 13 moons at varying distances, which is why two to three “moons” can usually be seen in Pandora’s night sky. Under Polyphemis’s glow, unlike the lush daytime scenery that resembles Earth’s, Pandora’s night is bathed in a fascinating blue, which is also why the Na’vi evolved blue skin. Earth at that time: Earth is a planet of the Sun in the Milky Way, our human home. In 2154, Earth faces a global energy crisis and environmental crisis. During this period, through space exploration, we’ve already discovered that Earth isn’t the only planet with life. Through space programs, we’re trying to mine minerals from distant planets to solve Earth’s energy crisis. Hell’s Gate: The official name of Hell’s Gate is “Resources Development Administration Extra-Solar Colony 01 (abbreviated RDA ESC 01).” It is the base for Earthlings’ colonial activities on Pandora; because it sits in a toxic environment surrounded by dangerous creatures, it’s called “Hell’s Gate.” The base covers 9.406 square kilometers, surrounded by a pentagonal wall 2.3382 kilometers on each side. On the wall’s watchtowers are heavy ground-to-ground and ground-to-air weapons for dealing with Pandora’s unfriendly wildlife. In addition, every 250 meters there are small towers to wipe out incursions by smaller creatures. Outside the wall is a 30-meter clearing that machines regularly and automatically clear. The base is heavily guarded, with soldiers on watch 26 hours a day (a day on Pandora), guarding against dangerous creatures that might cross the wall or burrow in. The base has the only spaceport on the planet; runways, landing pads, and support facilities take up a third of the entire base. Another third is garages, armories, and factories producing mining equipment and ammunition; in addition there are barracks, housing for technicians and miners, and an enclosed high-grade staff apartment building. The base is equipped with communal recreational facilities, such as the canteen nicknamed “Hell’s Kitchen,” and there’s also a basketball court between the research labs and the landing pad. Hallelujah Mountains: These boulders floating in the air are called the “Hallelujah Mountains” by Earthlings (also known as MontasVolans) and are one of Pandora’s great spectacles. These boulders contain a precious mineral: Unobtnium. Unobtnium is a rare room-temperature superconductor with a peculiar magnetic field; under the influence of Pandora’s magnetic field, it produces this spectacular scene of floating boulders. The tops of these boulder islands are relatively flat while their sides are extremely steep; rivers pour down the cliffs to form waterfalls hanging in midair. They float in the magnetic field like icebergs drifting in the ocean, and they even collide with each other. Pandora’s indigenous “Na’vi” call these island clusters the “Thundering Rocks” and regard them as inviolable sacred ground. Yet Earthlings came to Pandora precisely to mine the Unobtnium in these boulders and solve Earth’s energy crisis. [2010.1.12] With Mr. Wu’s strong support, at 1 a.m. on Monday the 11th, I watched the IMAX 3D version at Dongguan Wanda. I sat in row 10, seat 37, slightly left of center, 6 channels, the effect was decent. The one flaw was that the subtitles weren’t fully displayed: subtitle alpha .4, width 90%, and most frustratingly the subtitles were overflow”hidden”, and on top of that they were pure white with no inverse-color shadow — meaning that in white scenes you simply couldn’t see the subtitles at all.

title: Pure AS3 calendar control for Flash
content: Recently I was working on Flash and needed a calendar control, but Flash’s built-in component library doesn’t include a DateChooser for AS3, and searching around turned up nothing ready-made either, so I wrote one myself for AS3. (The rendered UI is based on com.thomas.DatePicker.DatePicker.) Sharing it with anyone else who needs one for Flash development. Usage: package { import org.mousebomb.utils.DateAndTime; import flash.events.Event; import org.mousebomb.ui.DatePicker; import flash.display.Sprite; ** * @author Mousebomb * @date 2009-7-21 * public class TestMain extends Sprite { public var s : Sprite; public var dp : DatePicker; public function TestMain() : void { dp new DatePicker(); dp.x 10; dp.y 10; dp.firstDayOfWeek 1; dp.disabledDays [6,0]; dp.showToday true; dp.selectableRangeStart new Date(2009,11,22); dp.selectableRangeEnd new Date(2012,11,22); dp.selectDate new Date(2012,11,22); addChild(dp); dp.addEventListener(Event.SELECT, onSelect); dp.addEventListener(Event.SCROLL, onScroll); } private function onScroll(event : Event) : void { trace(“scroll”); } private function onSelect(event : Event) : void { trace(DateAndTime.formatDate(“%Y-%m-%d”,dp.selectDate)); dp.hide(); } } } This example demonstrates the following behavior: Default style, default font Week starts on Monday Saturday and Sunday are not selectable Today is marked Selectable range set to 2009.12.22~2012.12.22 Download the org.mousebomb.ui.DatePicker class

title: China Network Television CNTV makes its debut
content: China Network Television (CNTV) made its debut today — go download CBOX and start watching free, fully licensed official TV. CBOX client download link: http://cbox.cntv.cn/ CBox is the most authoritative video client for watching CCTV and dozens of local TV stations from across the country over the internet. Its programming comes from China Network Television, the country’s largest online TV network — a massive library to browse at will, with both live streams and on-demand viewing. The homepage shows that China Network Television is divided into five channels: News, Sports, Entertainment, iBugou, and iXiyou. Starting in 2010, CNTV will also roll out a series of content services covering movies, TV dramas, documentaries, finance, discovery, health, weather, home, travel, education, ethnic affairs, music and more. CNTV says that on the video resources front, it will dig deep into CCTV’s 450,000 hours of historical footage and pull together the 1,000-plus hours of video that TV organizations nationwide broadcast every day; at the same time, it will preserve China’s history and culture in every field in video and digital form, build the country’s largest and most influential multimedia database with online video at its core, and turn CNTV into China’s largest legitimate online video distributor. On distribution formats and geography, CNTV says it will bring together web TV, IPTV, mobile TV, mobile media and other media terminals (buses, trains, airlines, subways, buildings, large plaza screens, etc.), build multilingual channels, and deploy global mirror sites to reach internet users in nearly 100 countries and regions across North America, Europe, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Africa and beyond — forming a globalized, multilingual, multi-terminal program distribution system. According to a relevant person in charge of CNTV’s preparatory office, CNTV is positioned as an approved national comprehensive online video public platform: a globalized, multilingual, multi-terminal, multi-dimensional distribution platform centered on audiovisual interaction and blending the characteristics of the internet with those of television. Earlier reports said CCTV wanted to strengthen its market-oriented operations by bringing in private capital, with the goal of “building an online TV network that fully reflects China’s national level and carries significant international influence, and fulfilling the media responsibility and platform value of ‘delivering the best content to the most users’.” I’m using the CBOX client right now to watch CCTV. The one thing that bugs me is that it doesn’t support full-screen playback on a secondary monitor; everything else is pretty good.

title: Avatar will be released on January 2 next year.
content: This year there are two big movies: one is 2012, the other is Avatar. 2012 has already sounded a warning bell for everyone on Earth, and the film I’m most looking forward to next is Avatar — a movie that will get people thinking, too. Avatar, that super 3D blockbuster, opens worldwide in both 2D and 3D on the 18th of this month, and mainland China has tentatively set its release for January 2nd next year. Plot: In the future, humanity launches the Avatar Program to get at the resources of another planet — Pandora — and, by mixing human DNA with that of the Na’vi (Pandora’s indigenous people), grows nearly 3-meter-tall “Avatars” so they can survive on Pandora and mine its minerals. Jake, a wounded ex-soldier, agrees to take part in the experiment and arrives on the paradise-like Pandora in his Avatar body. Yet in this gorgeous, secluded world, every creature that crawls on the ground, flies through the sky, or burrows in the earth is huge and deadly… Carrying a heavy mission and in constant danger, Jake, after an accidental first contact with the Na’vi, opens up the possibility of communication — but also stands on the brink of an unexpected, vast and spectacular conflict of the century, from which he will gain an unprecedented revelation… Chinese official site: http://avatar.mtime.com/ Official site: http://www.avatarmovie.com/ Like 2012, this movie is a must-see. Since it’s a blockbuster ten years in the making, of course I can’t miss it. After watching a few video previews, the visuals really are beyond reproach, and I hope the story holds up from beginning to end. Avatar will become for film what World of Warcraft is for games — a milestone of enormous breakthrough. It will raise audiences’ standards by several notches all at once, and for a long time afterward it will be imitated but rarely surpassed. [09.12.24] These past few days I’ve seen a flood of positive reviews, which keeps my anticipation building. Mixed into that ocean of comments are some negative ones too; some say the plot is too clichéd and has no substance (that it can’t compare with District 9). Actually, I think it has different selling points from District 9. This film has two big draws: flawless visual effects, and world-building that breaks with tradition. The visual effects are there for all to see and beyond doubt. After watching the official “Avatar Desktop App” and the 720p trailer, I’ve already gotten a feel for the outstanding quality. This film’s visual effects will be a milestone in the history of cinema. Beyond the flawless, state-of-the-art visuals, what draws me most to Avatar is its constructed world. The constructed worlds everyone knows — The Lord of the Rings, World of Warcraft, the several DD-based novels, Jiuzhou — the first three all draw on European history, medieval fantasy, and Norse mythology, reworked to a considerable degree, while Jiuzhou draws on ancient Chinese myth and legend, shot through with Eastern culture. All of them have created worlds that set the imagination racing. Avatar, by contrast, innovates on a much larger scale: with the planet Pandora as its grand framework, it uses the screen to show magnificent vistas and all kinds of strange plants and beasts (the first time I saw the world of Pandora, the first thing that flashed through my mind was the planet in Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War II). Going forward, adding more content on top of a base setting with enormous potential will be no poorer than the worlds created by those who came before. After all, I haven’t seen the movie yet, so it’s hard to speculate about much of it. bomb out.

title: Two little games I wrote last month
content: A puzzle game made by Tomorrow Angel Studio together with Little Sky for Ciwong Technology (www.ciwong.com). title: Eaze, the newest member of the easing family
content: Spotted this article translated by auzn over on Tiandihui — Eaze, the newest member of the easing family. Reportedly more efficient than TweenLite and packed with features. Bookmarked. Eaze was designed to: Make tweening in Flash lightweight, eye-catching, and easy to use, Introduce the smartest syntax and event system, Deliver the best performance balance, Use as few classes as possible, with no dependencies. The result is a maximally optimized, compact little library (~4Kb for the raw engine + ~9Kb with all plugins included) with jQuery-like syntax. Current status: tested and stable; the API may change slightly. Eaze on Googlecode:http://code.google.com/p/eaze-tween/ Download:http://code.google.com/p/eaze-tween/downloads/list Author’s blog:http://philippe.elsass.me/2009/11/as3-eaze-tween-library-update/

title: Loader's resources are not released
content: Yesterday I ran into a memory leak. After digging all the way down, I found it was caused by the bitmap captured for the reflection in an external .swf that had been loaded not being cleared. My guess is that although loader.unloadAndStop() closes the stream, it doesn’t release the BitmapData created inside the loaded program. Keep this in mind: aside from purely media-playback objects, if the external program you load has listeners, callbacks, or has created BitmapData, then that external program needs to clean up after itself before it’s unloaded. Otherwise, no matter how much you gc, it’ll still be eating memory. Solution:In this kind of situation, I usually have the loaded flash program implement a dispose method, and the loader that loads it calls dispose(); inside a try before unloadAndStop();. The external program cleans up after itself inside the provided dispose method. The cleanup steps differ from case to case — you have to take out your own self in a targeted way, based on everything you did while you were alive. Broadly speaking, this includes: cutting off your related callbacks and listeners, and freeing memory (closing sounds, clearing video, closing network connections, clearing bitmap data). Like this, in the main file: private function closeExFlash() : void { try { (exFlashLoader.content as IDispose).dispose(); }catch(e : *) { } try { exFlashLoader.unloadAndStop(); }catch(e : *) { } this.visible false; } There’s another approach: the loaded Flash maintains itself. This only works when the document class is placed directly onto the stage — I don’t often do this (in many cases I use the swf as a runtime sharelib, and I load it just to use some of its classes) — The loaded Flash listens for the remove\_from\_stage event itself, and when that event fires, it frees its own memory: cutting off its related callbacks and listeners as described above, and freeing memory (closing sounds, clearing video, closing network connections, clearing bitmap data). At the same time, make sure the main program holds no references to it.

title: Adoogen — Recording your and my gaming life
content: This morning, by sheer chance, a portal dropped me into “Adoogen - Connecting Game Lovers Everywhere“. A few minutes of scanning the whole site told me what I needed to know — this is exactly the kind of game community site I’d been hoping for. I’ve never had any love for BBS or grab-bag community sites, and I’ve been a Douban user since 2007. And over time, Douban has only gotten better at holding onto me — because the thing in this world that best understands my appetite for what to listen to, read, and watch isn’t a person. It’s Douban. The story of Douban’s beginnings Do you often find yourself staring blankly at the endless wall of covers in a bookstore? Or staggering out of a music shop, dizzy from the sheer variety? Now that broadband downloads and online shopping have arrived, even in the smallest town your options grow by hundreds and thousands every day. Surely some of them are things you’d love — but odds are you’ll pass most of them by without ever noticing. The media floods us with blockbusters meant for everyone, yet has little to offer the things meant for just a few. And one man’s meat is another man’s poison: no matter how fair and diligent the TV entertainment editors and newspaper book critics may be, their recommendations can’t possibly work equally well for everyone. The people who started Douban realized that for most people, the most effective help in choosing comes from friends, relatives, and colleagues. A casual recommendation or two doesn’t just convey their own genuine feelings — it also carries a judgment about your taste and the filtering that goes with it. They won’t recommend a baby-care bible to a bachelor, and they won’t bring Naked Killer home to Mom. Unfortunately, all your friends and family put together have still only heard and seen so much. And the people whose tastes most resemble yours are often total strangers. If you could know the tastes of tens of thousands of people without having to meet them one by one, and quickly pick out the ones who are most kindred spirits, the magic of word of mouth would be magnified a hundredfold — and everyone involved would get at least some benefit from it. Douban was born out of that wish. Douban isn’t aimed at any particular group; it tries to hold every flavor. Tall or short, fat or thin, highbrow or lowbrow, Douban helps you find kindred spirits through the things you love, and then, through them, find even more good things. The pity is that while Douban lets you share, discuss, and keep track of TV shows, movies, books, music, and blogs, it has never offered any way to talk about games. Through my Douban profile, my friends can find out what movies I like to watch, what music I like to listen to, and what books I like to read — but it’s hard for them to learn what games I like to play. In this age of ever-advancing information technology, there are more and more “homebodies,” and ACG is one big family. I can log the anime and manga I watch through Douban, but after I play a game, nobody knows about it. What a tragedy. Douban users have created plenty of game-related groups, and quite a few people even add games to Douban as movies so they can collect and share them. The classic example is World of Warcraft, whose Cast list boldly reads “You”! I really wished Douban would offer a dedicated games section, and I’m sure plenty of other people want the same thing. Earlier, when “My Bookshelf” showed up among Hainei’s “apps” and “Movies” appeared among Xiaonei’s “apps”, I wrote to them and asked for a “My Games” feature, suggesting they open up game-related discussion — but my little wish never came true. Maybe the core users of both sites just don’t care about that feature? Or maybe it was just a naive, silly idea on my part? Either way, at the time I was ready to build it myself, but I never found the right collaborator, and there was no investment behind it. Day after day, the naive idea turned into a story; month after month, the silly story turned into a beautiful dream sealed away in my memory. But today, the dream came true. This morning, by sheer chance, a portal dropped me into “Adoogen - Connecting Game Lovers Everywhere“. A few minutes of scanning the whole site told me — this is exactly the game community site I’d been hoping for. It has every core feature I wanted. It was love at first sight, and I only wish I’d found it sooner. Adoogen is a home built specifically for video game fans, and serving the millions of gamers just like me is its lifelong mission. On Adoogen you can: Log your gaming journey Find gaming buddies who share your interests Trade experiences and takeaways from the games you play Share the joy that games bring you Friends who play games, come on over — I’m waiting for you here: http://www.adoogen.com/gamer/mousebomb/

title: Luck plummets, laptop goes on strike
content: The day before yesterday I installed win7 on the N80vn. The machine got restored N times, then I formatted the recovery partition too, and after it finally installed, the problems never stopped. Yesterday: N blue screens plus N crashes, and my RP (luck) hit rock bottom. Today it crashed once, and after a reboot it wouldn’t start at all — the hardware self-test failed. Frozen forever at checking nvram… The one bit of luck in all this misfortune: before reinstalling I’d backed up the few projects I had on hand to the desktop, so I switched over to the desktop for the time being — at least its win7 is perfectly stable. I heard about Allods, which is all the rage lately. They say it’s the next WoW, so I’ve got to play it when I have time. But the laptop has to go in for repairs first… News from November 2009: Nival, the veteran Russian studio with 12 years of game development experience behind Heroes of Might and Magic V, has recently started recruiting closed beta testers for its newly developed cartoon-style MMORPG Allods Online (tentative Chinese title), which draws on Rage of Mages (aka Allods), a hugely popular RPG it released in 1998. The closed beta will kick off over the next few weeks. [11.23 13:45] Around noon, an engineer came over from the Shenzhou Dongli Digital service station to take a look, and my laptop was diagnosed as needing treatment at a bigger hospital. The suspicion is that it’s an aftereffect of my formatting the hidden Recovery partition. Right now it can only boot into winpe, it can’t install any OS, and the hard drive shows as unavailable. I’m using a pitiful 1GB USB stick to back up data to the desktop.

title: Obama Answers Questions on Internet Openness During His Shanghai Trip
content: U.S. President Barack Obama delivered a speech at the Shanghai Science and Technology Museum on the 16th. In answering a question about Internet openness, Obama said that the freer the flow of information, the stronger society becomes, because that way citizens around the world can hold their governments accountable. [Obama] Well, I’d now like to call on my ambassador, Huntsman. A netizen has submitted a question through our embassy website. [Jon Huntsman] First, in a country with so many Internet users, with 60 million bloggers, do you know about the firewall? Second, should we be free to use TWITTER? [Obama] First, let me say that I have never used TWITTER. I notice that some young people are always busy with all kinds of electronic devices—very bulky. But I still very much believe in the role of technology and attach great importance to openness. When it comes to the flow of information, I believe the freer the flow of information, the stronger society becomes, because that way citizens around the world can hold their governments accountable, there is accountability, they think for themselves, and that produces new ideas and encourages creativity. So I have always been a firm supporter of open use of the Internet. I strongly support not censoring content. I have talked about this before in the United States; it is one of our traditions. I also recognize that different countries have different traditions, but I can tell you that in the United States, we have unrestricted access to the Internet. This is a source of our strength, and it should be encouraged. But I should also be very honest with you: as President of the United States, sometimes I still wish information did not flow so freely, because then I wouldn’t have to hear people criticizing me. I think that is very natural. When someone is in a position of power, they think, Why are you saying this about me? It is very irresponsible of you to say that. But the reality is this: because information is free in the United States, because many people in the United States criticize me for all sorts of things, I still believe that this is what makes our nation’s system stronger and makes me a better leader, because it forces me to hear opinions I do not want to hear, and it forces me to examine what I am doing, every day, to see whether I am truly doing the best I can for the American people. So I believe the Internet has now become an even more powerful tool that allows citizens to participate. In fact, one of the reasons I won this election and became president is that we were able to mobilize many young people through the Internet. At the beginning, no one thought I would win, because we did not have the wealthiest supporters or the most politically powerful people supporting us. But people saw our campaign through the Internet, they got excited, and they organized campaign activities, events, and rallies. The result was a bottom-up movement that made us very successful. This is true not only in government and politics, but in the business world as well. Take a company like Google: less than 20 years ago, it was just two people about your age starting a company. It began as a scientific experiment, and then, because of the Internet, they were able to create an industry—one that revolutionized business all over the world. So if it weren’t for the very free openness—like the openness the Internet provides—Google would not exist. That is why I strongly support the approach of not restricting Internet use, access, or information technologies like TWITTER. The more open it is, the more it enables communication and connects the whole world. Take my two daughters, Malia and Natasha—one is 11 and the other is 8. They can get online in their rooms, and through the Internet they can reach anywhere in the world and learn whatever they want. This is a tremendous power for them; their having this power also helps promote mutual understanding. As I said just now, technology also has a downside: terrorists can use the Internet to do things they could not do before, and some extremists can also mobilize. Of course, openness definitely comes at a certain cost; that cannot be denied. But I think the good far outweighs the bad, so it is still better to remain open. I am very glad that the Internet is also part of this forum. Two final questions.

title: The wait for StarCraft 2's release is finally paying off
content: This afternoon halley summoned me over for a few rounds of Red Alert 3, and my craving for StarCraft 2 shot straight through the roof… Finally there’s some solid word: Q2 next year. Well, sooner than I can mentally handle, hehe. Blizzard’s RTS blockbuster Starcraft II was confirmed earlier today for a Q2 2010 release, though the exact day within Q2 is still unannounced. According to foreign media reports, Blizzard’s RTS blockbuster Starcraft II was confirmed earlier today for a Q2 2010 release, though the exact day within Q2 is still unannounced. The game will be split into three separate titles, each focusing on a single race. Terran, Zerg, and Protoss will appear in turn, with the Terran leading as the base game, while the Zerg and Protoss arrive later as standalone expansions — though content-wise all three are similar, each with 26-30 missions. Each part’s ending is fixed, but the specific progression depends on the player’s choices, and different playstyles lead to very different storylines.

title: Torchlight download
content: During the long wait for Diablo 3, we’re no longer lonely — because now we have Torchlight. Here’s some info (download links at the bottom): Chinese Name: Torchlight English Name: Torchlight Genre: ARPG, action role-playing game Release Date: 2009 DeveloperPublisher: Runic Games, Perfect World Entertainment Language: English Overview: Runic Games (a new company founded by Max Schaefer, one of the original founders of Blizzard North) has unveiled a new trailer for its ARPG Torchlight, and it looks like a lower-fidelity version of Diablo 3. The single-player version goes on sale October 27, priced at US$19.99 for the digital download. The online version isn’t expected to hit the market until 18 months after the single-player release. Earlier reports also said the global publishing rights for the game went to China’s Perfect World. AdventureAction RPG Torchlight is an action RPG built around adventure. In the game, adventurers set out from the town of Torchlight and head into the nearby mountains in search of a magical ore that can power their weapons — but also endangers their lives. With a simple, direct interface, the game aims to deliver fast, explosive action and a gorgeous, gripping world. A Quick Look at the Three Classes There are three classes to choose from. The Destroyer excels at melee combat, and his brutal methods make short work of many enemies; the Alchemist can summon minions to help him and kill enemies from a distance; the Vanquisher is an excellent shooter who can use traps to confuse and distract her enemies. Seven Game Features Randomization: The game world is randomly generated, so every adventure is unique — each time you set out on a journey you’ll run into different monsters, treasures, puzzles, and items. Approachable interface: Torchlight was designed from the start to be simple and easy to pick up, and the intuitive interface lets players explore this colorful world with ease. Retirement system: Once a character reaches a certain level, they can “retire,” and retiring grants specific perks and bonuses to a new character. Pets: Players can choose a pet to keep them company, and the pet levels up along with the player… it can help you in combat, carry items for you, and perform plenty of other useful services. Character creation: Players can create a personalized character and choose a pet companion. Through different face shapes and hairstyles, every player can customize a character that is uniquely their own. Fishing: When you’re tired of fighting monsters, you can head to a fishing hole to relax and show off your skills, seeing what you can reel in. Fishing is fun and can earn you and your pet some benefits — plus some other rewards, of course. Editor: Runic Games will provide an editor for all players to use, letting them create, design, and share their own content. Download Links: Original download page for the hard-disk version: http://www.verycd.com/topics/2777404/ Direct download link for the hard-disk version: [火炬之光].Torchlight.full.rip.rar Note: This is a hard-disk version, and it’s in English. If you don’t want to buy a legit copy but still want a full install, you’d better wait a while. Perfect World will put out the online version before long. Perfect World really is something — its worldwide partnerships keep getting stronger and stronger. [18:13 update] Adding an address for the disc image: Torchlight [Disc Image] Original download page: http://www.verycd.com/topics/2777397/ Direct download: [火炬之光].sr-torchl.bin [火炬之光].sr-torchl.cue [10.30 update] I played it a bit yesterday. The installer is only about one CD in size. I haven’t seen any cutscenes yet. The 3D engine is like Titan Quest’s, and the overall visuals and combat controls are like Diablo 3’s. The pet system is something I found genuinely novel and unexpectedly fun. You can keep a cat or a dog, and it has its own separate inventory and equipment slots. It can carry items for you, wear equipment, learn skills, and even run back to town in the field to sell things — then come back happily a few dozen seconds later and hand you the money! I still haven’t figured out how to fish. Maybe my pet is already hungry… [10.31 update] Last night I played until late and got down to dungeon level 19. Turns out this game’s territory just keeps extending downward. I figured out how to fish. There’s a fishing spot in the lower-right corner of the town of Torchlight, and other maps have fishing spots too. Click the mouse to start fishing, and just reel in at the right moment. The fish you catch can transform your pet, and different fish do different things. Besides class skills, you can buy scrolls in the game to learn spells. Your main character can learn 4 and your pet can learn 2, and you can forget them at any time to relearn. Sadly, on my first playthrough I bought a few of the most expensive ones — Ice Blast, Charm, Identify, and a lifesteal one… So far Identify is the only one I use smoothly. I’m an Alchemist, and I usually put 4 points into Magic and 1 into Defense when I level up, so my spell damage is already strong; these skills feel pretty useless to me. Ice Blast at level 1 has low damage and a long CD. Charm has a chance to make enemies switch sides for a few seconds, which badly slows down how fast I gain XP. Lifesteal doesn’t seem to do anything, so I can’t be bothered to use it — later I swapped it for Group Heal II. I kind of regret picking “Easy” difficulty — it’s a bit too easy. The few minions the Alchemist summons are really efficient at killing bosses! Back in Diablo 2, when my Necromancer’s skeleton army ran into a boss, it was as if the joints between the bones were held together with paste — so flimsy… This game’s music follows the Diablo style, and there are even a lot of familiar sound effects. The spells and controls borrow from Diablo 3, and a few of the Alchemist’s skills already give me a whiff of Diablo 3. That said, there are plenty of detail-level problems that still need fixing — Runic Games was too rushed during the final 10% polish phase, which makes me feel they haven’t quite matched Blizzard. 11.3 update Rumor: Torchlight forced Diablo 3 back into development (source) Word in the industry right now is that Torchlight’s release forced Diablo 3 back into development, and Blizzard has stopped announcing new Diablo 3 news. This is exactly the outcome we predicted long ago: a game that lets players experience most of Diablo 3’s ideas ahead of time will, from any angle, deal a huge blow to Diablo 3’s popularity and massively erode expectations for it. Blizzard has now stopped putting out any Diablo 3 news, and it looks like Blizzard’s determination to completely overhaul the game’s systems may take some of the edge off the awkwardness it feels about Torchlight. I remember how the open release of Nox in 2000 dealt a massive blow to Diablo 2 — merely a partial overlap in elements made a sensitive Blizzard send Diablo 2 back for a full year of rework. This time, Torchlight’s near-total imitation has convinced Blizzard to go for a complete rework. Looks like we players will have to wait until at least 2014, when plenty of players will be married with kids, before we get a chance to play Diablo 3.

content: A few days ago I watched the movie 9 — mediocre plot, but grand visuals — and the images of those future robots are still vivid in my mind. Yesterday, the big Flash game Machinarium entered my gaming journey. I spotted this game on auzn’s blog, and judging by the screenshots it looked well worth playing. And today halley recommended it to me too, which made me even more curious. I got the torrent from auzn, so here’s a BT torrent portal — anyone passing by who wants to play, let’s download it together: http://bt.ktxp.com/html/2009/1017/141714.html It’s already up on verycd too, along with a Chinese localization patch (3DM’s): Download page: http://www.verycd.com/topics/2775000/ The game is all about action puzzles, so language doesn’t matter. There is a Chinese patch, but I wouldn’t recommend using it. Here’s some useful info — you can treat it as a Machinarium walkthrough: If you’re at a loss, check the exclamation mark hint in the top-right corner. If you’ve read the hint and still have no idea, play the little plane-shooting game in the top-right corner (updown keys to move + space to fire, it’s simple), and it will open the walkthrough for the corresponding level. If your level of intelligence is so unique that you need to play that plane game over and over just to see the walkthrough, and you find that too tedious, then you can dig out all the game’s walkthroughs: in the \10\ folder under the installation directory (for example F:\Program Files\Machinarium\10), apart from the two files 11111111.101 and 11111111.111, just change the extension of every other file to .swf and you can open them with Flashplayer — each one is the walkthrough for a level. Have fun playing, and beat the game soon! ps: this game reminds me of a little Flash game I once played — 小黑轮的机器城.

title: Moved by *The Triplets of Belleville*
content: 疯狂约会美丽都 Les triplettes de Belleville, also known as The Triplets of Belleville. Watched it today. The first 5 minutes made me decide this was a unique and great piece of animation. So I paused it, hurriedly ate my meal, very reverently closed all my other programs, and gave Les triplettes de Belleville my undivided attention. For an animated film running a bit over 80 minutes, the plot unfolded quite differently from what I’d expected after those first 5 minutes. I’d assumed it was the moving story of a tough, capable grandmother raising a world-class athlete, but it turned out to be nothing of the sort (thankfully — if it had gone the way I imagined, it would have been a cliché). Later on, the grandson not only fails to achieve any great success, he gets abducted by gangsters, which left me feeling a bit regretful. Still, the grandmother’s cleverness, her being impervious to both blade and bullet, and her showing off her skills really left me gaping. Although there’s hardly a line of dialogue from beginning to end, the visuals already tell the story smoothly and completely, and the characters are drawn well enough. The power of the imagery is flawless. The innuendo and black humor reflect the dark corners behind the glitz and glamour of the beautiful city. The warm color palette and exaggerated visuals fill that gray city with comedic color once more. The ending is very subtle. I caught a glimpse of the photo on the wall, heard the final line of dialogue come out of the grandson’s mouth, and the tears just came pouring down. The original question is still there, still as kind and gentle as ever, but once the answer is spoken aloud, the listener who loved him most departed long ago. Springs go, autumns come; things are the same, but the people are not. The rivers and mountains remain as they were; how many times has the setting sun glowed red? This film is from 2003, and it has a very high rating on Douban — it really is well worth watching. I don’t have enough command of language to write a proper review of it; I’m just jotting this down: today, this animated film moved me.
