title: Fight — fight out a big watermelon; drag — drag out a big masterpiece
content: Ten years to sharpen a single sword — guarantee the quality, not the quantity. After watching Jiaokeli’s See Through, I fell unusually in love with it. (download page portal) One person spent three and a half years pouring himself into creating a personal short film, giving up a stable job and material comfort, all for a little over 16 minutes of animation. What conviction sustained him through it? How could it not be a masterpiece? A masterpiece is the daughter of time, not the son of money. Look around: animation and comics everywhere, games everywhere. They swamp our entertainment lives like a flood of wild beasts. Abundance is no blessing — it’s a curse. More and more shoddy products roll off the line as countless companies chase volume over quality, with their eyes fixed on money and their shining ideals cast to the four winds. For an otaku, ACG is a holy trinity — seeing (A)nimation naturally leads to thinking of (G)ame, so my mind wanders again — Blizzard’s success has taught us all a lesson. In nearly twenty years, Blizzard has conquered countless gamers with just seven games across three series. If I remember correctly, the grandfather of PC RTS games is Dune. Back in the day, Westwood was still a towering tree, its position at high noon. Every RTS player in the world had Dune II on their hard drive. Yet with such a formidable rival before it, Blizzard still set out on the path of RTS — and as events proved, Blizzard came from behind to take the lead. While developing Warcraft: Orcs Humans, they had already studied every strength of Dune II in detail and grasped all of its weaknesses. Blizzard’s goal was to perfect, perfect, and perfect again the very concept of RTS. It was exactly this passion that forged Blizzard’s early legend. In 1994, Warcraft: Orcs Humans broke into the RTS market. It was Blizzard’s first game made exclusively for PC, and the first time the Blizzard label appeared on a game box. The product was an instant hit. At its core it imitated the Dune formula, which made it easy for Dune players to pick up. Though it was an imitation, Blizzard still stamped Warcraft with its own mark. In terms of setting, it was the first to blend in a fantasy backdrop: swords and magic replaced planes and cannons, and the all-encompassing yellow sand gave way to lush forests, giving players a completely fresh combat experience. In terms of features — networked multiplayer, a random map generator, a wealth of hotkey settings — every one of these new experiences Warcraft brought to players pointed the way toward the future of game development. Afterward, Blizzard released sequels in the Warcraft series, the Diablo series, and StarCraft. Every product was a spectacular success. I once didn’t understand why one of the first subtitles in the World of Warcraft opening cinematic was “ten years.” Perhaps more than a decade ago (2004 for World of Warcraft, ‘94 for Warcraft — ten years) today’s Blizzard glory was already destined. The Warcraft series now holds kingly status; even when such well-known settings as The Lord of the Rings and Dungeons Dragons were turned into online games, they still couldn’t shake World of Warcraft‘s position. By the same token, as the world’s largest game company, EA Games’ titles just aren’t very replayable. Among strategy games, only the Tiberium Wars series still has a decent story left. As Jay (Chou) says: “Games come too fast, just like a tornado — can’t escape the storm circle, no time to flee. Games leave too fast, just like a tornado…” Near-assembly-line production makes games come fast and go fast. Too commercial. It lacks love. Why is Blizzard able to create such a legend? As Stephen (Chow) says: “As long as you put your heart into it, anyone can be the God of Cookery.“ The way I see it, the people at Blizzard all have boundless passion for their products, a ten-years-to-sharpen-one-sword attitude, and the mental readiness to scrap everything and start over whenever necessary (of course, they also have more material security than we do, so they won’t be blinded by profit and rush things through). More than nine months pregnant, Annie Strain grabbed the phone and dialed her husband’s number. “She told me the time had come,” recalls Blizzard employee Jeff Strain. It was the fall of 1997, and he was still at Blizzard Entertainment making a final sprint to finish developing StarCraft in time for the Christmas release window. “I went to the IT department, signed out a laptop, and then sped home,” admits Jeff Strain, who by then was already exhausted. “You know what? Five or six hours before the baby was born, I was still in the hospital writing code.” When Annie woke up, she found her husband still clacking at the keyboard. She was instantly furious: “You’re still working on that damn game while our daughter is being born?” Jeff Strain’s fingers stopped at once. He looked up and said, “It’s not a ‘damn game,’ Annie — this is StarCraft!” Three years later, Jeff Strain admits he’s still ashamed of what he said that day. But stories like his are commonplace at Blizzard Entertainment. The obsession Blizzard employees have for game development is often hard for friends and family to understand. For Blizzard employees, game development isn’t a job — it’s a way of life. This may make their family lives a bit rough, but for Blizzard Entertainment, whose principle is to “produce only top-tier, best-selling games,” a great deal of sacrifice and boundless passion are indispensable. Blizzard understands the difference between good and great, and that is precisely the hardest thing for a company to do: be willing to scrap everything and start over at any moment. If someone born in the ‘80s never played StarCraft, you can only say their childhood was incomplete — or that they were a computer-game illiterate. Perhaps not everyone knows that StarCraft was once sent back to the drawing board right before release. StarCraft remains to this day Blizzard’s “longest and most painful one,” yet Blizzard’s resolve to make a great game never changed. The earlier StarCraft ultimately kept only the race settings; all the rest of its design was thrown out. Because of the redo, the schedule slipped, and by the time Christmas came, StarCraft still wasn’t ready for release — just like how we’re now waiting for the repeatedly delayed StarCraft 2. StarCraft‘s lead designer Bob Fitch said: “Everyone at the company knows that just a few disappointing games would destroy all our reputation.“ As events proved, it was precisely this spirit of relentless refinement and this ten-years-to-sharpen-one-sword attitude that earned Blizzard the admiration of players. Blizzard once laid down a strict hiring policy: anyone who works at Blizzard must be a gamer. Make yourself both a user and a maker. As a user, you can understand the needs and judge the product; as a maker, you can find a way to meet those needs and make it happen. As our great “Three Represents” thought says: “Represent the fundamental interests of the broadest masses of players.” When leaders go among the masses and developers go among users, how could the work possibly be done poorly? A voice from the heavens: “So you watched Jiaokeli’s See Through — is that any reason to blow hot air and inflate a great big balloon?” Sorry, I’ve strayed off course, nearly fallen into a ditch. Enough said — hats off to Blizzard, hats off to Jiaokeli. StarCraft 2 and Diablo 3 keep getting delayed, dragged out again and again. Drag it out, drag it out into a masterpiece.

title: Microsoft's free antivirus, Microsoft Security Essentials (MSE)
content: My Norton is about to expire, and MS just released MSE the day before yesterday, so I quickly gave it a try. Microsoft Security Essentials (MSE) can protect computers running Windows XP, Vista, and Windows 7 against viruses, spyware, rootkits, and Trojans. The Microsoft Security Essentials software itself cannot fend off all web threats, but when used with the IE8 browser and a fully updated Windows operating system, it will provide users with a complete security solution. This product is free to use and will replace the previous paid antivirus product OneCare, aiming to encourage users who have not yet used security software to use security software as much as possible. The official MSE page: http://www.microsoft.com/security_essentials It seems the download link is no longer visible now. So I found a few direct download portals: XP 32-bit VISTA 7 32-bit VISTA 7 64-bit [11.21 update] Official download page http://www.microsoft.com/security_essentialsDefault_zh_cn.aspx

title: Security sandbox issue #2123
content: The first note on security sandboxes. Security sandboxes have tripped up plenty of people, so this is well-trodden ground. This afternoon I ran into error 2123. The scene of the crimeA certain list flash page needed to support gravatar avatars (gravatar’s cross-domain policy file lives at http://www.gravatar.com/avatar/crossdomain.xml). While loading the avatars they serve up, I hit a security sandbox violation, with this error: SecurityError: Error #2123: Security sandbox violation: Loader.content:http://www.\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*/lib.swf cannot access http://www.gravatar.com/avatar/3b3be63a4c2a439b013787721dfce802.jpg?s=26d=monsterid. Not authorized to access any policy file. at flash.display::Loaderget content() at org.mousebomb.srcloader::SwfLoaderonLoadComplete() At first I assumed I needed a crossdomain file, so I threw in Security.loadPolicyFile(“http://www.gravatar.com/avatar/crossdomain.xml“); to try it — no luck. Actually it isn’t needed at all — I just want to read and display an image cross-domain after publishing to a website, and within a remote network domain that is directly allowed as read-only access to audiovisual media content. The culpritLater I wrote a separate file and tested it with Loader — it read and displayed the image just fine. That got me thinking: the real cause of the security error was the resource loader I was using. In the resource pool’s smallest unit of work, the Loader hands off the visual object each time it finishes loading one, then calls unload so it can pick up a new task. The snippet: _isFree true; var _loadedData : DisplayObject _loader.content; _loader.unload(); var outEvent : SrcloaderEvent new SrcloaderEvent(SrcloaderEvent.COMPLETE, {key:_key, type:_type, data:_loadedData}); this.dispatchEvent(outEvent); Handing off the visual object like that (the error shows up on the _loader.content line) is treated by Flash Player as “cross-domain data handling”, which breaks the read-only permission and isn’t allowed. The solutionJust swap this part out and use Loader to load and display. For displaying and reading cross-domain audiovisual media objects, Loader has to be the container directly. [11.8 addendum]As far as I understand it, to process an image from a remote network domain (draw and the like), all you need is a cross-domain policy file on the server that says it’s permitted and a loaderContext that has read that policy file — but in practice, you still can’t touch it. Maybe I just don’t understand the security policy well enough; I solved the problem last time but never dug into it. Today a guy in the group (pickgliss), trying to solve this, proposed a way around the fact that images loaded with Loader can’t be drawn or have their BitmapData manipulated: first load the image as binary with URLLoader, then load it as a display object with Loader.loadBytes. I tacked on drawing to a bitmap and smoothing to test it, and sure enough, it works! Note: this method applies when the remote server has a cross-domain security policy granting permission but you still can’t operate on the display object. It does not apply when there’s no cross-domain security policy, or when the policy file doesn’t allow it. Example of getting around the security error: package { import flash.display.Bitmap; import flash.display.BitmapData; import flash.display.DisplayObject; import flash.display.Loader; import flash.display.Sprite; import flash.events.Event; import flash.net.URLLoader; import flash.net.URLLoaderDataFormat; import flash.net.URLRequest; import flash.utils.ByteArray; public class Test extends Sprite { public function Test() { var req : URLRequest new URLRequest(“http://uc.discuz.net/data/avatar/001/29/18/69\_avatar\_middle.jpg“); var loader : URLLoader new URLLoader(req); loader.dataFormat URLLoaderDataFormat.BINARY; loader.addEventListener(Event.COMPLETE, __complete); } private function __complete(e : Event) : void { var data : ByteArray e.target.data; var loader : Loader new Loader(); loader.contentLoaderInfo.addEventListener(Event.COMPLETE, imageDataComplete); loader.loadBytes(data); } private function imageDataComplete(e : Event) : void { var dio : DisplayObject e.target.content; var bmp : Bitmap new Bitmap(new BitmapData(dio.width, dio.height),”auto”,true); bmp.bitmapData.draw(dio); bmp.x 100; bmp.y 100; bmp.width 50; bmp.height 50; addChild(bmp); } } }

title: Garbled Chinese characters in Flash text input
content: Last time I ran into the problem of Flash’s NavigateToURL being blocked in IE, and the fix was to set wmode. Last night I hit another wmode problem: a text input field in Flash (a genuine TextField in CS4, type’input’), once embedded in a web page, couldn’t take Chinese input properly in Firefox — the IME worked, but everything typed came out garbled. My environment: Firefox 3.5.3 + Flash Player Plugin 10.0.32.18 debug build. IE8 + Flash Player ActiveX 10.0.32.18 release build. At first I suspected the swf itself, but opening it in IE worked perfectly fine. Then I grabbed standalone Flash Player 9 and standalone Flash Player 10 and ran them — no garbled text either. Only testing inside a Firefox web page had the problem. Next I suspected that some new feature in Flash CS4 was producing a file that was unusable under certain conditions, so I published three swf builds — fp10, fp9, fp8 — and tested each one. The problem persisted. With no cause in sight, I just dragged the swf straight into Firefox. And that drag turned out to be the breakthrough — I found the cause: opening it directly in Firefox produced no garbled text at all! That meant the culprit had to be the settings used to embed the Flash in the page. In the end I tracked down the problem: Firefox Flash Player 10 Plugin wmode’opaque’ garbles the input — under Firefox, the Flash Player 10 Plugin running a non-window-mode swf has a Chinese input garbling issue. (Maybe an Adobe bug?) Solution: I still have to switch wmode back to window… Never mind, I’ll accept it. Window it is, and I’ll find another way to force the frame rate…

title: A Peek at the Flash CS5 Rumors
content: This article gives us a bit of insider gossip about Flash CS5. There are a few typos in it, and for someone whose English isn’t up to much, like me, it was enough to bring tears to your eyes. A few things I paid attention to: Adoption rateLooking at the current state of the Flash platform, FlashPlayer10 installs are still climbing, and the new figures are expected to reach over 90% coverage in the near term. Flash CS5 featuresThe biggest news for developers is that Flash authoring is finally integrated with FlashBuilder. If you’re using Flash CS5, you can export a new FlashBuilder project through a new export dialog. If you work in FlashBuilder, it goes the other way too — you can point it at a FLA and it will build a FlashBuilder project for it. What’s more, Flash projects can be tested and profiled with the built-in FlashBuilder. Put together, these form a complete and efficient workflow: you write code in FB, then exporttest your files with the Flash IDE. (Mousebomb: personally, a lot of my projects right now are code in FDT + export and test in the FLASH IDE, so it looks like the CS5 era will be even more convenient and efficient) Editing in the Flash authoring environment has been improved as well, and the team has shifted its focus back onto “making Flash more user-friendly”. There’s now a new code samples panel, aimed at people learning AS3, which is something of a callback to how useful behaviors were in older versions. Click any of them and the code gets added to the timeline, making that part of the job easier for beginners — but since it’s configurable, it’s really more of a built-in Snippets panel for Flash, so you can stuff all kinds of things into it. Finally there’s a section on Flash Mobile upgrades that doesn’t really affect me for now, so I’ll skip it. Now that 3G is everywhere, mobile online games are about to become a hot topic — maybe I’ll need to dig into that someday.

title: Frequently Asked Questions About Time Travel (movie)
content: I stumbled on this movie this afternoon. It’s no blockbuster, but it’s a genuinely rare gem. The cast gives me the same feeling as watching a DND live-play video. The imagination runs wild, it’s got a real spoof vibe, and it’s a lot of fun. Halfway through I was laughing so hard my stomach hurt. This is nothing like the flood of pretentious sci-fi films that try so hard to be rigorous and end up riddled with holes. This movie doesn’t wrap itself in blockbuster packaging, its visuals are nothing special, and it doesn’t pile on VFX to sell some legendary future world. The whole thing is just a bunch of sci-fi maniacs playing a drunken game where you can’t tell what’s real and what’s not. A movie like this is something to enjoy as a casual game among friends letting their imaginations run loose. There’s absolutely no need to take it seriously — just enjoy how entertaining the ride is. By the time it ended, I was beside myself with laughter. I saw people on Douban tearing into this film as low-quality, complaining that it tosses around terms like “chaos theory” without being able to justify any of it. Personally, I don’t think there’s any need to be so serious. The opening already tells us: “As for how time travel works, the more you think about it, the less clear it gets.” It’s a humorous, wildly freewheeling fantasy farce from the start — it doesn’t owe reality anything, and the audience doesn’t need to go poking around hunting for bugs. Speaking of this film being disgusting, it reminds me of that new Journey to the West TV series that was in the news not long ago — the master and his three disciples all have romance subplots! Now that’s what you call cringe-inducing. Now that is what you call disgusting. Just a thought. There’s plenty of legitimately well-funded, big-budget garbage out there, and plenty of gems made with rough, knockoff-style craft. Every tier of film has its good and its bad. What’s most disgusting isn’t a knockoff spoof — it’s the self-serious trash. Btw, I watched the first episode of Fringe season 2 this afternoon and was a bit disappointed — maybe my expectations were too high.

title: Switched the OS on my desktop, and now I'm back to playing with WIN7
content: Yesterday I went through the hassle of reinstalling the OS on my desktop. I’d been torn between Windows 7 and Ubuntu, but in the end it was Windows 7. Whenever I mention Windows 7, my friends’ first concern is always compatibility. The last stretch of time I used Windows 7, as I recall, was back at Qoolu, and every night WoW, CnC3 and RA3 all ran without a single compatibility issue. Older games are a different story, though (why do I always start with games…). EA games from before Lord of the Rings: The Battle for Middle-earth, Warcraft, Diablo and the like are all unsupported. Oddly enough, it is compatible with StarCraft — the “garbled graphics” version, that is. Taobao and online banking, naturally, are not compatible. This time I wasn’t installing it for gaming performance. What I mainly wanted was a machine for the occasional bit of entertainment, but above all to serve as a test server for my development environment. My worry was whether it would hold up well as a server. Once it was installed, I found that as a dev test machine (setting aside the performance demands of high concurrency), it works pretty much ideally. I set up IIS7.5 + .net2.0 + php5.2.1 + mysql5 + phpmyadmin. Unlike when I’m at the office, this time I installed the Chinese version, and I found plenty of details are more user-friendly. There are still a few harmless bugs, though, while I wait for MS to put out patches. My poor desktop has put in years of service, slaving away for me like an ox; now that it’s getting on in years, I’m giving it a new heart so it can spring back to life. Time flies — after all these years, the system rating comes out at just 4.4 now; the CPU and memory have both aged. Back in the day it scored 4.8 under Vista. Norton on my laptop is about to expire. Once it does, I may reinstall Windows 7 there too.

Abrams (creator of Lost), Roberto Orci and Alex Kurtzman (the team behind Star Trek, Mission: Impossible III and Alias) — it will take you through the thrills and terror that lie somewhere between science fiction and reality. title: QQ personalized domain email
content: Domain email is a personalized mail service from Tencent. If you own a domain, a few simple settings are all it takes to create mailboxes that use your domain as the email suffix. It comes with the following features: a custom account name and email logo of your choosing, up to 10 mailboxes under the same domain, and group functionality. With the domain email service you can swap your QQ Mail address for one under your own domain. For example, 405572555@qq.com corresponds to mousebomb@flashj.cn. Today I gave it a try and set up mousebomb@flashj.cn along with domain mailboxes for a few friends. Process: 1. Log into your QQ Mail, go to [Settings]-[Experience Lab]-[Domain Email] and choose to activate it now. 2. Once activated, click “Try it now” to enter the domain email management page. You’ll need to verify and configure your domain. 3. Follow the prompts to upload the text file QQ Mail provides to your site, or go to your domain management platform and set up a CNAME record. 4. As prompted, add an MX record in your domain management platform — leave the host name blank and set the target host to mxdomain.qq.com. 5. Then come back to QQ Mail and click “Settings complete, submit for verification”, and you’re activated. After activation you still need to create an admin account: go to member management, where you’ll see prompts, fill in the info and you’re done. Then you can create a few more users, for example I set up a gfox@flashj.cn for gfox. Under basic info you can upload an image as the Logo. The supported image formats are jpg and gif, and the recommended image size is 190 pixels long by 40 pixels wide. QQ Mail itself is tied to QQ, so you get a notification as soon as mail arrives, and the user experience is first-class (I’d say it’s even better than Gmail). Now that it supports your own domain too, how could I not be on board? [09.09.19 update] Got an email saying Tencent has updated the domain email: 1. Supports accessing a personalized login page at mail.yourdomain.com. 2. Supports editing some of the admin info (the admin account can’t be changed yet, but support is coming later). 3. Domain email accounts can serve as the primary display account for QQ. 4. Others: fixed the display issue with custom LOGOs; member account phone numbers are no longer a required field; added more prompts during setup, etc.

title: getURL or navigateToURL popup windows are blocked by IE
content: Problem description:This afternoon I ran into a hassle: IE7 and IE8 intercept navigateToURL(xxx,_blank) inside Flash; getURL under AS2 gets intercepted the same way. I feel like I’ve run into this before, but it doesn’t happen that often, so I never bothered to dig into what conditions trigger the interception. It came up again today, so it’s a good chance to figure out why. After some searching, I found plenty of discussions from last year. Someone pointed out: IE7 and Firefox (the version I’m using is 2.0.0.11) block opening new windows with the navigateToURL method, while the getURL method in AS2 doesn’t — which is pretty annoying. Since the project chose AS3, we just have to find a way around it. The first thing that comes to mind is ExternalInterface, of course, but testing showed it still gets blocked. Then I wondered whether adding wmode would help, so I added the wmode attribute set to opaque to the page — and sure enough, it worked. Here’s the getURL method in AS3: function getURL(url:String,window:String”_blank”):void{ var broswer:StringExternalInterface.call(“function getBrowser(){return navigator.userAgent}”) as String; if(broswer.indexOf(“Firefox”)!-1 broswer.indexOf(“MSIE 7.0”)!-1){ ExternalInterface.call(‘window.open(“‘+url+’”,”‘+window+’”)’); }else{ navigateToURL(new URLRequest(url),window); }} Usage is the same as getURL in AS2. Also, I only tested IE67 and Firefox 2 — I didn’t test other browsers like Safari. Last but most importantly, you have to set the flash object’s wmode attribute to opaque or transparent in the HTML. Because the wmode attribute defaults to window, which means the Flash application has no interaction at all with the HTML layer. The idea above is to pop up the window via as calling js, and that requires wmode’opaque’ or wmode’transparent’. But times have changed, the rules of the game have shifted again, and the method above no longer applies. I just tested: Firefox 3.5.3 doesn’t intercept it. IE7 and IE8 both intercept it. How strange — how can that be! So I went through the handful of cool Flash sites I had bookmarked, one by one, and found that apsou‘s site has _blank content that doesn’t get intercepted~ I looked into the code on its page and found one difference from the many sites that do get intercepted: wmode. Solution:I finally found that setting wmode solves the problem: when wmode’window’ (the default value), IE no longer intercepts. This may have something to do with the ActiveX mechanism under IE. The line quoted above — “Last but most importantly, you have to set the flash object’s wmode attribute to opaque or transparent in the HTML” — isn’t something you need to worry too much about either. When wmode is window, you can still call js. Even though I have a solution, I’m really reluctant to change wmode to window. Looks like I still have to communicate with js and let the js side handle getting around the interception. But thinking it over carefully, it’s actually not a big deal, because the situation with domestic netizens is quite amusing. Generally, people using Firefox or IE7+ or Safari or Google Chrome are the trend-chasers, or the ones who’ve played with all kinds of web2.0 products — the more high-end netizens, so to speak. These people all know what blocking means, and well-intentioned features like “block pop-ups” work better for them. These people usually set up whitelists, so there’s no need to worry about them being unable to access content because of browser blocking. And the majority of the remaining users on XP + stock IE6 are largely not all that enthusiastic about the internet — and conveniently, these users’ browsers won’t intercept our flash either, so they don’t have to learn network filtering settings. Heh heh — each stays in its own place, naturally harmonious. The differences between the various wmode valuesEh, while I’m at it, let me list a few differences between the wmode values. Here’s a summary of how the various wmode values differ and what each is suited for: Window is the default, window mode, and doesn’t hog the CPU too badly. Transparent is transparent, windowless mode. Opaque is opaque, windowless mode. The most efficient is window mode. For transparency, use transparent. And when you need dynamic interaction (like js), or when window mode is unstable, use opaque. Window and transparent produce screen tearing when dragged inside an iframe under IE6 — personal experience. One more thing: windowless mode consumes a lot of resources, but it guarantees the frame rate.

title: Recent favorite album: Return to Purity
content: I happened to preview this album, and it’s the xianxia style I fell for on the very first listen. Why did 《相思引》 sound so familiar? Turns out a friend who plays 诛仙 had played it for me before. That reminds me — some of Liu Fang’s covers of classics are great too, and they really hold up. For a while I even had her version of 《青花瓷》 as my phone ringtone. Compared with the cookie-cutter pop music flooding everything right now, this new age style with its old-Chinese flavor is a real relief for the ears. Dong Zhen, long known in gaming circles for her behind-the-scenes songwriting, moved in front of the mic in 2007, and her debut audiophile album 《贞爱一回》 officially announced her arrival as a singer. Dong Zhen’s voice is sweet and tender with a character all its own; she can make a song achingly beautiful and utterly absorbing, and she is widely regarded as the best choice for Chinese guofeng xianxia music. She has sung theme songs for many well-known games, such as 《逍遥游》 for 《新绝代双骄前传》 and 《雕花笼》 for 《鱼戏江湖》. In May 2008 she wrote and performed 《情醉》 as the theme song for Perfect World’s online game 《诛仙》, in June 2009 she again sang for 《诛仙》, this time the theme song of a new expansion, 《相思引》, and in July she wrote and performed 《仙恋》 for Shanda Games’ 《蜀山新传》… The steady release of one classic xianxia piece after another cemented Dong Zhen’s status as “the first talented woman of Chinese-style xianxia music.” Dong Zhen herself produced 《返璞归贞》. Besides collecting all the hugely popular online game theme songs she has sung over the past few years — 《相思引》, 《情醉》 — and covering old classics like 《新鸳鸯蝴蝶梦》 and 《追梦人》, it also includes brand-new originals she wrote with care, such as 《金缕衣》 and 《返璞归贞》. It is the first album in China that genuinely represents the creative standard of xianxia music, a heavyweight compilation that xianxia music fans have been waiting for. Dong Zhen’s singing is fresh and free of convention, deeply felt, a style entirely her own — truly, “misty rain over Jiangnan reveals the return to simplicity; immortal notes, like tangled threads, all return to Zhen.” Tracklist 01.返璞归贞 02.相思引 03.金缕衣 04.雕花笼 05.仙恋 06.追梦人 07.情醉 08.刀剑如梦 09.回到起点 10.美人浴 11.新鸳鸯蝴蝶梦 12.逍遥游 13.你不在秋天 14.金缕衣(伴奏) 15.半月琴(笛子版) Download mp3: http://www.rayfile.com/zh-cn/files/9896c938-9a4f-11de-9a3b-0014221b798a/ http://www.verycd.com/topics/2766612/ APE: http://www.rayfile.com/zh-cn/files/e8c902c7-9a4c-11de-bfb3-0014221f469f/ http://www.verycd.com/topics/2766939/

title: “Creative Factory” sparks a war of words
content: On September 4, 2009, Dr. Kai-Fu Lee (http://blog.sina.com.cn/kaifulee) left Google. The Creative Factory site surfaced. This should have been a great thing, but it kicked off an argument on a few IT blogs. http://initiative.yo2.cn/archives/642502 That post blew up. Just in case it gets “harmonized,” here’s a copy: http://www.innovation-works.com/New.asp 1. ASP — is that innovation? 2. In English, “news” and “new” are two completely different words, right? New.asp shows just what a knockoff job the outsourcing firm that built the site did. 3. I won’t even mention the td-based page layout; the real kicker is content”texthtml; charsetgb2312” — that alone deserves a good rant. 4. Under Media Contact, there’s actually a .doc file. Honestly, I can’t be bothered to install Word these days, and if it were installed I couldn’t be bothered to open it — I just drag everything into G Docs. Good thing it isn’t .docx. 5. Fine, the English version is UTF-8, but http://en.innovation-works.com/new.asp?page=1‘ throws an error. A few signs suggest kaifulee was in a hurry this time — maybe his “20% time” all went into the student site. But also, I get the feeling that *.google.* is blocked, that the XXXXXX at Google’s Beijing headquarters was XXXXXX (credit here to the big shots at T University for the tip), that Kai-Fu Lee was “resigned” within 24 hours, and finally that some Twitter account muttered to itself, “After XXX, XXX is more obedient.” It’s not as if there’s no causal link between all of it. Innovation Works — well, the site is just so-so… On the art side, the clean style is quite nice, but look closely at the details and you’ll find plenty of blurry spots, which shows whoever did the design just phoned it in. The front end uses the transitional standard, the layout uses tables… in this day and age. The ASP and mojibake problems really threw me. And the main body of the site being stuffed with tons of .doc files always makes me think of some PR10 department that has screwed over countless webmasters… hidecloud Says: September 7th, 2009 at 19:36 Google Docs supports docx now. The site was outsourced by Kai-Fu Lee’s assistant to a university — 7,500 yuan for development plus a year of maintenance. I don’t know why Tsinghua students’ English has gotten this bad… Later, Lonely Volcano jumped in to flame the OP: If you’re so badass, go invent some XXP technology yourself — that’s what you’d call innovation! You use tech someone else invented, and just because the tech you use is a bit trendier, you think you’re innovative?! Kai-Fu Lee’s goal is to give other people opportunities to innovate and start businesses — he’s not the one who’s supposed to be innovating. Everyone get that straight, OK? China finally has someone with that kind of ideal, and you, as Chinese, not only don’t support him, you sit here sneering at him. What’s going on in your heads? What do you get out of tearing him down like this? You’re not trying to make China’s IT industry, and China’s environment for young entrepreneurs, as bad as Chinese soccer, are you? Why is it as hard as a man milking to say a few words of encouragement, while sarcasm just rolls off your tongue? It’s such a simple website — why fuss over the newest tech? Kai-Fu Lee isn’t a professional web developer anyway! Some of the commenters above even brought up LUA. Are you nuts? Your heads are stuck on nothing but tech — you’ve forgotten why technology exists in the first place! Support Chinese innovation, support Chinese youth entrepreneurship, support every view and action that helps! So I support Kai-Fu Lee! And if anyone else wants to pool a few hundred million to do something similar, I’d support that too! All the comments so far: Personally, I think chasing tech for tech’s sake is pretty extreme, and unnecessary. And the people being sarcastic aren’t mocking Dr. Kai-Fu — they’re mocking the quality of today’s university students, with a real “wanting iron to become steel” flavor to it. If that site really was outsourced to Tsinghua students, it says a lot about the caliber of today’s college students. Also, under everyone’s “criticism and encouragement,” the site keeps getting improved. Today I saw that new.asp has been changed to news.asp.

title: Watched District 9 last night
content: These past two months, what I’ve been watching wasn’t movies — it was loneliness… Finally, though, I watched something with a bit of substance — last night I saw District 9. In 1990, a massive spaceship appeared in the sky above Earth. People were terrified, yet wildly curious. After a tense stretch of waiting, the alien ship still showed no sign of activity. Humanity finally crept closer and forced its way inside the cabin, only to find countless aliens. They were hideous to look at, like shrimp, and in extremely poor health — weak and feeble. It turned out this was a group of alien refugees. Eventually the people of Earth took them in and quarantined them in an area of Johannesburg, South Africa, a place called “District 9.” After 20 years of reproduction, the alien refugee population had swollen to 1.8 million, and conflicts with the surrounding humans kept flaring up. More and more people were calling for the “prawns” to be driven off Earth. MNU (Multi-National United), after consultations, decided to relocate the alien refugees to an even more remote area. Wikus (Sharlto Copley), an agent in MNU’s Alien Affairs Department, is put in charge of the relocation. During the mobilization Wikus is arrogant and offhand, clashing with local residents again and again. In the end he pays for his behavior — the aliens’ mysterious fluid infects him, and Wikus slowly transforms into an alien… Very good impression. The story is unusual, the performances are spot-on, the director is exactly the right fit, the visuals are apt, the music is lovely. The film’s shooting style is highly realistic, telling the whole story through interview angles, news angles, surveillance footage and war-correspondent angles — it plays like a documentary. I’m not the biggest fan of this “shaky” perspective, but this deeply immersive approach really does suit this film better. The main ingredients of the story a grand, high-minded refugee camp + a bunch of down-and-out alien grunts + three aliens secretly scheming to fix their ship and go home + MNU’s live-experiment conspiracy + the sloppy protagonist infected by the fluid and undergoing genetic fission + betrayal by friends and family + a mutual faith in never giving up, never letting go. Refined by the screenwriters, director and crew, these ingredients undergo a magical chemical reaction, turning into communication barriers, racial discrimination, mockery, contempt and self-righteousness. Once again, it lays bare the ugliness of human nature. The process is riveting — full of ups and downs, one climax after another. The ending brings back the beauty of human nature. MNU’s conspiracy is exposed, the aliens are moved to a humane District 10, and the protagonist, now fully mutated, sits in a garbage dump making roses, one by one, for his faraway wife. The only thing I find strange is this: the aliens’ technology is so advanced, so why didn’t they communicate with humans from the start and ask for help repairing the ship? Instead they waited to be shipped off down to District 9 to live a subhuman life. Their intelligence must be highly developed — so why couldn’t they communicate effectively? On a ship carrying millions of people, was there no interstellar diplomat? But the film never explains any of this, so there’s no point in overthinking it. title: GTA4 Construction Site Battle Mission
content: Last night I got to that mission, can’t remember the exact name. It’s the one you pick up from Playboy X — head into the construction site and kill a few gang leaders. I died a ton of times. Every restart meant driving for ages just to get back to the site, and I don’t even want to talk about how much time that wasted. Sigh… The combat in this mission is great though — lots of enemies, plenty of cover, outdoors, and it doesn’t show you where all the enemies are, so it feels pretty realistic. More than half of my deaths were from my own grenades. I just can’t get a feel for the damn things — I’d always throw one, it’d bounce off a pillar and come right back and blow me up, or else I’d get that ringing in my ears… Alas. Back when I played CS at the office I was a crack grenade thrower, everyone ran for their lives when they saw me coming. That night, karma came back for all of it. Later I figured out the mission is actually a piece of cake if you take the right route. Grab a car, drive up from the left, and whenever you spot an enemy, get out, press Q and pop shots from behind a window. On the platform, take out the No. 2 guy first, then kill the No. 1 leader, then snipe the No. 2. Don’t follow the map to point three — instead loop around from the left platform and hit them from behind, toss a few grenades, then snipe the No. 3 guy from way off. The last one, No. 4, is right behind you, not far — just run over and finish him. I also came across a video online, so I snatched it (this guy goes in wearing a black suit to do his killing — I was his color inverse that day): Update — found a walkthrough description: Mission: Deconstruction for Beginners Niko arrives at Playboy X’s place. Playboy’s house is basically a mansion, and you can even play pool. Playboy gets to talking about life with Niko, asking what his motivation is. Niko says just to make some money, and adds that he doesn’t care whether he lives or dies. X wants Niko to go with him to a construction site. Right in the middle of the conversation, an ugly-looking Black guy shows up — Playboy’s good friend Dwayne, just out of prison. You can tell Playboy treats this friend coldly, even muttering under his breath: “Shit, what’s he doing here?” Dwayne doesn’t think much of Playboy either, feeling he’s forgotten where he came from, and after Playboy takes Niko out he curses: “Shit, ungrateful bastard.” Mission briefing: Drive Playboy to the construction site. On the way, Playboy says there’s a construction tycoon from Dubai, and the site has been taken over by the Mafia. He says that in Liberty City, the so-called union is just another word for the Mafia — if the Mafia wants the union to strike, they strike. He wants Niko to wipe out the Mafia holed up at the site. Niko asks why he’s helping this Dubai tycoon, and Playboy says, well, we’re all from Africa, right, so of course we look out for each other. Niko corrects him that Dubai isn’t in Africa (Dubai is in the Middle East), so Playboy changes his tune to something about how the whole world is one family. Niko says Playboy’s a successful guy, so why doesn’t he build a school or something for the ghetto he grew up in? Playboy says he isn’t successful enough yet — once he’s truly made it, he’ll give back to the neighborhood. Once you reach the site, take the construction elevator up to the top floor with Playboy X, and snipe the 3 Mafia guys holding the high ground. They’re not easy to spot, but if you look carefully you can find them. Then Playboy says he’ll direct you from up here, and you go take out those union leaders at the site. Niko takes the elevator down and heads into the site. Same as before: find good cover, advance step by step, and throw grenades when necessary — they can take down a whole crowd. Kill the 4 union leaders one by one. Each time you take one out, the next one’s position gets marked on the map. Afterwards, Playboy says Dwayne complained that he’d been snubbing him, so he sends Niko to find Dwayne and do a little something for him.

title: So busy, such a homebody
content: Been swamped lately with a few websites, running myself half to death, but my resource pool is finally about to free up. Recycling worker thread 0… recycled successfully, resources released. Recycling worker thread 1… recycled successfully, resources released… Saw an old post the other day: “Keywords for Homebody Guys and Girls, Plus a Self-Test” Obsession — Obsessed with something: anime, video games, a pop star, a certain person, a certain thing… This obsession can also strike suddenly — you fall for it out of nowhere and can’t pull yourself out. Computer dependence — Going a long time without a computer is brutal. Internet dependence — Whatever you’re doing, you want to go online; once online, there’s nothing to do, so you just stay connected. Don’t want to go to workschool — Sometimes you’re sick of workschool, absolutely hate it. But there’s nothing you can do about it. Irregular daily schedule — No regular routine to speak of. Rarely go out — Rather than go out, you’d stay home. Joining an activity that requires going out often takes a long time to think over. Don’t like meeting strangers — Interacting with or getting to know strangers in real life fills you with dread. More or less two-sided personality — When faced with things you don’t like, you’ll mask your true thoughts and just muddle through; sometimes you feel like you have a dual personality. Collector’s compulsion — You like collecting at least one kind of item, or several, and never tire of it. Single — Under normal circumstances, you’re single. Like keeping a blogdiary — You like writing a blog or diary, or using photos to record your life. Fall for fictional characters — You have a tendency to fall for fictional characters, like characters in manga or books — people who don’t exist in real life. Outwardly cool, inwardly passionate — Undeniable: homebodies are among the most “still waters run deep” people in the world. More or less, people will comment on how reserved you seem on the outside. 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 are all way too accurate… Just now I saw another site that bills itself as “Stay home to the max! Vegetables and fruit delivered to your door.” The URL is http://www.caidaojia.com/ Merchants really know how to find a market, huh. Back in Shanghai, 129T.com was already plenty convenient, and now Beijing has online grocery shopping too. Looks like the future of the homebody life is bright.

title: Farm Frenzy 3

You keep completing tasks to move on to the next level, and the more money you make, the better farm equipment you can buy. You build five types of farms across the world’s five continents, i.e. five major levels, and each level yields farm equipment with different functions. Basic gameplay: Raise chickens, ducks, sheep, cows, yaks and other livestock, and make enough money to meet the requirements. When wild animals attack, click like crazy to cage them and sell them off; dogs keep the wild animals away, cats pick up items. Click the well, then click the ground to get grass to feed the cows. title: A gotcha with 404 error pages under IIS
content: I was just testing the site and ran into a problem with Flash image loading. I found that when loading a nonexistent file, Flash still reports progress info, and after reaching 100% it shows nothing. I was completely baffled. Later I checked with Firebug and found that the image being loaded actually came back with an HTTP header of 200 status, and there was even a file there! Then it hit me — it was caused by the 404 error page I had set up in IIS. There’s one thing to watch out for here: IIS lets you specify the 404 error page in two ways. One is a relative URL, the other is a local file. If you use the URL method, IIS returns the 404 page but sends a 200 status header with it, which is effectively a redirect. Only with the file method does IIS return a 404 status header. Remember this, remember this…

title: Musings Inspired by Cats
content: Thoughts inspired by a cat Half a month ago, a cat came scrambling in off the balcony. It lives with me now. At first, its demands were simple: just a place to crash. So much so that on the first day it refused to leave — even though I had nothing to feed it. I opened the door and carried it out; it darted straight back in. I carried it out and quickly shut the door; it stood outside yowling at the door, dead set on getting back in. Later I got it some food, gave it a bath, bought cat food and kept its bowl full every day, bought cat litter and set up a toilet. Every time I open the front door, it comes over to take a look — but it doesn’t step out. Life keeps getting better. It doesn’t have to worry about food, drink, or the litter box. It’s getting stronger, braver, and it’s developed a temper. Two weeks in, it’s bouncing off the walls doing whatever it pleases. It’s got it in for my network cable — swatting, pouncing, until it gets tangled up and left dangling in midair, yowling for help… When it hears noise outside the door, it walks over too. Thinking about going out, I guess. Heh, I knew this day would come. No rush. Maybe one day its urge to explore the outside world will hit the threshold, and with the smell of good food drifting in through the door, it’ll slip out during some careless moment when I open it, and take off without a backward glance, off to explore an infinite, unknown new world. Maybe opportunity is waiting for it out there — a change of scene might mean a better life. After all, I’m the kind of guy who never even leaves the house; where this exercise-loving cat’s needs are concerned, we’re hopelessly mismatched. Or maybe its luck won’t be so good: curiosity satisfied, but the easy life gone. The day passes, it’s hungry, it’s thirsty, and a whole pile of troubles shows up… My mind immediately starts modeling the different possibilities: Possibility 1: It slips out, happily trots over to someone else’s home, and sweetly meows at a family eating dinner. They’re delighted and take it in. From then on, the cat lives a happy life. Possibility 2: It slips out, happily trots over to someone else’s home, and sweetly meows at a table of strangers eating dinner. They’re delighted and take it in. Two weeks later, the cat finds this boring life tiresome again, picks a random day, and runs away from home. Possibility 3: It slips out, happily follows the smell to someone else’s home, but they ignore it. It meows pitifully and sweetly outside, meows until it’s hungry, then comes back at night and knocks on my door, back to a carefree life of eating, drinking, and sleeping. Possibility 4: It slips out, happily follows the smell, running and running. Where there’s a will there’s a way — even for a cat — and it finally finds something good to eat. After eating its fill, it forgets the way home. So it keeps going door to door, looking for a kindred spirit to take it in. Hmm, living the free and easy life… Possibility 5: It slips out, happily follows the smell to someone else’s home, but they ignore it. It meows pitifully and sweetly outside, meows until it’s hungry — but it’s forgotten the way home. So it becomes a stray cat, one meal away from no meal, with the next meal possibly stewing in a pot. At night, hungry and sleepy, it wants to find a place to shelter, wants to find something good to eat, misses its old life, and feels miserable — but there’s no going back. As a cat, what should it be after? I’m not a cat, so I can’t really know. But I do think that as cats, we already have a pretty comfortable life, and we should learn to appreciate it. This reminds me of Shinjuku Incident, which I watched not long ago. The narration and dialogue go: The most primitive human desire is nothing more than food and warmth. But once people see what they don’t have, the desires kick in. You have to learn to be content A group of people band together because they’ve been bullied, or because of some demand. Once they build up power, the rights follow. That’s how violent gangs have evolved since ancient times. Unfortunately, power changes human nature. The old habit of swallowing your pride turns into arrogance, and the behavior starts spinning out of control. I’m not saying a cat shouldn’t refuse to ever go outside. The point is that we should cherish what we already have first, and not lose ourselves to the flashy temptations of the outside world. So desire is something you absolutely have to learn to control. Human Weaknesses says that men are all lustful and women all love to look pretty. And this cat is a glutton. Same principle: cats and people alike are likely to trip over these impulses. So purify your mind, shake off temptation, and be content with what you have.

title: World of Warcraft's new expansion — Cataclysm
content: Yesterday I heard from Fenix that Blizzard had registered a new trademark. At the time I figured it was a new game. And I thought to myself, pfft — with Diablo 3 and StarCraft 2 delayed this long, any new game has to be at least 10 years out. Fenix(2500402) 15:03:15 BLIZZARD just registered a new trademark called Cataclysm 鼠標炸彈 15:14:57 When did that news come out? 鼠標炸彈 15:15:01 So there’s a new game? 鼠標炸彈 15:15:10 Coming out in 2019… Fenix(2500402) 15:15:27 Oh yeah Didn’t expect to see the news today: turns out “Cataclysm” is the name of the new World of Warcraft expansion. At 9 a.m. North American time on the 21st (early morning of the 22nd Beijing time), BlizzCon opened. Blizzard officially announced the new World of Warcraft expansion: Cataclysm. (World of Warcraft - Cataclysm) Updating with a Simplified Chinese version of the video: Below is the official introduction to the new expansion, World of Warcraft: Cataclysm: After witnessing the downfall of Yogg-Saron, the other Old Gods also decided to descend upon Azeroth. And Deathwing, swayed by the Old Gods, is involved — this great cataclysm that has befallen Azeroth was brought about by Deathwing and the Old Gods together. While players were still fighting in Northrend, Deathwing had already summoned an army of elementals to scour Azeroth clean. General The level cap will be 85, because the designers wanted to focus on doing the right things well: redoing Azeroth and providing more high-end game content. The new advanced guild system will let players learn guild perks and level their guild up to a maximum of 20, and also spend points in a talent tree. You’ll gain things like cheaper repair costs, less durability loss on wipes, and even mass resurrection. Phasing technology can now add and remove terrain as you progress through the game — for example, a coastline will push inland as you advance along your quest line. Path of the Titans The talent trees won’t be expanded; there will only be 5 more talent points. The Path of the Titans system will let players build their character along specific paths. This is a new talent system that will offer new abilities and passive skills. A specialization system has been added, and a large number of talents will be redone. The point here is to move away from masses of talent skills, so you’re no longer dumping every single talent point into something just because a talent gives more damage or higher crit. Archaeology Archaeology is the new secondary profession. Details aren’t clear yet, but there should be more in the interview section below. Deathwing Deathwing, leader of the black dragonflight, will be the main villain of this expansion. After the Burning Legion’s invasion, Deathwing heard the whispers of the Old Gods, and he became immensely powerful yet utterly insane. His plan is to make the Alliance and the Horde let their guard down about things like drawing out the Elemental Planes. The Elemental Planes are worlds the Titans created for elemental creatures, but those creatures weren’t happy about it — guys like Ragnaros are very angry, and the consequences are severe. New Race — Worgen A few other races were once on the shortlist for the Alliance, but the designers felt the Alliance needed a feral race, and the Horde needed some wacky, cute flavor. Genn Greymane sealed off the Greymane Wall to block the Scourge invasion. Gilneas was on edge as the Scourge swept south in force. Arugal was once a good man and a patriot. He summoned the worgen hoping they would fight for Gilneas, but he was horrified by just how dangerous these creatures are. The worgen come from somewhere else… even from another time we don’t know about. They have a wolf inside, and for a long time they’ve been trying to come to terms with the beast spirit within them. Racial — Viciousness: increases damage dealt by 1%. Racial — Darkflight: increases movement speed by 70% for 10 seconds. Racial — Aberration: reduces the duration of curses and diseases affecting you by 15%. Racial — Flayer: increases Skinning skill by 15. New Race — Goblin Goblins are a high-tech race from Kezan, and their society is made up of various cartels, each led by a trade prince. They’re a new faction, not the ones you see in the game right now. The Cataclysm hit Kezan hard, and it may well have destroyed it. The goblins are now refugees stranded on the Lost Isles. As a goblin you’ll start out neutral and join the Horde through a quest line. Racial — Best Deals Anywhere: always get the best discount regardless of faction. Racial — Pack Hobgoblin: summons your servant, who provides bank access, lasts 1 minute, 30 second cooldown. Racial — Better Living Through Chemistry: increases Alchemy skill by 15. Racial — Rocket Barrage: fire a rocket from your belt at an enemy, dealing fire damage. 2 minute cooldown. Racial — Rocket Jump: activate your rocket belt to leap forward. 2 minute cooldown. Racial — Time is Money: increases attack and casting speed by 1%. The World Azeroth can now be flown in. Many zones will change to some degree — places like Elwynn Forest won’t change noticeably, but zones like the Barrens will be torn apart by Deathwing. The Wailing Caverns is now a lush area overgrown with tropical plants. The Barrens has more water, and the screenshots show a lot of vegetation. The Horde has finally conquered Southshore. Auberdine has been destroyed, and the night elves have built a new camp north of it. Garrosh wants to expand the Horde’s territory here, and has built a fortress in the south. Stonetalon Mountains has been cleared out by the goblins, and Azshara will be the new goblin zone — they’ll use Azshara’s quarries to build their city. We left only a tiny mark of ourselves on Northrend, while the old world will grow darker, and heroism and brotherhood will both become more indispensable than ever, just as the Warcraft series has always championed. Every zone will be redone with new quests, items, and art design. The old world will be a whole new experience, and you won’t be crying over quest rewards with agility plus spirit anymore. 7 new zones: Twilight Highlands, Mount Hyjal, Deepholm, Uldum, Gilneas, the Lost Isles, and the sunken city of Vashj’ir. The worgen and goblin starting zones will cover levels 1-15. The sunken city of Vashj’ir will be an underwater zone. Before the great cataclysm of the War of the Ancients, it was originally the capital city of Vashj. There will be a portal here leading to the Abyssal Maw, and through the Abyssal Maw you’ll reach the Elemental Plane of Water. Even though it’s underwater, you’ll be able to walk along the sea floor. There will be new underwater mounts, just as fast as regular flying mounts. Deepholm will be the hub of the expansion — from here you’ll be able to teleport to places like Mount Hyjal or Uldum. The Twilight’s Hammer now serves Deathwing, and summoned him back at full health and full power to the Temple of Earth at the center of the map. Uldum will have at least 2 dungeons and plenty of Egyptian-style scenery. The sea west of Tanaris is merely an illusion created by the Titans; Uldum is actually a brand-new zone. It’s said that some kind of ultimate weapon is hidden here. Uldum is also home to the Tol’vir, a race of stone cat-like beings created by the Titans. Ragnaros took advantage of the Cataclysm to return from the Elemental Plane of Fire, and he now wants to burn down the World Tree at Mount Hyjal. Malfurion has returned from the Emerald Dream. The entire Mount Hyjal zone will make heavy use of phasing technology. Twilight Highlands will be Grim Batol. When Deathwing returned from beneath the earth, he tore apart the seals of Grim Batol. This will be the Twilight’s Hammer’s base in Azeroth, and both the Alliance and the Horde will have port outposts here. The red dragonflight is still here, but has been pushed back to the western side of the zone, near the Wetlands. Orgrimmar has been rebuilt and reinforced with a lot of steel, and looks more like Garrosh’s fortress. The Undercity has been redesigned so you can fly there, and it looks way cooler from the outside. Deepholm isn’t directly connected to Azeroth — it’s just where Deathwing is bound to the earth. Dungeons and Raids The new raid is the Firelands. You’ll enter the Elemental Plane of Fire and visit the heart of Sulfuron, calling on a very angry, very serious Ragnaros. Uldum will have 2 new dungeons: the Lost City of the Tol’vir and the Halls of Origination (a Titan city). Skywall (the Elemental Plane of Air) will have a level-up dungeon and a raid. Grim Batol will have a level-up dungeon and a raid. The Deadmines and Shadowfang Keep will return as level-85 heroic dungeons. The new level-up dungeon Blackrock Caverns, located in Blackrock Spire. This will be a completely new dungeon — new art, new monsters, everything new. PvP New battleground: the Battle for Gilneas, where the goal is to control the city by capturing as many districts as possible. New PvP zone: Tol Barad. Like Wintergrasp, a battle starts every few hours, and the winning side takes control of Tol Barad Prison and can complete lots of richly rewarding daily quests. A rated battleground system has been added, offering the same tier of rewards as the arena. New arena maps. Blizzard, you are my faith, you are my light… When I see the state of the world shift with the story’s development, I feel both excited and thoroughly satisfied — this game, forever imitated yet never surpassed, has moved me once again. World of Warcraft, you have a soul. You lead countless players in witnessing the story unfold and the world change. Ice Cool! Looking forward to the new novel Arthas… looking forward to the movie…

title: Finished watching The Barber of Siberia
content: Last night I watched The Barber of Siberia until 1 a.m. before going to sleep. My mom said a friend recommended it — a really good film. Jeanne could have had a beautiful romance, but precisely because she made her living by deceiving people, misunderstandings piled up and complications multiplied. In this way, she unwittingly caused Andrei to accumulate more and more jealousy, until finally it spiraled out of control. Andrei’s jealousy drove him to do a series of things that would shape his entire life. Hot-blooded and young, he challenged a classmate stronger than himself and ended up badly wounded. When Jeanne whispered to the general to plead on his behalf, in his eyes it became an insult and a provocation from the general. In the end he attacked the general with a piano wire, was exiled to Siberia, and ruined his own future. Jealousy, possessiveness — the weaknesses of human nature, the punishment of impulse. Jeanne married her employer to get a Siberian passport — truly unscrupulous. And at last she got her wish and set off for Siberia. See, love makes people lose their heads. But it’s okay to do foolish things. Fate and time are always just, and the judgment of cause and effect is always irresistible. When all of this turns to dust, what can you say? You deceived people, you were jealous, you flew into a rage — weren’t you just playing yourself all along? Of course, Jeanne’s job was to deceive people, so she wasn’t wrong to deceive — but even without right or wrong, you’re still bound by cause and effect, and there’s no resisting it. Ten years of entanglement, and a young, handsome officer became a weathered forest ranger. Ten years of searching, and at last she reached the place where Andrei lived after his sentence ended. Twenty minutes of exploring, and once again she missed him in a daze, finally realizing she had come too late. Everything from those ten years was wiped out in the instant she got her answer. She opened the music box, looked at the photograph, and ten years of memory collapsed just like that. All the people, all the events, and the ten years of waiting at any cost — all of it settled into those twenty minutes. It takes ten years of karma to share a boat crossing, a hundred years to share a pillow in sleep. Swindlers never come to a good end, and romantic luck is always ruined by one’s own hand. Attitude determines destiny. Only sincerity keeps complications from multiplying. Where there is a beginning of affinity, there will be an end of affinity — and if what you do wounds morality and justice, the day your affinity ends will come all the sooner. Believing in love is useless; practicing compassion is enough. Life is truly precious, but love is worth even more. Though body and bones be shattered without a care, affinities gather and scatter, and another ten years pass. 8.22: Last night I watched Duplicity, and it was really great. Compared to The Barber of Siberia, it suits my taste much better. Super rational! Yeah, only love that hasn’t lost its reason can stand up to scrutiny. Watching Duplicity, by the end I was silently crying out, “So satisfying.”

title: The legendary 《Dong Dong Never Dies》
content: I remember, back before I switched my blog over to WordPress — that was more than a year ago now — I came across an amateur-made fighting game online. Most of the characters are played by real people. Hilarious, brilliant, seriously impressive. I remember the author’s blog was called “Jiangxi Dinosaur’s Lair” back then. There were only a handful of characters, the story wasn’t finished, and there were plenty of bugs, haha. I downloaded it and played for a while, but after I reinstalled my system I never went back to it. Not long ago (August 8), I saw the whole internet buzzing about this game, Dong Dong Never Die. This is the second version I’d been waiting over a year for — long awaited, finally here~ How great would it be to have the spare time to put together something this fun. Good stuff is meant to be shared, so here are the links: Download: rayfile: Click me, go on, click me if you dare Duowan download page Click me, go on, click me if you dare Author’s blog: http://blog.sina.com.cn/t850 Game description: Dong Dong Never Die Online Official Version Genre: FTG fighting Platform: PC Size: 376M zipped, 930M unzipped Made by: Zhang Qiang, Wang Dong, et al. Release date: August 8, 2009 In 2009, Guangzhou is set to host a “Street Fighter” tournament. On the eve of the finals, a large number of contestants mysteriously disappear, and every clue points to “Bio Man”. “Dong Dong”, a criminal police officer with the Sichuan Provincial Public Security Department, sets off southward. Disguised as a fighter, he vows to uncover the truth of the case. Who exactly is Bio Man? Why have so many contestants gone missing? In 2009 the winds of change blow, and a catastrophe is about to arrive. This battle of Dong Dong’s will change the fate of many people… Work on Dong Dong Never Die Online Official Version began in October 2006 and was finally completed in August 2009 — three years of spare time in total. The game was made by a group of Chinese game enthusiasts, developed with 2DFM. The game features Chinese voice acting throughout (Mandarin plus some regional dialects) and Chinese subtitles throughout. It contains 36 stages, 24 selectable characters and 15 non-selectable characters. The photos collected for the game numbered as many as 18,000, of which roughly 10,000 actually made it into the game. Version notes: ★ Building on the full version bundled with issue 231 of Game Console Practical Techniques, the main menu logo now carries the label “August 8, 2009 Online Official Version”. ★ Fixed a number of bugs; tweaked the stats of some characters; lowered the difficulty of Bio Man and the 1V7 stage; some infinite combos were weakened; Marshmallow gained a new super special move. Cutscene story content was added and revised. ★ Because 2DFM wasn’t optimized well enough, the character select screen lags badly the first time you enter the game; after the game has been running for a while it smooths out. This bug can’t be fixed. ★ The currently unresolved bugs are as follows. If any 2DFM enthusiast has found a solution, please do let me know: 1. Pause the game for more than a few dozen seconds and then resume the fight — there’s a chance a small number of visual effects will disappear, such as shockwaves, hit effects, etc. They return to normal after the round ends. 2. At the moment a super move is triggered, you can’t stop projectiles in flight. ★ The most important update is the bundled Chinese-localized online play program — it supports internet and LAN matches, and supports random stages during local versus play (see “说明_Readme.txt” included with the game).

title: GTA4 Top-Tier Cheat Guide
content: Cheat mode In the game, you can use Niko’s phone to enter the following cheat codes and activate the corresponding cheat functions. Note: don’t save your game after using them, to avoid unforeseen problems. Some cheat codes may affect achievement unlocks. Replenish health Dial “ 3625550100 “ on your phone. Note: this code affects the achievements for “Cleaned The Mean Streets”, “Finish Him”, “One Man Army”, and “Walk Free”. Replenish health and ammo Dial “ 4825550100 “ on your phone. Note: this code affects the achievement for “Cleaned The Mean Streets”. Weapons tier 1 Dial “ 4865550100 “ on your phone. This unlocks the baseball bat, pistol, shotgun, mp5 , M4, sniper rifle, RPG and grenades. Note: this code affects the achievement for “Cleaned The Mean Streets”. Weapons tier 2 Dial “ 4865550150 “ on your phone. This unlocks the knife, Molotov cocktails, pistol, shotgun, Uzi submachine gun, ak47 , sniper rifle, and RPG. Note: this code affects the achievement for “Cleaned The Mean Streets”. Remove wanted level Dial “ 2675550100 “ on your phone. Note: this code affects the achievements for “One Man Army” and “Walk Free”. Increase wanted level by one Dial “ 2675550150 “ on your phone. Get an Annihilator Dial “ 3595550100 “ on your phone. Note: this code affects the achievements for “One Man Army” and “Walk Free”. Get a Cognoscenti Dial “ 2275550142 “ on your phone. Get a Comet Dial “ 2275550175 “ on your phone. Get an FBI Buffalo Dial “ 2275550100 “ on your phone. Get a Jetmax Dial “ 9385550100 “ on your phone. Get an NRG-900 Dial “ 6255550100 “ on your phone. Get a Sanchez Dial “ 6255550150 “ on your phone. Get a SuperGT Dial “ 2275550168 “ on your phone. Get a Turismo Dial “ 2275550147 “ on your phone. Change the weather and brightness Dial “ 4685550100 “ on your phone. Map locations In the game, use a computer at an internet cafe to enter “www.whattheydonotwantyoutoknow.com“, and you’ll get information on all locations (such as where to find weapons, vehicles, leisure spots, etc.). Easy money Go to an ATM, then cause a traffic jam in the area. Wait for someone to withdraw money from the ATM, then kill them. Be sure to block the nearby roads, so that an ambulance can’t get in to rescue anyone. Pick up the money they drop on the ground, then run some distance and come back. The money will respawn on the ground. You can repeat this process. You can also kill more people who are withdrawing money from the ATM to increase your money-farming efficiency. Repair the engine If your vehicle becomes undrivable or the engine won’t start, dial 911 and the engine will restart. content: There’s word on IMDB.com that David Wenham may play Arthas in Sam Raimi’s World of Warcraft movie. Also, the World of Warcraft movie is expected to be finished in 2011. See IMDB.com for details.

title: Changing the height of a Flash Slider component's Skin
content: Based on the design, I found that Flash CS4’s Slider component is too thin — it needs to be thicker, i.e. I have to change the Slider’s height. I checked the API docs, and there’s nothing for setting the SliderTrackSkin’s height. Looks like I’ll have to dig into the UI components myself. Exploration… Result: In Flash CS4, the UI component files are under [X:\**]\Adobe Flash CS4\Common\Configuration\Components, and the source files are under [X:\**]\Adobe Flash CS4\Common\Configuration\Component Source\ActionScript 3.0\User Interface Solution… The plan: write a class that extends Slider and override Slider.configUI() to set the sizes. The thumb is the handle, and the track is the rail. package org.mousebomb.wodewang.control{import fl.controls.Slider; public class MySlider extends Slider { override protected function configUI():void {super.configUI(); thumb.setSize(21, 23); track.setSize(193, 16); }}} Then just bind the Slider in the Flash Library panel to your own class.

title: The trouble with jQuery's window.resize in IE
content: To do size control on a Flash site, you usually need the Flash movie to scale up and down automatically along with the window size. The approach I took: put a container div in place to hold it, with the Flash set to 100% width and height inside. JS listens for browser window resizing and then resets the size of the container div. The Flash side listens for stage changes and moves views to the corresponding positions, etc. The problem showed up in the jQuery window-resize listener. Code: $(document).ready(function(){ WSWFobj(“100%”, “100%”, ‘swfSiteLoader.swf’, [‘allowScriptAccess’], [‘always’], ‘flashContainer’, ‘mainFlash’); confSize();});$(window).resize(function(){alert(‘resize’); confSize();}); function confSize(){ var w $(window).width(); var h $(window).height(); if (w minW) w minW; if (h minH) h minH; $(“#wrap”).width(w); $(“#wrap”).height(h);} var minW 1004;var minH 650;function setMinSize(w, h){ minW w; minH h;} Testing in browsers, I found that IE calls confSize() over and over. The reason: IE fires the window resize event multiple times (instead of once) per actual resize. In practice, for every single resize, IE always fires multiple window.resize events rather than one. An off-the-shelf solution: this jQuery plugin fixes the problem http://plugins.jquery.com/project/wresize(http://plugins.jquery.com/project/wresize) This plugin tries to fix it by introducing a specific method, wresize, which you can use like this: $( selector ).wresize( your_handler )

title: Echoes of War: Echoes of War
content: The game soundtrack Echoes of War: 战争的回响, produced entirely by Australia’s Eminence Symphony Orchestra, collects the full orchestral renditions of music from Blizzard’s blockbusters Warcraft III, World of Warcraft, and Diablo III, and is now available for online order. The idea came from the World of Warcraft tracks previously sold on iTunes, which unexpectedly won the support and purchases of many players. Players said that music is an important form of leisure in many people’s lives, and that being able to buy it openly let them listen to World of Warcraft music on their commute to and from work — until they got home and couldn’t wait to turn on the computer, log into World of Warcraft, and set off on their own epic journey. “We want to bring the music out of the game and into people’s hearts, so they can listen closely — without the clang of swords from conflict, and without the splatter of corpses and ghosts,” says Hiroaki Yura, founder of the Eminence Symphony Orchestra. “We hope to add a lot of our own character to the game music. Because Blizzard’s music is just so classic, we’re being very careful as we go about adding that character,” Hiroaki Yura continued. With the release of Echoes of War: 战争的回响, two versions are now on sale online: the standard edition and the legendary collector’s edition. The standard edition includes not only Diablo (a guitar-arranged version of the theme is included too), StarCraft, StarCraft II, and World of Warcraft: The Burning Crusade, but also tracks from the yet-to-be-released StarCraft II: Trilogy, Diablo III, and World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King. In addition, the legendary collector’s edition comes with an extra DVD featuring behind-the-scenes footage of the making of Echoes of War: 战争的回响, Japanese composer Kow Otani discussing Diablo III, plus a 32-page color booklet and nine exclusive postcards — 15 tracks in total, over 90 minutes of great value. Echoes of War: 战争的回响 went on sale in November 2008, with the standard edition priced at $29.95 and the legendary collector’s edition at $49.95.
