title: The file is clearly there, yet require_once(./*.php) throws an error
content: Problem description:Right after installing PMA, accessing it in Firefox shows a blank page with no output at all. In IE you can see a 500 error (Internal Server Error). Turn on error reporting and you find this: Warning: require_once(.librariescommon.inc.php) [function.require-once]: failed to open stream: No such file or directory in ***\mousebomb\pma\index.php on line 35 Fatal error: require_once() [function.require]: Failed opening required ‘.librariescommon.inc.php’ (include_path’.;C:\php5\pear’) in ***\mousebomb\pma\index.php on line 35 And yet the file really does exist, and IUSR (the IIS anonymous access user) has permission on it. Solution:Fixing the blank page: change the relevant error output settings in php.ini. With the default php.ini, you just need to change display_erroroff to display_erroron. Fixing the require error: any file that require pulls in through a relative path starting with ., you must grant IUSR read permission on the parent directory. This isn’t just about configuring PMA — with any site, under WIMP you have to remember that a file whose path starts with . can only be accessed if its parent directory is readable. Related references:http://hi.baidu.com/ucsec/blog/item/193bc1b6e3ae98fc31add1ab.html Sometimes after installing PHPmyAdmin, accessing it in IE gives you something like this: Warning: require_once(.librariescommon.lib.php): failed to open stream: No such file or directory in ***\index.php on line 40 Fatal error: main(): Failed opening required ‘.librariescommon.lib.php’ (include_path’.;c:\php5\pear’) in ***\index.php on line 40 There are a few reasons this happens: Your PHPmyAdmin directory is sitting in the root of a disk. 2. There’s a permissions problem with your PHPmyAdmin directory and its parent directories. Fix: · Don’t put the PHPmyAdmin directory in the root of a disk — put it somewhere like D:\SiteManage\phpmyadmin · Set the permissions on the PHPmyAdmin directory and its parent directories as follows: Users Read Execute IUSR_…… Read Execute Another fix: －－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－ I hit a strange problem. After installing phpmyadmin, I got this error: Warning: require_once(.librariescommon.lib.php) [function.require-once]: failed to open stream: No such file or directory in X:\Xxxxx\phpmyadmin\index.php on line 36 Fatal error: require_once() [function.require]: Failed opening required ‘.librariescommon.lib.php’ (include_path’.;C:\php5\pear’) in X:\Xxxxx\phpmyadmin\index.php on line 36 I imported the MySQL database into a freshly installed MySQL 5.2, opened the blog home page, and still got a similar error. After a round of debugging I finally found the fix: it came down to insufficient ACL permissions on the parent directories of the phpmyadmin and php install directories, hah! Give phpmyadmin, php, and their parent directories the same read permission for the ACLs user; then open the blog again — done! ^_^ Things to watch out for and security risks: １、Don’t install phpmyadmin in the root directory of a site or virtual host, because then the guest user gets permissions on the root directory. ２、Just grant phpmyadmin read permission for the IIS worker process user and the IIS anonymous user. It’s strongly recommended not to add everyone to the ACL permission list. 3、When debugging a program or setting up a script environment, try reading the FAQ first! Then hunt for the cause in the error output… (for example, with the error above, open line 36 of index.php and see what command the PHP code is executing — the cause of the error becomes obvious) Tips: １、Don’t unzip and install phpmyadmin in the root directory, because then the guest user gets permissions on the root directory. ２、Just grant phpmyadmin permissions for the iis user and the user group. Adding everyone permission is not recommended. －－－－－－－－－ Both approaches above follow the same idea — give them a try.

title: Forgotten by time
content: Though I keep reminding myself, I always quietly forget. What a wondrous thing time is. Traversing the four corners and the heavens and earth In the haze of illusion, I feel you once again — that is a childhood memory, blurred and hard to recall clearly anymore. I miss the muddy roads of childhood, the fresh green scent of the trees along the way, and that park I had to pass through every day, packed on weekends with brothers and sisters at play. I was once caught off guard there and pushed down the tall slide. In my panic, a full three-hundred-sixty-degree spin — as if by divine aid, I landed safely yet was utterly bewildered. Why push me down? A prank, or something more deliberate? Perhaps it was just an accident that froze the instigator stiff. But I seized the opening and yanked hard at that person’s collar. No resistance, no crying. I figured we were even. Years later, thinking back, I feel terribly sorry. I miss the old iron shed downstairs — our secret base back in elementary school. That rundown iron shed became our adventure game. We added a chimney and steps inside, and when we were tired of playing, we’d cook up something tasty. Of course, we ran into another bunch of mischievous little rascals too. We fought hard over that turf. And it was around that time that drawing terrifying skull pictures became my greatest passion. Think you can scare me off? Not a chance. Naive ideas are often quite amusing. In the end the shed’s owner showed up at the “base,” tidying and packing up, probably getting ready to leave. The owner likely knew that our marks of time were in there too. I miss the not-so-big simulated city, with its planes, cannons, warships, and weapons. I had so many friends back then. I made lots of models out of foam and got lost with my companions in a virtual world of illusion. You were the defense minister living in seclusion in the mountains; he was a dashing high-ranking sailor. My dwelling was very mysterious, hidden deep in a vast primeval forest. Magic was nothing special — put plainly, it was just high technology. We soared through the sky and burrowed into the earth, plucking the moon from the ninth heaven, catching turtles in the five oceans, entertaining ourselves and thoroughly pleased with it. I remember a “Mushroom Mall” with outrageously high prices. Two naughty fellows slapped seals on every single one of its storefronts. A whole afternoon gone, never tiring of it. Childhood ideas were fun and thrilling, but all of it is far away now. I feel some reluctance to let go, yet there’s no need to live it all again. Then I got sick again, and couldn’t get out of bed. So during the vibrant, youthful days of middle school, I spent almost all of it at home. From then on I had fewer and fewer friends, and so more and more personal time to stay calm. With nothing to do but think — think about the world, think about life, think about myself. On cold, lonely afternoons, music outside the window would often play. Sunshine always comes after wind and rain; misfortune is what good fortune leans upon. Occasionally I’d go back to school for exams and could feel countless pairs of envious, jealous, and resentful eyes. Later still, I started going online at home, watching Flash, playing games. The colorful world of the internet drew me in deeply. Sitting before the computer, only then did I find the drive for life — as if I was born for this, so in tune. The fire of life was lit again, giving me wisdom and courage. I found my place, and I will walk together with the internet. Middle school ended quickly, leaving regret and remembrance. Carrying my ideals about the internet, I stepped into a brand-new campus, full of delight, ready to meet brilliant senior and fellow students. Yet reality and ideals often differ as much as heaven and earth. A chaotic school culture — not illegal, but still a mess. How many people actually studied with real interest? Disappointment after disappointment struck. It turned out most people couldn’t be trusted, that the general run of them were garbage. Clubs, teachers — all bullshit. Who could solve my problems? Who was willing to talk craft with me? More and more suffocated. In the end, everything comes down to yourself. If others don’t work hard, that’s nothing to do with me. Anger and helplessness were the brands my school years left on me. Thinking back now, I’m truly sorry — what meaning did my inner complaints have? Each has their own path, each their own fate. I’ll be free and easy, roaming the heavens and earth. To everyone who’s left the school gates, I wish you all the best. Twenty years have hurried by. Student days are in the past. Life moves forward; the dream doesn’t die. Let the past be the past — no need to care. The heavens and earth stretch on, I am alone, and through ten thousand rivers and a thousand mountains I walk on my own. What a mysterious thing time is. Everything can be wiped out by time, discarded by it. Later I understood: the me of the past has died. A new me is reborn and returns. I set down the memories of the past, then pick them up again. They are the witness and the mark that I once lived. But I can no longer draw the line between reality and the virtual. A year passes like a day, detached from time, never noticing the silent flow of years. Yesterday is already gone. The future is murky and uncertain. This moment vanishes in an instant. The most beautiful flower blooms in the deepest, most knowing ground. Though I keep reminding myself, I always quietly forget. What a wondrous thing time is. Traversing the four corners and the heavens and earth — and we, all of us, are insignificant, nothing more. - By Mousebomb @ 09.07.27

title: WordPress permalinks under wimp
content: Not long ago I switched from LAMP to WIMP (windows2k3+iis6+mysql5.2+php5.2), and WordPress lost two important features: one is permalinks (static URLs), and the other is email sending. I’ve just perfectly solved the permalink problem, so I’ll share the method. (A so-called permalink is something like http://www.flashj.cn/wp/wimp-wordpress-permalink.html这样的格式) Because Windows doesn’t support .htaccess, to do rewrite you need to download an ISAPI_Rewrite component to implement rewriting. I tried it, and personally I didn’t find the result very ideal. I saw a clever method online for implementing permalinks with a 404 page, and after adapting it, it felt pretty good. The principle is: write a 404.php file that forwards requests to WordPress’s index.php. The version that’s commonly circulated now is: Create a PHP file with the following content: Save as 404.php 2. Put this 404.php file in the WordPress root directory 3. Set IIS’s 404 page to 404.php in the WordPress root directory 4. Enable permalinks in the WordPress admin panel In other words, 404.php acts as a rewrite. However, when implementing it I ran into two problems: 1. Subdirectories Friends who often read my blog should know that my domain is flashj.cn, the landing page is www.flashj.cn, and I actually have two WordPress blog installations, in the www.flashj.cn/wp and www.flashj.cn/personalblog directories, so I can’t directly set the site’s 404 file like friends with standalone sites can. 2. Chinese garbled text Because the IIS6 on Chinese WIN2k3 uses GBK encoding, while WordPress uses UTF-8 encoding, Chinese characters in permalinks make WordPress unable to recognize them. After my “improvements”, I’ve now successfully made them static. Here’s how: Enable support for extensionphp_mbstring.dll in php.ini (it’s usually enabled anyway) Write a 404.php like this I just added Chinese transcoding to the commonly circulated online version, converting IIS’s GBK to the UTF8 that WordPress needs. Put this 404.php file in the wp and personal directories (one in each of the two WordPress directories) In IIS, create applications for the subdirectories: Open IIS Manager, switch to the flashj.cn site, and create applications for the wp and personalblog subdirectories. For example: open the properties of the “sitewp” subdirectory, and in the “Application Settings” area at the bottom of the “Directory” tab, click “Create” application. This way, the subdirectory can now have its own independent error page. Set IIS’s 404 page: Following step 4, switch to the “Custom Errors” tab and set the 404 page. The key here is to change the 404 setting to: message type URL, URL subdirectory-name404.php (mine is wp404.php) Enable permalinks in the WordPress admin panel Leave a comment at the end of this post to say hi and celebrate the success I’ll go continue looking into how to get the email feature working…

title: AS3 digital audio processing library with wav support: StandingWave
content: StandingWave is an AS3 code library designed for high level control of Flash Player 10’s SampleDataEvent API for streaming audio output. It is based on a subset of the audio engine used by the Noteflight Score Editor. The goal of StandingWave is to encapsulate the following kinds of objects, permitting them to be easily chained together and combined to produce complex, dynamic audio output: audio sources (MP3 or WAV files, algorithmic sound generators…) audio filters (echo, envelope shaping, equalization…) timed sequences of audio sources, which may be hierarchically composed For example, the following code snippet plays a synthesized sine wave with a calculated amplitude envelope: var source:IAudioSource = new SineSource(new AudioDescriptor(), duration, freq); source = new EnvelopeFilter(source, attack, decay, sustain, hold, release); new AudioPlayer().play(source); There are no fundamental musical concepts embodied in StandingWave, but it may be straightforwardly extended with such, for instance by reading MIDI files or by writing utility classes to manage tones, scales, instruments, and so forth. Noted: http://code.google.com/p/standingwave/

title: EA announces Command & Conquer 4 arrives in 2010
content: EA recently announced that it will release Command Conquer 4 in 2010, and the game will take players through the finale of the Tiberium War saga. EA really is prolific. We’ll get to see Kane again next year. I’m rooting for Kane, hehe. The story of Command Conquer 4 mostly takes place after Command Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars. It’s 2062, humanity is on the brink of extinction, and Earth has only six years left before it becomes uninhabitable. The two opposing factions, the Global Defense Initiative (GDI) and the Brotherhood of Nod, finally realize they have to stop the spread of Tiberium to keep it from wiping out humanity; Nod’s leader Kane decides to set out for GDI. Just what is Kane planning on enemy territory? Command Conquer 4 will bring this Tiberium world to its final, epic conclusion, and players will at last learn the ultimate fate of Nod, GDI and Earth, and most importantly, the real motivation behind Kane’s long-standing plan. The story of Command Conquer 4 takes place after the events of the critically acclaimed Command Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars™. The year is 2062 and humanity is at the brink of extinction. With only six years left until the mysterious crystalline structure Tiberium renders the earth entirely uninhabitable, the two opposing factions - Global Defense Initiative (GDI) and the Brotherhood of Nod - inevitably find themselves in desperation for the same cause: to stop Tiberium from extinguishing mankind. The unthinkable becomes reality and Nod’s enigmatic leader Kane takes off for GDI headquarters. What is Kane planning in the heart of his enemies’ base? Command Conquer 4 draws the epic conclusion to the beloved Tiberium universe, where fans will learn the fate of Earth, Nod, Tiberium, GDI and most importantly, Kane’s motivations behind his decade-long plan. ——Official Besides bringing the epic GDI and Nod campaigns, playable solo or in co-op, cnc4 will also offer a new 5v5 objective-based multiplayer mode. It fosters team spirit and encourages teamwork. And it delivers a real-time strategy experience built on teamwork and social interaction, the likes of which have never been seen before. In addition to the two campaigns on the epic battles of GDI and Nod, which players will get to conquer alone or in a cooperative mode, Command Conquer 4 will also feature a new 5v5 objective-based multiplayer mode, promoting teamwork and cooperation and delivering a social real-time-strategy experience never seen before in a Command Conquer 4 game. For the full details, see the official site: http://www.commandandconquer.com/cnc4/

title: Chinese Paladin 3 — Immortal Melodies Endure, Time Forgotten
content: It’s been a few days since I finished Chinese Paladin 3, but it still has a hold on me, and I don’t want to let it go. Those moving love stories have ended. All that’s left are scene after scene of vivid memories, image after image of bittersweet beauty. Those stirring background melodies keep lingering in my ears. Click here and let’s listen together: He came out of the tree, following a true love from a past life; he has lived through spring’s passing and autumn’s return himself. Xiyao poured her longing into the immortal fruit and created Xuejian, hoping she would keep Feipeng company in her place. Xuejian carries Xiyao’s dreams and Xiyao’s tenderness — surely she can keep Jingtian company in her place. When Xuejian first met Xiyao, she said that everything she received came in doubles: if there was a share for her, there was a share for Xiyao. Yet later Xuejian actually came out with “I’m going to snatch that blasted Veggie-Tooth back from Xiyao’s hands.” That was truly heartbreaking. Reading that, how I wished Xiyao and Xuejian could become one. Xuejian is Xiyao’s longing — isn’t she already a part of Xiyao? But what about Xiyao herself? She turned into flowers and grass to nourish the immortal tree. All she can do is watch Jingtian and Xuejian keep each other company day and night, and silently wish them well. To her, the Feipeng of old is nothing but a memory now. This love, sealed away in time, never changes. A single memory lasts as long as three lifetimes; in the end, a bowl of water is all it takes to forget it. Changqing and Zixuan — a love across three lifetimes, so long, so true. Hand in hand, together until old age. Each lifetime is a new beginning; each lifetime is more sublime than the last. Time cannot be cut through; it flows back into the past. The changes etched into the bone are not far away. Even ten thousand years from now, this deep feeling will not change; love spreads like a blazing fire. In this life, Changqing’s many years of cultivation and Zixuan’s complete understanding let them make the rational choice for the sake of all living beings, giving up their own romance and turning private love into a greater love. They agreed to drink the water of forgetfulness, to forget each other’s love, forget the time that had passed, and break free of every entanglement. But how could the memories of three lifetimes be wiped away so easily? Even if I give up loving you, let me keep something to remember. Love is so clear, yet we must accept separation; all I have left is the right to miss you. I’m truly sorry — I promised you I would stop loving you, but I never promised myself. And yet how could I truly stop loving you? And finally — Zixuan gets her wish, and snow fills the sky. You and I are strangers now; tears fall in sorrow. Changqing dances with his sword, all alone — the road to Shu is hard. To be apart, I’m not used to it. No matter how you reckon it, it’s too hard. After parting, we are braver. After a thousand years of loneliness you see the sunlight again, yet you turn and leap into the sea of fire, becoming a phoenix. A thousand years of waiting, only to meet her brother once more. Fate was settled long ago: what awaits her is yet another sacrifice to the sword. In the end she lets it go, leaving her brother behind with a heart full of blessings. No longer trapped inside the sword, she begins a new life of her own. Time cannot be cut through; it flows back into the past. The changes etched into the bone are not far away. Even ten thousand years from now, this deep feeling will not change; love spreads like a blazing fire. May this love be passed down through the generations. From then on — Feipeng becomes an ancient myth, Xiyao turns into beautiful flowers, Longkui enters the black-and-white cycle of reincarnation. The world returns to the right path, and Jingtian and Xuejian, two people fated for each other, are finally united. They had Maomao and Biping quietly supporting them, a thousand years of memories, and an undying blessing. Those familiar smiling faces will be engraved in their hearts forever. They have Yong’an Pawnshop, they have Tangjia Fort, and at this moment, they also have — each other. To save the people killed by the Evil Sword Immortal, Jingtian agreed to give the Heavenly Emperor his own time in exchange for everyone’s lives. So Jingtian doesn’t have much time left, does he? Hey, who cares. They love each other, forever and ever, and time is nothing to be afraid of. Snow falls thick and heavy, exactly as it did when Xuejian fell into the mortal world… -———————– TV series OST download (eMule): Soundtrack Album - “Chinese Paladin 3 · TV Original Soundtrack” [MP3] Soundtrack Album - “Chinese Paladin 3 TV Original Soundtrack” [APE]

title: html5: The Rising Star of the Rich Internet
content: HTML 5 is the next generation of the Hypertext Markup Language. Since HTML 4 was released in 1997, HTML development had been at a standstill, while the Web has advanced by leaps and bounds in recent years — so much so that HTML 4 can no longer keep up with today’s increasingly “rich” Web applications. HTML 5 not only addresses HTML 4’s functional shortcomings for Web applications, it also aims to improve HTML’s interactive capabilities and support today’s diverse, complex Web content. Exciting features:1. New tags that describe content semantically Take a look at two examples from IBM: the source code of a typical blog today might look like this: Mokka mit Schlag Mokka mit SchlagSpring Comes (and Goes) in Sussex CountyYesterday I joined the Brooklyn Bird Club for our annual trip to Western New Jersey, specifically Hyper Humus, a relatively recently discovered hot spot. It started out as a nice winter morning when we arrived at the site at 7:30 A.M., progressed to Spring around 10:00 A.M., and reached early summer by 10:15. But does it count for your life list?Seems you can now go [bird watching via the Internet](http://www.wired.com/science/discoveries/news/ 200704cone_sf). I haven’t been able to test it out yet (20 user limit apparently) but this is certainly cool. Personally, I can’t imagine it replacing actually being out in the field by any small amount. On the other hand, I’ve always found it quite sad to meet senior birders who are no longer able to hold binoculars steady or get to the park. I can imagine this might be of some interest to them. At least one elderly birder did a big year on TV, after he could no longer get out so much. This certainly tops that. « Previous Entries Info Comment Policy Todo List Archives April 2007 March 2007 February 2007 January 2007 Copyright 2007 Elliotte Rusty Harold Even with proper indentation, this is still a rather messy collection of deeply nested divs. In HTML 5, you can replace them with elements that carry direct semantics, as in the example below: Mokka mit Schlag Mokka mit SchlagSpring Comes (and Goes) in Sussex CountyYesterday I joined the Brooklyn Bird Club for our annual trip to Western New Jersey, specifically Hyper Humus, a relatively recently discovered hot spot. It started out as a nice winter morning when we arrived at the site at 7:30 A.M., progressed to Spring around 10:00 A.M., and reached early summer by 10:15. But does it count for your life list?Seems you can now go [bird watching via the Internet](http://www.wired.com/science/discoveries/news/ 200704cone_sf). I haven’t been able to test it out yet (20 user limit apparently) but this is certainly cool. Personally, I can’t imagine it replacing actually being out in the field by any small amount. On the other hand, I’ve always found it quite sad to meet senior birders who are no longer able to hold binoculars steady or get to the park. I can imagine this might be of some interest to them. At least one elderly birder did a big year on TV, after he could no longer get out so much. This certainly tops that. « Previous Entries Info Comment Policy Todo List Archives April 2007 March 2007 February 2007 January 2007 Copyright 2007 Elliotte Rusty Harold That way, the browser knows what each part of a page represents — for example, which part is navigation and which part is the main content. Beyond cleaner code and semantic tags, this change brings more benefits: search engines can more accurately tell which part of a page matters most, and it will also render better on the non-standard browsers used on phones and other devices. 2. Improved Web form handlingHTML 5 introduces Web Forms 2.0, giving developers many new options and new features for handling form input and submission more simply and efficiently. The most exciting feature of Web Forms 2.0 is input validation. Today we have to implement the same functionality through JavaScript or server-side logic. Take, for example, a form like the one below: In HTML 4 we would have to write code like this, then validate it with JavaScript or a server-side script: In HTML 5, the required and email attributes handle validation directly, like this: 3. Providing APIs for Web developmentHTML 5 will provide several APIs that can do what many plugins do today. Audio and video playback support: Audio and video tags, for instance, let developers play Web video and audio directly without third-party tools — which means users can toss a lot of plugins and keep their browsers cleaner: Download this video Download this song Today, the Opera browser already supports the video tag. Vector graphics support: The tag will let you draw directly on it with scripts. People absorb information from images more easily; for example, the same information below looks noticeably different when shown as a table versus a pie chart: In the past, though, achieving this effect meant using static images that couldn’t be adjusted. With the tag, you can tweak parameters and redraw the graphic in real time — generating a pie chart on the fly from user votes, for instance.In HTML 5, 2D drawing technologies like Canvas have long been a priority for companies such as Apple, Google, and Mozilla (though Microsoft, while it praises some HTML 5 features, still doesn’t support Canvas to this day) 4. Editable portions of a web pageHTML 5 will support user interaction. The contenteditable attribute lets you decide which part of a page can be edited — very practical for wiki-style sites that anyone can contribute to. 5. Local storageLocal storage lets users keep using the Web while offline. Support for some HTML 5 features:After five years of work, the HTML 5 specification was released in 2008, and parts of it are already implemented in some browsers. Still, the full feature set of HTML 5 won’t be finished for several years. At the Google IO developer conference, Google Engineering Vice President Vic Gundotra expressed the company’s commitment to the next generation of HTML, HTML 5. Although HTML 5 is still a draft and the W3C committee is still engaged in lengthy discussions about it, HTML 5 is already being widely implemented — whether as an experimental demo or as the core of certain Web applications. Vlad Vukicevic, technical lead on the Mozilla Firefox project, says HTML 5 supports video, Firefox 3.5 has just added video support, Google Chrome also supports the video tag, and Microsoft supports certain HTML 5 features in Internet Explorer 8, such as local storage, AJAX navigation, and several DOM prototypes. Molly E. Holzschlag, Web evangelist at Opera, says Opera supports Canvas and plans to support video. Apple, too, supports video and audio tags plus Canvas technology in its Safari browser (Canvas was invented by Apple). Will HTML 5 defeat RIA technologies like Flash and Silverlight?Ian Hickson, co-designer of the HTML 5 specification, says the goal of HTML 5 is to free the Web from those closed rich-media plugins — they come from independent vendors and don’t belong on the open Web. Hickson says using a single company’s products is a risk for the open Web: what if they stop development, or start charging? Hickson adds that, as with Windows in the past, it would be frightening if our main development platform were controlled by a single vendor. Vukicevic, who leads Firefox, says Mozilla wants to stay open and ensure that technologies like video aren’t controlled by a handful of companies, but whether HTML 5 and Canvas ultimately replace Flash, Silverlight, and JavaFX is up to developers. Vukicevic thinks IE8’s lack of support for some HTML 5 features is a problem for developers: given IE’s market share, developers either have to use Microsoft’s APIs for extra work or fall back on technologies like Flash. The plugin side: they’re better, and they’re already implemented Although Adobe, Microsoft, and Sun all took part in drafting the HTML 5 specification, they all say their own technologies are necessary. HTML 5 is still a standard in progress and may take five to ten years to be finalized, so it’s too early to make comparisons. A Microsoft spokesperson says Silverlight still needs to exist because it includes advanced features such as a better programming model, C#, 3D capabilities, and the ability to run outside the browser. Dave Story, Adobe’s vice president of developer tools, says HTML 5 faces many challenges: the browser market is still fragmented, compatibility problems between browsers are severe, and the HTML 5 timeline suggests HTML 5 + CSS 3 may take ten years to be finalized. In the meantime, Flash will keep evolving and delivering a better user experience. Sun vice president James Gosling, widely known as the father of Java, says JavaFX is far superior to HTML 5 in rendering, performance, and presentation. Analyst Cote says these rich Web plugins face no immediate threat — it will be many years before their features are achieved — and he hopes these plugin technologies will continue to exist even after HTML 5 ships. Google’s Fette agrees: HTML 5 is just a starting point, and companies like Google will keep rolling out their own technologies, such as dragging and dropping images onto the Web. Several industry giants will face tough choices Most of the companies involved in HTML 5 are either browser vendors or rich Web application tool developers — rarely both, with Microsoft being the exception. Almaer says this puts Microsoft in a bind: it has invested heavily in Silverlight, and the Silverlight team exists to enhance the browser. If HTML 5 does that easily, what’s the point of Silverlight? Google, too, will have to make some choices. Its YouTube uses Flash for video, and HTML 5’s video support will force it to revisit the question, weighing cost against benefit. To a developer like me, HTML 5 is essentially about adapting to today’s Web 2.0 by pushing higher-level technology down a layer, so that “rich” applications are supported directly by the browser. At most it replaces Ajax and some closed plugins. But I don’t think it will have much impact on Flash. The Flash family is an interesting one: people use it for animation, for websites, for desktop apps, and for browser-plugin-based web apps, and so on. Adobe is in the imaging business to begin with — however excellent HTML 5 may be, you’re not going to make animations with it, are you? If there is any impact, it will be on the web app and desktop app side — and after all, Flash started out as just an animation tool. Wouldn’t it be better if HTML 5 considered letting SWF files play directly without Flash Player? Let’s get one thing straight: Flash and HTML 5 will be complementary, not adversaries!

title: Life Online — yet another web-based version of The Sims
content: The new Battle.net for World of Warcraft still hasn’t shown any sign of life today, so let’s try a few new games instead. Remember playing The Sims years ago? That cookie-cutter AI really wasn’t much fun at all, and I got bored of it fast. If an online version of The Sims ever came out, I’d be rolling up my sleeves and would definitely have to give it a go. And what do you know — Yangbo Network recently put out a 3D online life-simulation game: Life Online! Life OL is China’s first 3D management-simulation online game. While doing its best to keep the essence of The Sims, it also brings in a whole range of online game elements. Life OL doesn’t simply move The Sims onto the internet; in some details it even goes further than The Sims. What’s even more of a pleasant surprise for veteran Sims players is that Life OL delivers true DIY: from your avatar to the exterior of your house to the interior decoration, whatever you want your house to look like is entirely up to you! In Life OL, there’s no longer the endless killing, grinding and PK of traditional MMORPGs. Instead, it takes the mechanics of single-player management-simulation games as its foundation and adds the popular community-interaction model, building a lifelike online life whose core gameplay is planting, raising livestock, running a business and socializing. It pioneers a user homestead system: starting from a small house, and later, as the user’s wealth accumulates, gradually growing into a highly show-off-worthy personal estate, villa or castle! In the game, users can live all kinds of different lives, fulfill their life’s dreams, and experience all sorts of pleasures that reality can’t give them. This June, the single-player classic The Sims 3 and the Life OL pioneer test shine side by side — this June is bound to be a joyous celebration for every Sims fan! Life OL official site: www.hi365.com Life OL official forum: bbs.hi365.com Testing only just started this month, and the test activation code giveaway officially kicked off on June 5! Take a look at the game’s full world map — hehe, isn’t that a map of China? I’ve downloaded the client, and now I’m off to grab an activation code as fast as I can…

title: World of Warcraft's server shutdown and the "Professor Sheep" career crisis
content: World of Warcraft going offline triggers a “Professor Sheep” career crisis: (Couldn’t find the original author — if you know who it is, please speak up) Click the images below to view them full size A few days ago I came across an article, “American Education Expert Suggests Using World of Warcraft to Teach,” which mentioned that Lucas Gillespie of EduRealms founded “WoWinSchool,” a site dedicated to teaching teachers how to use World of Warcraft in the classroom. Founder Lucas Gillespie says students who are at risk of dropping out aren’t failing because they lack the ability to learn, but because they find the coursework boring and irrelevant. “Math is boring and reading articles is just as tedious for them, because they feel these things have nothing to do with them. They don’t write at school because they feel their own feelings can’t go into an essay. Usually, these students just need a catalyst, a source of inspiration, so they can focus on reading, writing, and doing arithmetic. Most kids today play virtual social networks and online games. So using online games like World of Warcraft can serve as a great jumping-off point for all kinds of coursework.” And then look at “Professor Sheep,” who’s now the target of everyone’s outrage online — what a stark, ironic contrast. Shouldn’t Professor Sheep grab Lucas Gillespie and give him a few zaps? While I’m at it, a big thumbs-down to certain bad actors. One parent said: “The music in the game makes me feel like I’ve walked into a demon’s maze. My heart kept pounding, and I had no choice but to take some heart medication just to get through it.” Why is it only your heart that pounds? Why do so many people in China feel calm and happy when they hear this powerful music? Is there something wrong with your ears? I’ve heard WoW’s background music in plenty of CCTV programs. Let’s set aside for now the fact that CCTV used someone else’s composition without permission — but when CCTV played that track back then, how come it never realized it would make people feel like they’d walked into a demon’s maze? — Reflections on CCTV’s 《战网魔》 Some shameless organization — I’ve heard illegally pirated music in plenty of programs too, including game music and TV show music: World of Warcraft, Red Alert 3, The X-Files, and so on. So that author’s words really struck a chord with me. “Professor Sheep” made his name off World of Warcraft, and now mainland WoW’s servers are down. Go do whatever you’re supposed to be doing, or it’ll really turn out like the cartoon describes.

title: Plants vs. Zombies
content: Having gotten bored of every other game, and with WoW’s Chinese servers temporarily gone, I was bored out of my mind. Into this gap stepped Plants vs. Zombies — a plain but adorable, simple but fun single-player game — and it was a real eye-opener. The art is just so kawaii. At its core this game is a plant TD — a horde of terrifying zombies crawling out of nearby graveyards intends to take over your house and eat your brains. Oh yeah, eat… eat brains. To fight off these undead, the defending side — that is, the player — can plant all sorts of cute yet powerful plants outside the house to resist the invasion. The classic plants include: Sunflower: produces sunlight, which you use to plant more plants; Wall-nut: a frontline tank with high defense and no attack; Cherry Bomb: a one-time self-destruct with area damage, hoho, very handy in emergencies, and later on you get the Jalapeno; Peashooter: cheap damage output; Chomper: swallows a zombie one square ahead in one bite, but then needs a while to digest… Depending on the time and the battle location, there are more and more battle conditions, making it increasingly difficult. Night and day determine which plants are active — at night there’s no natural sunlight. The pond in the backyard requires you to plant Lily Pads before you can put land plants there. At night the pond can also fog up or rain, and sometimes the sky goes completely dark so you can only see the battlefield by lightning flashes. The sloped terrain of the roof requires a Peashooter catapult to hit enemies up high, and so on. Besides combat, the game also has money-making and development elements, plus extra minigames. Later on the game unlocks a lot of puzzle games and minigames; playing the minigames earns you more coins, and coins buy items. Common items include extra seed slots — which increase the variety of plants you can bring into each battle — and upgraded versions of various plants. These items all improve your odds in battle. Haha. The most important thing is that this game’s characters are adorable — even the scary-looking zombies are comical. Some of the game’s story bits are hilarious too, like the guy who sells you goods being a lunatic; and the zombies will even pretend to be your mom writing you a letter telling you to open the door, and so on. After you kill the Boss in the main storyline, all the plants and zombies even throw a party together at your house and sing a song in chorus. Play this game in your spare time and you definitely won’t be disappointed. title: World of Warcraft Rebirth Log [Updated 7.30]
content: I’ve been playing WoW since the open beta, and after the 9C servers started having frequent, mysterious and unstoppable energy fluctuations that made the game really unpleasant to play, I gradually went AFK. After TBC launched, I went back in and played casually for quite a while, but in the end I left again. I once thought WoW could no longer tempt me, but now that I’ve lost WOW, I feel an unprecedented sense of powerlessness — like the Kaldorei Moon Guard losing the source of the Well of Eternity. At the end of the battle a while back, Netwing and 9 Village channeled the magic that the nobles had used so carefully into chaos. On June 7, the unstable vortex deep in the lake waters exploded catastrophically, and a huge chain of shockwaves tore the world apart — wreaking enormous devastation on Kalimdor and on all living beings of the world of Warcraft: the servers went down! The explosion shredded the surface of the land and polluted the skies. The shockwaves shook the very bones of the world, and seawater filled the wounds in the earth. 80% of the continent of Kalimdor was ripped open, forming scattered continents centered on the newly created sea. At the center of that sea — where the waters of eternity once were — churned a force of rage and chaos. This terrifying scar, known as the Maelstrom, records that chapter of history… Four years of an ideal world, gone for good. Now countless beings yearn for the Well of Eternity. “Give me some bread, give me some water — oh, just give me some damn magic…” Longing for the source of magic, longing for rebirth. Fortunately, someone saved the water of the Well of Eternity before the great explosion — as the fighting inside and outside the temple escalated, the Blizzard folks appeared at the edge of the spring. They knelt by the spring, filled a magic bottle of their own making with the water that shimmered with energy, and captured a snapshot of this world at the very last moment. Thinking that the demons would destroy the whole civilization of World of Warcraft, they decided to stockpile this holy water for later use in restoring the world. It wasn’t until I lost WOW that I wanted to go back and play properly again, and I’m now actively preparing to set foot in World of Warcraft once more. HOHO. To welcome the rebirth to come, I’ve been recording the process of this rebirth: — 6.7 The great explosion — the servers went down; the official site was flooded with sorrowful memoirs 6.8 Reminiscing about World of Warcraft, downloaded CampaignsCN.exe from the internet, and played through the Warcraft III campaigns properly once more 6.10 Took out the War of the Ancients trilogy I hadn’t finished before and kept reading 6.12 NetEase’s brand-new Battle.net account system for WOW 6.13 Planning my gear, playstyle and so on for after the rebirth 6.14 Heard a rumor that World of Warcraft opens on the 23rd and that NetEase has obtained the complete player data: After verification, the player data from before the servers went down at midnight on June 6 has been confirmed as retained (meaning it was checked for both human tampering and accidents). The next time you log in, things will be exactly as they were when you logged off. Blizzard China’s general manager and the NetEase crew worked overtime to get the data transfer and server setup done. To boost morale, in the manner of Mei Lanfang: until WoW goes live, no male employee shaves. The currently confirmed launch time is the 23rd.The player data NetEase obtained this time will include all of every player’s virtual items in World of Warcraft. When players log in, they will see themselves exactly as they were when they logged off in the old World of Warcraft. (Not to be trusted, but having hope is always nice)… 6.18 Game-card rumor: the new version of the World of Warcraft game card can be used starting on the 19th; the rumor mill speculates that Battle.net will be usable on the 19th 6.19 The rumor that Battle.net opens today also turned out to be false 6.20 NetEase hasn’t surfaced at all since 6.12. Players are getting anxious, and plenty of forum posts are venting frustration. 6.23 The legendary news of a launch on the 23rd also turned out to be false. I downloaded the Taiwan server’s WLK. 6.24 Finally, some official news: Latest Bulletin on Hardware Installation and Data StatusDear players: Today we would like to brief everyone on the latest developments in the World of Warcraft transition. Over the past few weeks we have made smooth progress in a number of key areas, and we recently reached an important milestone. Thanks to the tireless, round-the-clock efforts and close cooperation of the engineers at NetEase and Blizzard Entertainment, our brand-new hardware infrastructure has been 100% installed. Configuration and testing of the new facilities are also now proceeding in an orderly manner. We wanted to share this good news with you now, and to have you witness this important moment together with us. We also have the latest news for you regarding the game and player data, which we know you have all been eagerly awaiting. We have safely received the final data snapshot at the moment the servers went offline, and we are now doing everything we can to test and analyze the data to ensure its integrity. The preliminary test results look good. We hope that when players return to World of Warcraft, they can start playing immediately from the state they were in before the shutdown. However, World of Warcraft is a highly complex game, involving a massive amount of account information, character details and data across multiple servers (including the auction house, quests and more), so there is still a great deal of analysis and preparation to do before the final answer is revealed. Our top priority is to ensure that players get the best possible experience when they return to World of Warcraft. As we complete the key steps of the transition period, we sincerely thank you for your continued patience. Once again, thank you to all players for your boundless enthusiasm and long-term support. We look forward to your “return of the heroes.” Please stay tuned to the official transition website for the latest progress during the transition period. The World of Warcraft Transition Team June 24, 2009 Basically the effect of looking at plums to quench your thirst… we still have to wait 6.30 Since the official announcement on the 24th — that thirst-quenching yet meaningful notice — discussion among industry folks and players has only grown more heated. The impatience is understandable, but there’s nothing to be done about it. I’m sure NetEase is even more anxious than we are and will do its utmost to resolve this as soon as possible. With WoW on holiday during this period, why not brush up on the history and the storyline? According to related news reports, the approval process for NetEase’s World of Warcraft has already been suspended, or at least there has been no response. It looks like The9’s lawsuit really has had some effect. Under China’s Provisions on the Administration of the Publication of Electronic Publications, the process for an operator seeking to submit an imported game-type electronic publication for review is to first submit an application to the local press and publication bureau, and after approval is granted, for the local copyright bureau to report it up to the General Administration of Press and Publication. As for NetEase’s filing for World of Warcraft specifically, the public reply from the Beijing Municipal Press and Publication Bureau was that NetEase’s application was approved on June 8 and submitted to the General Administration of Press and Publication. Article 26 of the Provisions on the Administration of the Publication of Electronic Publications states that, within 20 days of accepting an application to publish an electronic publication authorized by a foreign copyright holder, the General Administration of Press and Publication shall make a decision to approve or not to approve; if it does not approve, it shall state the reasons. “If we count from June 8, when the Beijing Municipal Press and Publication Bureau reported it to the General Administration of Press and Publication, then the 29th will be the deadline for the General Administration of Press and Publication to give its reply,” said a person familiar with the matter. “Whether it approves or not, the General Administration of Press and Publication will give a clear answer. But there are now signs that the approval of World of Warcraft has been suspended, so there is no such thing as approval or non-approval.” 7.2, early morning Battle.net registration is open, and you can bind your account! 7.13 News from July 13: according to people familiar with the matter, the General Administration of Press and Publication recently instructed the Shanghai Municipal Press and Publication Bureau to conduct an in-depth investigation into matters relating to the joint venture set up by US-based Blizzard Entertainment and NetEase to operate games. If it is true that the joint venture operates games, then NetEase and Blizzard will be penalized for violating relevant domestic regulations. Under Chinese regulations, foreign companies may not operate online games in China, whether through a wholly-owned entity or a joint venture. Since April 16 this year, when Blizzard and NetEase jointly announced that the operating rights to World of Warcraft in mainland China would be transferred to NetEase after the contract between Blizzard and The9 expired, there has been much industry speculation about how NetEase obtained the right to operate this “world’s number one” online game in China. Two of the most closely watched points: first, NetEase paid a sky-high revenue-share amount, increasing Blizzard’s income fourfold compared with its partnership with The9; second, Blizzard and NetEase set up a joint venture that, under the name of technical support, actually operates World of Warcraft and other games. Especially recently, media analysis of the relevant information disclosed in NetEase’s 2008 annual report (Form 20-F) drew the attention of the industry and the relevant regulatory authorities. In response, NetEase spokespeople have repeatedly stressed in the media that World of Warcraft is operated by Shanghai Wangzhiyi, and that the Blizzard-NetEase joint venture (StormNet, which the media tentatively translate as “Baowang”) only provides “technical support such as anti-cheating, anti-account-theft and anti-private-server measures,” and has not broken any rules. However, according to an analysis by someone familiar with Nasdaq financial reporting principles, based on the information disclosed so far, the joint venture set up by NetEase and Blizzard should play more than just a “technical support” role. The analyst said that NetEase’s Form 20-F mentions that the joint venture’s revenue will be consolidated into NetEase’s reported revenue. If this company only provides technical support such as anti-cheating, anti-account-theft and anti-private-server measures to Shanghai Wangzhiyi, then its revenue is simply Wangzhiyi’s expenses, and consolidating that into NetEase’s overall financial statements would create a double accounting problem and would not be reasonable; even if the joint venture provides “technical support” to other companies in the industry besides NetEase, based on what we can see now, the revenue it could plausibly generate should not be of a magnitude that warrants consolidation into the financial statements. In addition, NetEase’s repeated emphasis that Baowang only provides “technical support” is a change of wording that came only after the media and the public began paying attention to this matter recently. Back on August 13 last year, when NetEase and Blizzard jointly announced the signing of contracts for Warcraft, StarCraft and Battle.net and the simultaneous establishment of a joint venture, the English announcement at the time said the joint venture was for “operational support,” while the Chinese announcement said the joint venture was for “technical support.” It is reported that the government department responsible for investigating this case has already obtained a large amount of relevant information. According to relevant sources, because the media and players have recently paid a great deal of attention to the transfer of World of Warcraft’s operating rights, and because this concerns the key question of whether a joint venture may operate games in China, the state** recently specially assigned the Shanghai Municipal Press and Publication Bureau to investigate the matter in depth. Industry analysts point out that, because it involves major laws, regulations and policy issues, the approval of World of Warcraft is very likely to be suspended until the outcome of this investigation is clear. —— http://forum.games.sina.com.cn/index.php?topic=755396.0 If this news is true… 7.21 Sina Tech news, the morning of July 21: according to public information on the Ministry of Culture’s website, the online game World of Warcraft has passed the Ministry of Culture’s content approval stage, with the filing number “文网进字[2009]006号”. The online game content review system on the Ministry of Culture’s website shows that World of Warcraft, operated by Shanghai Wangzhiyi Network Technology Development Co., Ltd., has passed the Ministry of Culture’s content approval, with the filing number “文网进字[2009]006号”. 7.30 NetEase’s World of Warcraft closed beta begins We are happy to inform all players that World of Warcraft has now officially begun its closed beta! The closed beta period is currently planned to last up to one week. During this time, existing World of Warcraft players can log in to all servers and play for free, helping us test our brand-new hardware infrastructure before we receive government approval for formal operation of the game. Players taking part in this closed beta must create a Battle.net account and bind their World of Warcraft account before they can start playing. Players who have not yet created a Battle.net account and bound their account should visit https://www.battlenet.com.cn as soon as possible to create and bind one. In addition, players must upgrade their client to version 3.1.3 so that they can play on the new hardware infrastructure — please refer to our earlier notice for details. Please note that players cannot create new accounts during the closed beta. We will open new account creation once the game goes into formal operation. Since this is a closed beta, one of our goals is to keep optimizing the hardware and ensure that players get the best possible experience once the game is in formal operation. Please be aware that during the free closed beta, players may run into issues related to stability, connectivity and other performance matters. In addition, there may be unplanned downtime andor extended unplanned downtime at various points during the closed beta. Once we receive the relevant government approval, we will announce the official launch time of the game on the official website www.warcraftchina.com. We hope you enjoy the game now that the closed beta has begun, and thank you for your continued support of World of Warcraft. The World of Warcraft Operations Team, July 30, 2009

title: NetEase's brand-new Battle.net pass system for WoW
content: Just saw the news on the WoW transition site — NetEase is about to roll out a brand-new Battle.net account system in mainland China: “With a single, unified Battle.net account, you’ll no longer be limited by region — you can log in and play on any World of Warcraft server in mainland China, and any game time you purchase will be valid across all World of Warcraft servers, with no need for extra activation verification.” That’s genuinely exciting. It makes me wonder: will the StarCraft II Battle.net down the road share this same Battle.net account? Here’s the full text of NetEase’s announcement: An Introduction to the World of Warcraft Battle.net Account Dear players: You’ve all been following the new account system closely, and wondering how you’ll log in to World of Warcraft once it comes back online. Today we’re happy to tell you: to make it easier for everyone to manage their World of Warcraft game and enjoy a better experience, we’re rolling out a brand-new Battle.net account system in mainland China. With a single, unified Battle.net account, you’ll no longer be limited by region — you can log in and play on any World of Warcraft server in mainland China, and any game time you purchase will be valid across all World of Warcraft servers, with no need for extra activation verification. Work on creating China Battle.net accounts and linking World of Warcraft accounts has not started yet, but we will make sure players can create their own Battle.net account before the servers reopen. We’ll update you with more information as soon as possible, so keep an eye on the World of Warcraft transition site (http://wow.163.com). Below is a walkthrough of creating a Battle.net account and linking your World of Warcraft account: Step 1: Create a Battle.net account Log in to the official Battle.net China website (launching soon) to create a Battle.net account. You’ll need a regularly used, valid email address to serve as your username. Step 2: Verify your email address A verification email will be sent to the email address you registered with. You’ll need to click the link in that email to verify your address. Step 3: Link your World of Warcraft account to the new Battle.net account Enter your previous World of Warcraft account and password, and link them all to your new Battle.net account — no matter which region your previous characters were on. Going forward, World of Warcraft will not require region activation verification. Once the servers reopen, you can use your unified Battle.net account to log in to World of Warcraft and play. We hope to keep sharing more information with you throughout the transition via the transition site and temporary forums. The address of the World of Warcraft temporary forum is http://wowbbs.163.com. The World of Warcraft Transition Team June 12, 2009

title: The Mystery of Teldrassil's Location
content: Warcraft Chronicle: In the explosion of the Well of Eternity over 10,000 years ago, Mount Hyjal in Kalimdor survived, and Illidan released the waters of the Well of Eternity into the lake at the mountain’s summit, turning it into a new Well of Eternity. Later, the red dragon planted an acorn from an oak tree in the new Well of Eternity, and it grew into Teldrassil_ the Crown of the World. Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos: The map shows the World Tree standing in the new Well of Eternity atop Mount Hyjal. But in WoW, Teldrassil, where the night elves live, is in the Great Sea. Why? Answer found: I really was ignorant. Nordrassil and Teldrassil are two different trees. The one at the original Well of Eternity is Nordrassil — the Crown of the Heavens. Teldrassil is Darnassian, meaning Crown of the Earth — it isn’t the tree on Mount Hyjal.

title: Goodbye, World of Warcraft
content: “It has been 4 years since The9 and Blizzard fought shoulder to shoulder, together resisting the invasion of countless online games. Though they succeeded in pocketing endless cash from players, the fragile agreement between The9 and Blizzard has long since vanished into nothing. Now, the war drums thunder once again…” April 26, 2005 — I’ll always remember that day. Lao Niu and I queued like madmen at an internet cafe just to register a World of Warcraft open beta account. That year I was taking an authware course at school, and I even turned out a project that the teachers later used as a student showcase — a World of Warcraft-themed one. World of Warcraft, a deeply admired online game, a flawless worldview, spotless balance, a whole pile of innovative gameplay… Nostalgia So many of those childhood firsts in the game are things you never forget for the rest of your life. The first time I arrived at the night elf capital and saw the majestic Ancients of War and the other patrolling guardians from Warcraft; the first time I arrived at Stormwind City and felt the masterful craft of human stonemasons and the cozy scenery of the canal city; the first time I ran a dungeon and experienced that innovative design; the first time I saw players of other races! The first time doing world PvP! … Those thrills are carved into my heart, and they’re still rippling today. The Battle for the Agency Rights It’s really ironic, when you think about it — that opening line everyone knows by heart turned out to foreshadow their ending: “It has been 4 years since The9 and Blizzard fought shoulder to shoulder, together resisting the invasion of countless online games. Though they succeeded in pocketing endless cash from players, the fragile agreement between The9 and Blizzard has long since vanished into nothing. Now, the war drums thunder once again…” Fine, then I want to know: what else does that “10 years” at the opening of the first World of Warcraft foreshadow? Infernal Affairs 4 – The Warcraft War video: Infernal Affairs 4_The Warcraft War original soundtrack album: “Warcraft Infernal Affairs” Lyrics Theme song: Warcraft Infernal Affairs Lyric adaptation: 不是坏人 Performed by: 伟伟爱绿茶 机枪哥哥 Post-production: 机枪哥哥 Open — why did you forget to open? If you won’t open it, I’ll open it — the Wrath of the Lich King Look at me, the footsteps about to stop, the burning journey about to end Who can find the Infernal kingdom? Who knows how muddled Blizzard is Who understands just how cruel the Warcraft war is, it’s just that no one is willing to admit defeat The9, having lost WoW, how is it supposed to change? Layoffs or going under aren’t far off NetEase, holding the Lich King, how does it make money? A tomorrow that needs no explanation A chaotic world, no end in sight, on this Warcraft Infernal Path Who can find the Infernal kingdom? Who knows how muddled Blizzard is Who understands just how cruel the Warcraft war is, it’s just that no one is willing to admit defeat The9, having lost WoW, how is it supposed to change? Layoffs or going under aren’t far off NetEase, holding the Lich King, how does it make money? A tomorrow that needs no explanation A chaotic world, no end in sight, on this Warcraft Infernal Path Along the way we put on a show of wise oblivion Along the way we look back in rare numbness On this path where we’re inseparably close Let me be like you You like me Never lonely The9, having lost WoW, how is it supposed to change? Layoffs or going under aren’t far off NetEase, holding the Lich King, how does it make money? A tomorrow that needs no explanation Since there’s no end, back to the starting point, back to Warcraft’s In~Infernal Path Why say goodbye to World of Warcraft instead of goodbye to The9? A while back I came across an article: http://www.loveyuki.com/Article/Bad-The9City.aspx The cause of action I marked in yellow is the key point — a commercial defamation dispute counts as an intellectual property dispute. Kou Xiaowei, deputy director of the Audio-Visual, Electronic and Online Publishing Administration Department of the General Administration of Press and Publication, said at the 2007 China Game Industry Annual Conference that when a Chinese online game company gets into an intellectual property dispute with a foreign company, once the foreign company is hit with a lawsuit or arbitration by the Chinese company, its products will immediately be halted from import approval. And everyone knows that after Warcraft changes operators it has to be re-approved before it can go online, so The9’s sinister intentions are glaringly obvious. Back when it was Audition, The9 screwed over 9you; now NetEase has screwed over The9. First they leaked an internal letter to play the victim, then found that players weren’t buying it — everyone seemed delighted that Warcraft was changing operators. And so, along came a vicious move. As for how that move ultimately plays out, right now you really can’t see a clear outcome. But The9 can disappear from here on out. Anyone who plays another game published by The9 has something wrong with their head. If Blizzard’s products really are stopped from being imported, that’s still rather worrying. (There’s already related news saying it won’t be that serious.) Playing WOW is actually pretty painful… If you ask me, this life — in the blink of an eye, you’ve leveled up 10-odd levels; sob~ Then you log off, and this whole life is over… sob~ After switching servers, all your old character data and playtime are kept, plus you get a free pet and an achievement.

title: Deserts Chang - City Download Share
content: After the release of her second album Dear… I Still Don’t Know, Deserts Chang brought in her bandmates Algae, and the four of them buried themselves in the studio and the recording room for eight straight months. After grinding through that long production period, Deserts Chang’s third all-original album, City, finally hit shelves everywhere on May 22. Unlike her first two albums, this time Deserts Chang tried her hand at “thematic songwriting” for the first time! She settled on the album title City first, then gathered tracks around that theme — ten songs, each expressing one of ten directions of the same theme, all taking “city” as the starting point and running through love, society, land, and everything that happens on that land. You could call it a complete concept album! During production, Deserts Chang even spent three months writing four brand-new songs; the lyrics are like poetry, keeping her signature style while being more profound and more on point. To stay true to her long-standing commitment to music, Deserts Chang took on the role of main producer this time, handling everything big and small herself. During production it was inevitable that the four of them would disagree at times, and Deserts Chang had to keep reminding herself, from a producer’s standpoint, to put the essence of the music first! Even though the pressure left her short on sleep and wrecked her body clock, Deserts Chang still declared that being able to handle lyrics, composition, arrangement, and production all with her bandmates was a real thrill! Just like the album title City, this new album came together through the joint efforts of professional musicians from several cities. Over the eight-month production period, besides recording at three studios in Taiwan, Deserts Chang and Algae made a special trip to Beijing for mixing, and in the end even sent the album’s master tape to the United States for post-production — the making of it carried out the album concept of City to the letter! title: AS3 GIF player and Encoder
content: AS3GIF lets Flash play animated GIF files, and implements GIF encoding in ActionScript 3. Introduction as3gif download (Google Code) Bookmarking it here for easy lookup. Playback: Using AS3GIF’s class files, you can load a gif by loading a URLRequest or a ByteArray. Example: package { import flash.display.Sprite; import flash.net.URLRequest; import org.gif.player.GIFPlayer; public class Main extends Sprite { public function Main():void { var request:URLRequest new URLRequest(“diego.gif”); var player:GIFPlayer new GIFPlayer(); player.load(request); addChild(player); } } } Encoding: Example: package { import flash.display.BitmapData; import flash.display.Shape; import flash.display.Sprite; import flash.utils.ByteArray; import org.gif.encoder.GIFEncoder; import org.gif.player.GIFPlayer; public class Main extends Sprite { public function Main():void { var frames:Array createFrames(); var encoder:GIFEncoder new GIFEncoder(); encoder.setRepeat(0); AUTO LOOP encoder.setDelay(500); encoder.start(); MUST HAVE! encoder.addFrame(frames[0]); encoder.addFrame(frames[1]); encoder.finish(); MUST HAVE! playGIF(encoder.stream); } private function playGIF(data:ByteArray):void { data.position 0; var player:GIFPlayer new GIFPlayer(); player.loadBytes(data); addChild(player); } private function createFrames():Array { var shape:Shape new Shape(); shape.graphics.lineStyle(1, 0); shape.graphics.moveTo(60, 0); shape.graphics.lineTo(60, 120); var frame1:BitmapData new BitmapData(120, 120); frame1.draw(shape); shape.graphics.clear(); shape.graphics.lineStyle(1, 0); shape.graphics.moveTo(0, 60); shape.graphics.lineTo(120, 60); var frame2:BitmapData new BitmapData(120, 120); frame2.draw(shape); return [frame1, frame2]; } } }

title: Spending your whole life loading org.eclipse.php.core?
content: Problem description:At the company I use Zend Studio for Eclipse Professional Edition to write PHP projects. It’s a great piece of software, but it still has plenty of bugs. This morning it suddenly refused to start — it got stuck on loading org.eclipse.php.core and the progress bar never moved again. I tried reinstalling over the existing installation and it still didn’t work, which left me baffled. Was I going to be stuck at loading org.eclipse.php.core forever? Solution: Move C:\Documents and Settings\*\Zend\workspaces\DefaultWorkspace\.metadata\.plugins to any other directory Start Zend Studio for Eclipse — it launches successfully, but all the projects are gone Close Zend Studio for Eclipse Copy the contents of the C:\Documents and Settings\*\Zend\workspaces\DefaultWorkspace\.metadata\.plugins directory back (choose “No” to overwrite for every project it prompts about) Start Zend Studio for Eclipse again — oh yeah, back to normal!

title: GTween Tweening and Animation Library
content: Spotted a GTween AS3 library, thought I’d share it. GTween is a compact but quite robust AS3 library developed by Grant Skinner. It can be used to implement tweens, animations, and gradients. It currently consists of 4 key classes: GTween (4.5kb). A robust tweening engine that fully covers its authoring features. GTweenTimeline (1kb). A powerful virtual timeline that inherits from GTween, allowing tweens and actions to be chained in sequence. GTweenFilter (0.5kb). An extension of GTween that implements tweening for filters. GTweeny (3kb). GTween’s little brother — the ultimate lightweight version of GTween. It sacrifices some features for a smaller file size.GTween is licensed under the MIT license, so it can be used and modified in commercial projects with virtually no restrictions. title: STARCRAFT:GHOST still awaiting censorship?
content: News source: China Court Network. Blizzard Entertainment, the well-known American game company, applied to the State Administration for Industry and Commerce of China to register the English name of the new StarCraft title — STARCRAFT: GHOST — as a trademark for esports services and other items. The application was rejected by the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board on the grounds that the name involves promoting feudal superstition. Blizzard then filed suit with the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People’s Court, asking the court to overturn the Board’s decision to reject the review of the “STARCRAFT: GHOST” trademark application. This morning, reporters learned from the court that Blizzard’s claims were not upheld. Blizzard Entertainment is known worldwide for developing StarCraft, Warcraft, and many other online games. In 1998, the real-time strategy PC game “STARCRAFT” — StarCraft — that the company released took the world by storm, and the game also became one of the four major titles in today’s global esports competitions. As for the rejection of the “STARCRAFT: GHOST” trademark registration, the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board’s stated reason was that “STARCRAFT: GHOST” is a term prone to producing negative effects, carrying the meanings of “astrology” and “ghost,” and thus constitutes feudal superstition contrary to socialist morality. The Board held that a trademark, beyond indicating the source of goods, is also a vehicle with a cultural and promotional orientation, and must not carry any circumstance that could produce negative effects. “Astrology ghost,” from any angle, is inconsistent with socialist morality, and if it were not stopped, the trademark field would be flooded with a large number of word marks of the same character. After the trademark was rejected, Blizzard sued in court, stating that its application to register the “STARCRAFT: GHOST” trademark for game news, esports services and other items was for the purpose of providing related information and game services on its online game service platform Battle.net, and was absolutely not for promoting feudal superstition or engaging in illegal superstitious activities. “STARCRAFT: GHOST” is the name of a computer game, has nothing to do with superstition, and will not produce negative effects. Moreover, the company had already registered the “STARCRAFT: GHOST” trademark, No. 4809949, in Class 9 goods, “computer game software,” which shows that the trademark is registrable. In addition, Blizzard submitted a large number of web pages found through Baidu and Google searches to prove that “STARCRAFT: GHOST” translates as StarCraft: Ghost, is simply a game name, and has nothing to do with feudal superstition. This morning, it was learned from the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People’s Court that Blizzard’s claims have been rejected by the court, which held that using the text “STARCRAFT: GHOST” as a trademark is likely to lead to negative effects. It is understood that Blizzard has already appealed the case. This article is reprinted from http://www.cnbeta.com/articles/76985.htm

title: View world-famous paintings in ultra-high resolution with Google
content: Getting a close-up look at the world’s great paintings and witnessing the masterpieces of the old masters will set you back a fair amount of money — but now you can get up close and personal with 14 world-famous paintings for free in a virtual gallery on Google Earth. A newly added layer in Google Earth showcases 14 world-class masterpieces from Spain’s Prado Museum by famous painters such as the Dutch artists Rubens and Rembrandt. Every painting is displayed in ultra-high resolution — you can even see the sweep of the brush, the weave of the canvas, or the fine cracks that have formed on the surface over the years. Open Google Earth, check “3d Buildings” (3D building models) under “Layers” in the bottom-left corner, then expand Geographic Web - Places - Preview - Museo Prado (Prado Museum) in turn, and you’ll arrive at the famous Prado Museum in Spain. More info: http://googlechinablog.com/2009/01/blog-post_16.html
