title: Pleasant Goat and Big Big Wolf: Bullish Rampage
content: Pleasant Goat and Big Big Wolf is a cartoon that has long dominated the domestic TV animation ratings. Its character designs are adorable, the plot is witty and humorous, and these endlessly entertaining stories are never short on educational value. Every night, whenever I go to that restaurant near the office and Pleasant Goat and Big Big Wolf comes on the TV, I’m rooted to the spot…… Yesterday, the theatrical feature Pleasant Goat and Big Big Wolf: The Super Snail Adventure hit theaters! So excited! Plot summary: Spring returns to the earth, and it also happens to be the 100th anniversary celebration of Village Chief Slow Goat. But Slow Goat’s mount, the old snail, suddenly falls ill, and after examining it, the chief senses the gravity of the situation and plans to go inside the snail to wipe out the virus causing the disease. The young goats think it’s too dangerous and insist on going into the snail’s body to destroy the virus in the chief’s place. What they don’t know is that Big Big Wolf has overheard them, and he wants to get inside the snail too, to catch the goats. Pleasant Goat, Fit Goat, Lazy Goat and Pretty Goat arrive on the snail’s two antennae. Before Pleasant Goat and Pretty Goat can figure out what kind of place this is, they’re forcibly conscripted by white bacteria (white ox) soldiers. And with no boot camp at all, they’re dragged straight onto the battle-scarred front lines. In the barracks they learn that this is a bacterial kingdom perched on the snail’s antenna — the White Ox Kingdom. Lately this snail world has been anything but calm, with earthquakes going on day after day. The king concludes it must be the work of the black bacteria (black ox) kingdom on the other antenna — the Black Ox Kingdom. To wipe out the evil Black Ox Kingdom and stop this bacterial infection, the White Ox Kingdom drafts its entire national force and launches a war. Since their goals are the same, Pleasant Goat joins the White Ox Kingdom’s army and fights the Black Ox Kingdom’s bacteria alongside them. The two kingdoms draw up their battle lines at the border, and Pleasant Goat discovers that the Black Ox Kingdom is actually led by Big Big Wolf, who has even built newfangled weapons — tanks and aircraft. The White Ox Kingdom’s army is routed and surrounded on all sides. The communicator Pleasant Goat brought along has had no signal the whole time. To get in touch with the village chief, Pleasant Goat has to cross a dangerous forbidden zone — the Whirlpool Black Forest, where bacteria hardly ever set foot and where entering means almost certain death. But Pleasant Goat sets off without hesitation. After a long journey, just as he’s about to reach the forest’s exit, he runs into the mysterious barbarian bacteria tribe (yellow ox). He manages to escape, but the communicator falls into the barbarians’ hands. Big Big Wolf even becomes their military strategist, building all sorts of bacteria-controlling devices and wiping out both the Black Ox and White Ox bacterial kingdoms in one stroke. Once it’s done, the bacteria of those two kingdoms will be food for the barbarians, while the goats will be Big Big Wolf’s to enjoy. The mighty barbarian bacteria army surrounds the two kingdoms so tightly that nothing can get through, and declares that the bacteria of both kingdoms will become their food. Neither king could ever have imagined that the always gentle, peaceable barbarian bacteria were actually the true root cause of this world’s disease! Just as Big Big Wolf is gloating, he never expects that he himself gets eaten by the barbarian yellow-ox bacteria king. To save everyone, Pleasant Goat enters a life-and-death battle with the yellow ox, and in the end even makes the sacrifice that brings Little Grey back, getting Big Big Wolf to promise never to eat a single strand of wool again. In the end, the snail finally recovers its health, and the goats and Big Big Wolf and his wife return to the grassland. But at the victory celebration Big Big Wolf makes his move, declaring that he hasn’t broken his vow — he won’t eat a single strand of wool; he’ll skin them first and then eat them! To his surprise, Pleasant Goat was prepared all along and turns the tables on him. When the other goats angrily want to finish Big Big Wolf off, Pleasant Goat lets them go instead — because everything in this world has its own reason to exist, and you can’t just wipe things out on a whim —— On the Green Green Grassland, the joyful story of goats and wolves will go on forever!——http://www.douban.com/subject/3356338/

title: Joanna & Wang Ruolin
content: Two exciting things today, and here’s the second: Joanna Wang’s new album is out! About the album: Joanna steps up to producer, co-producing with her father Wang Zhiping. A dream production team, and Joanna thinks the album came out even better than she expected. Joanna’s first album was produced by her father, Mr. Wang Zhiping. Her father is a musician she respects and admires, but because Joanna has her own very distinct sensibility and ideas about music, the two of them actually argued nonstop throughout the production process. Still, after going through the first album together and seeing the enthusiastic response it got, this time Mr. Wang Zhiping gave Joanna more space and co-produced this album with her. For the arrangements and recording they brought in a dream production team, including guitarist Freddy Koella, who has worked with Carla Bruni; keyboardist Roger Joseph Manning Jr., who has worked with Beck; bassist Paul Bushnell, who has worked with Faith Hill; and drummer Brian Macleod, who has worked with Sheryl Crow. As before, the album was recorded at Mad Dog studio. Recording engineer Eric Corne is himself a fine independent artist, he has a particularly good grasp of the atmosphere Joanna wanted to create, and he gave her a lot of help and advice. As for the engineer handling mastering, mixing and post-production, Pete Doell, he not only has years of experience and has worked with Miles Davis, he is currently producing the music for the globally popular video game Guitar Hero 3. Beyond singing, writing and producing, she can write lyrics too — Joanna shows off her all-around talent on the new album. On top of her naturally gifted voice and singing and her one-of-a-kind songwriting, on this album Joanna also shows her talent for writing lyrics. Her lyrics, as she describes her own personality, carry a touch of wry humor; the more serious the subject, the more she tends to state it with a slightly playful, ironic touch. Four songs on this album were composed by the album’s keyboardist, with lyrics by Joanna: Tikiville, Maybe Some Other Time, 我的爱, and 一种念头. Keyboardist Roger Joseph Manning Jr. is himself a member of the band Jellyfish, which has a following in Japan, and is also an excellent songwriter. This time Joanna set Chinese and English lyrics to his brand-new compositions, revealing a new side of her all-around talent. Book your personal request chart for this year. title: Jingru & Love Songs - Don't Cry for Him Anymore
content: Two exciting things today. First: Fish Leong’s new album is out! Not long ago she released the EP I Do, and I was still hungry for more. Now the new album has landed — awesome! Album intro: Fish Leong’s new album officially drops on January 16, more than a year after her last one. This new record, Jingru Love Songs – Don’t Cry for Him Anymore, is her tenth solo release since her debut. Determined not to disappoint fans who had waited so long, and set on delivering the most perfect work possible, the ever-obedient Fish Leong actually went to the mat with her record label over the release date! She wheedled and pressured the company for ages, giving the label its first taste of the “Leong power” of a queen of love ballads! Jingru and the label each held their ground; the album’s release hit a stalemate. It turned out the label had very high hopes for the new album. Not wanting to miss out on submitting for next year’s Golden Melody Awards, it wanted to get the album out before the end of the year. Company execs felt that for Jingru, nominated four years running at the Golden Melody Awards, missing the entry deadline because the album couldn’t come out by the end of December would be a real shame. But although Fish Leong thought the Golden Melody Awards mattered, she didn’t want the time for vocal and album recording squeezed because of them. There was plenty of time ahead, she felt; making an album she could truly have no regrets about mattered more! Jingru wanted the release date pushed back so the album would have ample time to be as good as it could be. So the two sides locked horns in meeting after meeting over the timing, and the release was deadlocked for a while! Delayed by three weeks, the new album misses Christmas and New Year’s In the end the label had no choice but to respect Jingru’s perfectionism and kept pushing the release date back. Because Jingru’s earlier concert had been themed Today Is Valentine’s Day, the label had originally planned to tie the album’s release to Christmas on 1224. For the reasons above it had to be pushed to 1231, but Jingru still insisted the post-production be flawless, and finally the official release was set for 116 — a full three weeks late. When the label heard the finished master recently, it had to admit that the perfect result her insistence produced was more convincing than any award! Two idol dramas’ theme songs hit back to back; the “K-song queen” adds “theme song queen” to her titles The new album is titled Jingru Love Songs – Don’t Cry for Him Anymore, and its concept revolves around “bravely bidding farewell to old love, fearlessly pursuing new love.” From Happy Breakup to Worship, “Fish Leong love songs” has already become a proper noun, and this time it drew even more requests to be named as a drama theme song. From Blue Lan’s new drama I Do to My Queen, starring Ethan Ruan and Sonia Sui, both productions approached Jingru as soon as they learned she was about to release a new album, hoping the appeal of the spokesperson for love ballads would add to their stories. I Do airs on TTV Mondays through Thursdays at 10 p.m. starting 1222, with reruns on TVBS-G Saturdays at 10 p.m. from 1227; My Queen will also air on TTV Sundays at 10 p.m. from 14, then on SETTV Saturdays at 9 p.m. from 110 — almost creating the monopoly spectacle of hearing Fish Leong every night of the week. Confident that the album had too many good songs, the label spent nearly 3.5 million before release to lock up all the theme songs for both idol dramas, so new Jingru songs could be heard every day from Monday to Sunday — and unexpectedly created the first case of Jingru “PK-ing” herself on TV through drama theme songs! Find Someone 11. The Piper 12. Nursery Rhyme Disc 2 Belonging 02. PK – Fish Leong Gary Cao 03. Still Good Friends – Fish Leong Leo Ku 04. It’s Not That I Don’t Understand – Fish Leong Crowd Lu 05. Way Back Into Love – Fish Leong Victor Wong Listendownload: eMule download page RayFile download page PS: If you like the album, make sure to buy the genuine CD!

title: PDO transaction error?
content: Today I hit an error in the PDO transaction-handling part: Fatal error: Uncaught exception ‘PDOException’ with message ‘There is no active transaction’ in datawwwweb.passportpayclassesclass.Mydb.php:145 Stack trace: #0 datawwwweb.passportpayclassesclass.Mydb.php(145): PDO-rollBack() #1 datawwwweb.passportpayyeepayOrder.php(138): Mydb-transaction(Array) #2 {main} thrown in datawwwweb.passportpayclassesclass.Mydb.php on line 145 Looking through the error log I saw: 2009-01-16 09:27:57: 事务处理出错:SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 2014 Cannot execute queries while other unbuffered queries are active. Consider using PDOStatement::fetchAll(). Alternatively, if your code is only ever going to run against mysql, you may enable query buffering by setting the PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY attribute. My code is: ###Transaction function transaction($sqlQueue) { $this-connection(); if(count($sqlQueue)0) { if($this-charset ! NULL) { $this-db-exec(“SET NAMES “.$this-charset); }else{ $this-db-exec(“SET NAMES utf8”); } try { $this-db-setAttribute(PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE, PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION); $this-db-setAttribute(PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY, true); $this-db-beginTransaction(); foreach ($sqlQueue as $sql) { $this-db-exec($sql); } $this-db-commit(); return true; } catch (Exception $e) { $this-logWriter-writeLog(“事务处理出错:”.$e-getMessage().” SQL语句:”.Utils::arrToString($sqlQueue)); $this-db-rollBack(); return false; } }else{ return false; } } After searching a bunch of sites, I’ve summed up several ways to solve this kind of problem. 1.setAttribute(PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY, true); When you receive error like this:General error: 2014 Cannot execute queries while other unbuffered queries are active.This means that you need to uncomment the following:On line 137 of “libVarienDbAdapterPdoMysql.php”, find:#$this-_connection-setAttribute(PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY, true);and then uncomment it out, so it should be$this-_connection-setAttribute(PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY, true); ——(http://www.magentocommerce.com/boards/viewthread/35/) Many people have tested this and it does solve the “Cannot execute queries while other unbuffered queries are active” problem.But I added this line and it still didn’t work.And some say that since PHP 5.2.1 this attribute has defaulted to true. 2. fetchAll() the query result set to release the PDOStatement:A passage from the PDO::query docs: If you do not fetch all of the data in a result set before issuing your next call to PDO::query(), your call may fail. Call PDOStatement::closeCursor() to release the database resources associated with the PDOStatement object before issuing your next call to PDO::query(). ——(http://www.unbe.cn/blog/?p=21) In other words, issuing a new query before the previous one has finished will throw an error, so you have to release the previous query. Exactly as the error message says: “Consider using PDOStatement::fetchAll()”. 3. Install the latest PHP…..http://bugs.php.net/bug.php?id=44081 mentions that PHP 5.2.5 has a bug, and this guy was going out of his mind: “ however i closed the cursor after each result fetch!!!! ” He suspected he’d hit a bug (one that appears in PHP 5.2.5). I think that suspicion is not unreasonable — my code runs fine on the company’s internal PHP 5.2.6, but on the company’s external server (PHP 5.1.6) it throws the error above. Fixing it properly (installing PHP 5.2.6 or later) seems like a real hassle, so it’s better to work around it and find another way. 4. Only one CREATE TABLE statement can be executed at a timeThen I saw this comrade: http://blog.chinaunix.net/u/4891/showart.php?id=1672950 ran into the same error, and the cause was putting two CREATE TABLE statements separated by a semicolon into a single statement to execute, whereas php.net says: “CREATE TABLE statements can only be executed one at a time” 5. Use closeCursor() to release resourcesBefore querying, if you have already executed query(), you need to run PDOStatement::closeCursor() to release the database resource connection. So I changed it to: ###Transaction function transaction($sqlQueue) { $this-connection(); if(count($sqlQueue)0) { * * Manual says: * If you do not fetch all of the data in a result set before issuing your next call to PDO::query(), your call may fail. Call PDOStatement::closeCursor() to release the database resources associated with the PDOStatement object before issuing your next call to PDO::query(). * * $this-result-closeCursor(); if($this-charset ! NULL) { $this-db-exec(“SET NAMES “.$this-charset); }else{ $this-db-exec(“SET NAMES utf8”); } try { $this-db-setAttribute(PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE, PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION); $this-db-setAttribute(PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY, true); $this-db-beginTransaction(); foreach ($sqlQueue as $sql) { $this-db-exec($sql); } $this-db-commit(); return true; } catch (Exception $e) { $this-logWriter-writeLog(“事务处理出错:”.$e-getMessage().” SQL语句:”.Utils::arrToString($sqlQueue)); $this-db-rollBack(); return false; } }else{ return false; } } Problem solved. (In fact this solution is the same as #2.)

title: Heartbeat...
content: Damn it, this Wang Leehom album falls so far short of what I expected… It’s bad, bad, really bad. Especially that song “Loving Properly” — the lyrics seriously gross me out… To each their own. Even if I don’t think it sounds good, I still want to show some support. About: Close your eyes. Quiet down. His heartbeat. Do you hear it? A heartbeat born of days and nights without pause, creating a musical life force that never dies out. The peak of Wang Leehom’s love songs — hear the most tender beat of his heart before anyone else. In his life, the number of times he has heard someone say “I love you” to him far exceeds that of an ordinary person by ten millionfold. A single concert might have tens of thousands of people shouting in unison: “Wang Leehom, I love you.” On stage, amid the passion and the frenzy, he is a radiant superstar. Yet “I love you” is also, for him, the hardest sentence to come by. A glance, a moment of tenderness, a memory of a heartbeat — Leehom wrote this song. It digs out, as never before, what he truly feels about love deep in his heart. This song sat on Leehom’s computer for months; he only brought it out when album production had entered its final stage. Perhaps, for a musician who has always been clumsy at putting inner feelings into words, a song like this is like laying his inner world bare in front of the public. Leehom struggled with it for a long time. In the end, we heard “Heartbeat.” This musical work, built around Leehom’s inner world, became all the more complete because of this song. The story of this song begins like this… That night, Leehom walked out of the concert rehearsal room. It was already some unknown number of days into his busy schedule — he often woke up unsure of where he was, needing a few seconds to recall before he could be sure whether he was in Taiwan or overseas. The August night was still sweltering. Every cell in his body was already too exhausted to think, yet notes surfaced in his mind — only that fragment vanished before it could go on, while the moving melody of that moment stayed deeply imprinted in his heart. Then came rehearsals spinning on like a top without stopping, commercial shoots, performances, recording songs for the new album… Once again he buried himself in his music work, and whatever care or contact came from friends had to rely on email or text messages. He remembers that on the way back to Taiwan after finishing a commercial shoot overseas, he closed his eyes to rest — and suddenly recalled the melody that had flashed through his mind so long ago. It was only a short bit of melody, but he felt it should be more than that! The first “MUSIC-MAN” show at Taipei Arena was an unprecedented success, and the second won unanimous praise and acclaim from media at home and abroad. After it ended that night, his ears were filled with the music that had just finished and the fans’ screams still echoing; his heart was full of an indescribable mix of feelings. He was happy — he had once again successfully completed a challenge. And he was also lost: it was as if this farewell would bring yet another new beginning. A complicated, contradictory mood filled Leehom’s heart. When he stepped into the building’s elevator with the gait of someone who has spent every last ounce of energy, it was already past three in the morning. Suddenly the melody sounded at his ear, flying at him like snowflakes — out of order, regardless of length or tempo — overflowing with incredible notes, as if it had been piling up in his heart for a long time and was now pouring out. Never mind that his flight overseas was less than five hours away — Leehom went straight into the studio, picked up a guitar and wrote the melody down. As he wrote, the lyrics came out at the same time. By the time he put down his pen, it was already light out; in another hour he would have to leave for the airport. This song made Leehom’s heart race from start to finish, and left a deep impression on him. Leehom Does It All Himself: Crafting “Heartbeat” by Hand, Playing Every Instrument Leehom personally handled nearly every part of “Heartbeat.” Beyond writing the melody, the lyrics and the arrangement, he played every instrument on the song himself — guitar, bass, piano, drums and more — conveying the song’s most genuine inner emotion with a purely hand-crafted, warm touch. International Mixing Master Mick Guzauki Brought On Board; Leehom Demanded Dozens of Mixes in Pursuit of Perfection To make the instruments and tones of “Heartbeat” deliver the most moving listening experience, he specially brought in international mixing master Mick Guzauki (who has worked with such international stars as Mariah Carey, Brian McKnight, Micheal Jachson, Cekine Dion…). During the process Leehom repeatedly demanded that the mix reach the most heart-racing emotion, almost setting a record for the most mixes Mick Guzauki has ever done on a single track — showing just how extraordinary the challenge and difficulty of “Heartbeat” are, and making this 2008 peak love song from Leehom all the more anticipated! Tracklist: Loving Properly Heartbeat The Sun Washed by Spring Rain Everything I Have Absolutely No Reason to Pay You Any Mind Another Heaven - Wang Leehom + Zhang Liangying Doll Script Competitor What’s Wrong with Rock

title: TV drama "Demon" premieres
content: Starting January 4, 2009 Beijing time, the TV series Demons began airing. I’m not particularly drawn to this vampire-fantasy genre; I finished Heroes, so I’ll make do with this one for now. Downloaded it and took a look — ha, several of the actors are from the cast of Merlin. The show’s lead, Luke Van Helsing, is Arthur in Merlin, and his godfather Rupert Galvin is his father the king in Merlin… This series is adapted from the classic Dracula vampire story, set in modern-day London. The story begins when teenager Luke Rutherford (played by Christian Cooke) is suddenly visited by his arrogant and insufferable American godfather, Rupert Galvin (Philip Glenister). Galvin’s visit is no casual one — he brings Luke some shocking news: the dark forces of the world are gathering, and as the last bloodline of the Van Helsing family (the famous vampire hunter — see the film of the same name), it is now his duty to destroy them. Luke barely has time to think about this news before he’s thrown into intense training. Helping Galvin with this task is the beautiful but ice-cold Mina Harker (played by Zoe Tapper), a blind concert pianist revered as the leading authority on “half-lives” (vampires, demons, voodoo, ronin, and so on). The last member of the four-person team is Luke’s best friend Ruby (played by Zoe Holliday). Ruby is a very feisty girl who not only loves bickering with Luke, but is also extremely keen on “destroying” things. In addition, whenever Luke runs into “unidentified creatures”, the dangerous voodoo priest and bishop Simeon (played by Richard Wilson) will supply him with the traditions and myths behind each creature. Luke’s first enemy is Gladiolas Thrip (guest-starring Mackenzie Crook), one of the most dangerous vampires in the underworld (the netherworld). A bounty hunter with a dark sense of humor, Thrip harbors a burning hatred for the Van Helsings, and he is determined to kill the last of the line. Other half-lives Luke will battle include the “Noisy Boys”, a pack of hyenas in eye patches running wild through London’s streets; “Red Lips”, monkey-like creatures that lurk in the shadows and stalk human victims; “Mr. Tibbs”, a half-human, half-rat creature that experiments on humans in his basement; and “Gilgamel”, an ancient demon that devours children’s souls. At the same time, Luke will also learn a secret: the truth about his father’s mysterious death fifteen years ago during a “business trip” abroad. The more-than-six-episode Demons will air on ITV1 early next year. If you like stories of the Underworld or Van Helsing movie variety, you’re bound to enjoy this series. Episode 1 plot: Luke Rutherford is an ordinary teenager — until one day, his late father’s friend Rupert Galvin suddenly shows up at his door. Galvin tells Luke that his origins are anything but ordinary: he is the great-grandson of the famous vampire hunter Abraham Van Helsing, and Van Helsing was the sworn enemy of the vampire patriarch Count Dracula. Supernatural monsters are plotting a global attack, and Luke must take up the family mantle and fight them to the end. Meanwhile, the most dangerous vampire in the underworld (the netherworld), Gladiolas Thrip, has awakened… This bounty hunter with a dark sense of humor harbors a burning hatred for the Van Helsing line, and he is determined to kill the last of the family. ——verycd.com Download link: http://www.verycd.com/topics/2725530/ http://www.verycd.com/topics/2725674/

title: More Flash online image processing
content: After seeing Halley’s image processing tool, I came across another mature online image-processing RIA, similar to Photoshop, very powerful, specializing in bitmap work — you can open images uploaded from your local machine and edit and composite them. It even has layer styles, filters, and all that. Extremely capable, but at the same time relatively complex to operate, and fairly heavy on machine resources. Let’s just look at the results: http://www.sumopaint.com/app/ That also brings to mind the https://www.photoshop.com/ platform I saw a while back — a great experience.

title: Online image processing built with Flash
content: I came across an online image-editing RIA on Halley‘s blog. MediaCreator alpha1 is an online multimedia authoring app built in Flash — a prototype along the lines of scrapblog. Some basic functionality is already in place: it lets users edit images, text and vector graphics online, and add masks, borders and backgrounds. Down the road it may also support uploading images from your local machine, importing images directly from platforms like photobucket, Flickr, webshots, Facebook, Picasa, Smugmug, and even adding audio, video and online animation creation. For now it’s still experimental. If anyone with similar interests is keen, collaboration and joint development are more than welcome. Screenshot: Address: http://www.asblog.org/MediaCreator Author’s blog: http://www.asblog.org/2009/01/10/mediacreator-alpha1/[http://www.asblog.org/](http://www.asblog.org/)

title: In IE, the .type of an input element is read-only!
content: Today I hit an error and discovered that in IE the .type of an input element is read-only! Related description:In IE the .type of an input element cannot be set dynamically; input.type=hidden; in IE an input cannot be dynamically switched between text and hidden; Problem description:There’s a chunk of js like this: together with this chunk of html: What nickname do your parents call you? What’s the name of your best friend? Who is the teacher you respect most? Custom question What I wanted to do: let the user pick an item from the dropdown; if the last item “Custom question” is selected, make the text box visible and give it focus; if any other item is selected, hide the text box and set its value to the text of the selected item. In FF this works fine, but in IE you can’t set safeQuestion.type=text. Cause:In FF, input element .type [ = sType ] is supported; in IE the input.type property is read-only. Official statement: In IE, except for elements created dynamically with the createElement method, the type property is read-only in all other cases Solution:Just switch to controlling visibility with Style… What nickname do your parents call you? What’s the name of your best friend? Who is the teacher you respect most? Custom question

title: Jane@Music!
content: Dolphin Princess Jane Zhang is set to release her new album “Jane Zhang@Music” on the 20th of this month — another treat for the ears in time for the Lunar New Year! 2009, waiting for this voice to warm us once again… Tracklist: The Sound of Flowers Blooming That Can’t Be Love, Right? Light in the Dark Night It’s Me My Music Lets Me Speak Torn Close to You Sunshine Alike A Child’s Eyes My Way Download verycd download page “The Sound of Flowers Blooming” lyrics: Though people change, though hearts change, but you know, but I know, how good it is to love someone. In the time it takes for a cup of coffee, holding hands and watching the fallen leaves drift. Those heart-to-hearts, those little secrets — anyone who has loved understands. Though life changes, though feelings change, but you know, but I know, love is in every minute, every second. As long as I lean shoulder to shoulder with you, sharing the smallest feelings, everything goes quiet, everything is so beautiful, and I don’t care how loud this world is. I hear the sound of flowers blooming, and you, warm, looking at me with your radiant smile. I love the way you look at me like that; in your eyes I am the only one. I love the way I love you like that; I can’t hold back my heart. My heart keeps thinking, keeps thinking of you. Though life changes, though feelings change, but you know, but I know, love is in every minute, every second. As long as I lean shoulder to shoulder with you, sharing the smallest feelings, everything goes quiet, everything is so beautiful, and I don’t care how loud this world is. I hear the sound of flowers blooming, and you, warm, looking at me with your radiant smile. I love the way you look at me like that; in your eyes I am the only one. I love the way I love you like that; I can’t hold back my heart. My heart keeps thinking, keeps thinking of you. (Why do I love you like that and yet not want to hold back my heart?) I love the way I love you like that; I can’t hold back my heart. Like a flower blooming, radiant and beautiful. My heart keeps thinking, keeps thinking of you, thinking of you. Three years into her career, Jane Zhang has kept up a pace of one new album a year. At the start of 2009, her third solo album, “Jane Zhang@Music”, is about to be released. This highly anticipated new album went through a production cycle lasting as long as half a year, and after being carefully crafted by Huayi Music, it will hit stores before the Spring Festival. For the album as a whole, renowned Taiwanese musician Wawa served as production coordinator, with musicians Keith Stuart, Zhang Yadong and Guo Liang handling production, fully expressing Jane Zhang’s diversity through ten songs in different styles. You could say that after three years of hard work, Jane Zhang has finally found her own musical direction in this album, and the early-released album cover lets fans be the first to feel the visual impact of her brand-new image. “Jane Zhang@Music”, a special album title, announces to the world with a somewhat audacious attitude Jane’s ambition in the world of music. The starting point of this album is “Jane Zhang’s music” — “Jane Zhang is in the music, and the music is Jane Zhang”. And @, a widely known internet symbol, looks quite ordinary in this somewhat unique album title, yet it is no meaningless expression. It highlights youth and vitality, and stands for endlessly more extension and more possibilities. This abstract concreteness is just like Jane’s performance on this album: free, unrestrained, effortless. All 10 songs on the album are good, so in the end they could only cast aside every flashy gimmick and return to simplicity, taking “Jane Zhang@Music” as the album title. The ten songs collected on the album, each in a different style, are each like a wonderful short story, existing on their own terms. The lead single “That Can’t Be Love, Right?” has the passion and quirkiness of youth, “Light in the Dark Night” shows grandeur and beauty, and “Torn” is for those struggling in love and their friends… Listening to these songs, you hear a girl who loves to sing, transforming from a green, groping beginner into someone confident, truly enjoying the happiness of singing; through all the twists and turns of music she gradually takes on a distinctive shape. Listening to these songs, any kind of explanation may be superfluous — only the singing can find a meeting of hearts. When a certain song becomes an irreplaceable memory in the years of your life, you and your lover, your friends, and you and yourself will all hear a song that belongs to you in Jane Zhang’s new album. In order to bring out the album’s musicality in its visuals, Huayi Music specially invited the well-known photographer Jiang Junmin to shoot a new set of promotional photos for Jane Zhang. In the early-released album cover, intense tones form the basis of the whole image, paired with Jane’s flowing long hair and an incomplete face — it looks like a photo gone wrong, but in fact expresses the core concept of this album: valuing musicality and breakthrough. It is said that in addition to this set of boldly conceptual promotional photos, the album also includes another set of fresh, simple images, striving to show every smile and glance of Jane Zhang in front of the camera through two sets of images in different styles. “Jane Zhang@Music,” Jane Zhang’s third solo album, will go on full sale before the Spring Festival, and Huayi Music will also arrange a series of promotional events before the New Year, giving fans more chances to meet Jane Zhang face to face. — From the internet

title: After finishing season 3 of Heroes, seeking the truth
content: The show Heroes has an astonishing imagination (omitting 10,000 lines of praise code here)… After watching the first three seasons, I’ve found plenty of mysterious events that the show’s own rules can’t explain. After three seasons I feel trapped in the mystery, and I hope that one day some expert will tell me the truth! Mystery 1: About the 2 annular solar eclipses. According to the plot, one annular solar eclipse appears in the first season and one in the third, one year apart. In the third season, the heroes start to realize that most of their powers manifested after that annular eclipse a year earlier. The annular eclipse in the third season caused everyone’s superpowers to vanish, including people like Arthur who had powers long before. And since Arthur, after the annular eclipse struck and he lost his powers, was baffled and ordered Dr. Surush to hurry up and develop a way to restore them, we can see that he was utterly unprepared for and utterly ignorant of the effects the annular eclipse brings. That being so, did the annular eclipse a year earlier not affect him at all? Why does he have zero experience with it? Now let’s look at Adam. He’s lived for countless years—has he never once been through an annular eclipse messing with superpowers? We see that when Adam’s powers were absorbed by Arthur, he instantly turned to dust, and because all the injuries Claire had ever sustained flared up once she lost her powers, so Adam’s immortality, once it stops working, should likewise turn him to ash. What’s more, at the very start of the first season, Peter’s powers were just beginning to manifest, and his abilities were granted at birth by his parents using the company’s research. From Angela Petrelli’s dramatic account of how back then they were fully confident that Peter and Nathan could master their powers, it’s clear the Petrelli family understood the effects of granting superpowers, and Peter’s powers only surfacing at the eclipse ought to have been something they expected. Yet Arthur’s expression makes it look like he has no clue whatsoever about the relationship between the eclipse and superpowers! Mystery 2: Relativity—time flowing backward The last episode’s opening and closing are way too sloppy—they actually drag relativity into it. Ando’s power-amplification + Daphne’s super speed running speed exceeding the speed of light time flowing backward, going back 16 years to save Hiro… Never mind why they didn’t go back even earlier to help Hiro stop Arthur—the mystery here is: time being able to flow backward doesn’t mean you can go back and forth. If you can explain going back to the past, how do you explain running back to the present again? Mystery*: I won’t even mention the N other small bugs. Small bugs I don’t much care about—you can still paper them over. Big bugs I’m powerless against; my brain is turning to mush, mush… I’ve gone off the deep end.

title: The Fountain
content: On 08.12.12, I watched The Fountain — a truly rare gem of a film! Through a unique story, the film recounts the protagonist’s eternal love for his wife, and reveals the meaning of life and the value of death. If you go into this film thinking it’s about humanity’s search for immortality, you’ll definitely be disappointed — you might even despise it and write it off as a bad movie. In fact, the film ranges from Genesis in the Bible to Mayan civilization, touching on Zen, Buddhism, enlightenment, and wisdom. The plot follows one man’s journey from an almost mad desire to find a way to save his deeply beloved, terminally ill wife, and his fear of death, to his realization that the true meaning of death is to give birth to new life. The deeper you love someone, the deeper your fear of losing her. The protagonist researches day and night, searching for the hope of conquering cancer and achieving immortality. He throws himself fully into his research, growing more and more agitated, obsessed with creating a miracle on earth, yet he doesn’t spend his time with his wife through her final days. “Come take a walk with me,” “The first snow has fallen”… To these final requests, he can only keep apologizing, leaving his wife behind for one experiment after another. Although the experiments make remarkable progress, he still can’t save his beloved in time. Finally, death arrives… How is the unfinished final chapter to be completed? How can humanity escape the fear of death? “But I don’t know how it ends,” “You do know. You will know,” “Finish it”… He finally reaches the Tree of Life, plunges in a knife, and fresh sap of life flows out; he drinks it frantically. When he pulls out the ring and is about to put it on, every cell in his body is transforming; plants grow out from within him, devouring him… He finally attains enlightenment. “Come take a walk with me,” “The first snow has fallen” — he hesitates for a moment, and instead of choosing the lab, he rushes toward his wife in the snow. He walks out of the “crystal ball” alone, and in the explosion he and the tree turn into dust in the cosmos. He breaks through his inner demons and finds the answer — the final chapter: “I finished it.” “Is everything all right?” “Yes, everything is all right.” “You may have love, but do not cling to it, for separation is inevitable.” “When you let go, that is when you have no more troubles.” On mtime I came across a very powerful interpretation; the author, Shunxi Tianya, offers a complete and incisive appreciation of the film: I’d very much like to call it a conceptual film. Director Aronofsky uses a visual language full of metaphor and symbol, along with interwoven, psychedelic montage, to provide the audience with an open text. The mysterious tone of Mayan mythology, the cosmic thinking reminiscent of 2001: A Space Odyssey, the love and pain of earthly life, and the philosophical reflections on death, eternity, rebirth, reincarnation, redemption, faith, meaning, and much more — all of this makes it seem as though behind every frame of the film lurks some kind of revelation and meditation. It’s like a marvelous Rubik’s cube: although the film itself has only one structure, it lets you understand, through different paths, those intricate hidden messages concealed behind the structure — and what’s here is merely one of many possible realities or illusions. (1) Narrative Through a parallel, intercutting narrative, the film fuses three stories set in different times and spaces — the Spanish conquistador, the pharmacological scientist, and the space traveler — around the common themes of love and death, forming a kind of science-fiction visual style. In my view, the pharmacologist Tommy did not actually embark on a millennia-spanning odyssey, and neither the conquistador Tomás nor the space traveler Tom are simply fictional characters in Izzi’s book modeled on her husband. What the film really wants to tell is the process Tommy goes through as he faces his wife’s impending death — from pain and fear and frenzy to eventual enlightenment. Here, the conquistador is the plot described in Izzi’s book, while the space traveler symbolizes Tommy’s inner world. The true starting point of the story is the year 2001. Tommy, who deeply loves his wife, is afraid of losing Izzi, who is already in the late stages of brain cancer, so he leads his research team in conducting drug experiments with near madness, longing to save his wife’s life through a miracle. But in reality, the ever-changing nature of her condition and the death that could come at any moment make Tommy more and more anxious and more and more afraid. He is fixated on his experiments and neglects the last chance to be with and care for Izzi. Of course, all of this is entirely out of love for his wife, out of that intense desire to be together forever. Izzi, who loves her husband just as deeply, fully understands what Tommy is feeling at this moment; she can’t bear to stop him, nor does she have the strength to, from chasing that last glimmer of hope. But she knows she will eventually leave this world. To help Tommy accept this cruel fact and pull himself together to go on living bravely, she adopts something like a philosophical form of enlightenment: she expresses her expectations — her dying wish — through the form of a novel. She prepares pen and ink for Tommy, hoping he will help her finish the story’s final ending. When Tommy says, “But I don’t know what the ending is,” she tells him, “You do know. You will know.” At first, Tommy clearly cannot grasp his wife’s intention, blinded by his own fear and avoidance, but after a difficult odyssey of the soul, he finally understands Izzi’s good intentions and the feelings about life and death she has been telling him about all along. You can see that the film’s cross-cutting narration of the three stories appears chaotic on the surface but is in fact logical. After Tommy’s story is told for the first time, the narratives about the conquistador and the space traveler are closely tied to Tommy’s real-life situation. The transition from the real-world scenes to the Spanish setting is bridged by the act of reading a book; the text that flashes quickly across the screen and gradually fades out indicates to us that the story set in Spain is a set of interpretive codes for the personal philosophical dialogue between Tommy and Izzi. The conquistador Tomás is the symbolic counterpart of the Tommy who is immersed in experiments in reality; like Tommy, he takes risks to save his beloved and to be with the queen of his heart forever. To fulfill his promise, Tomás kills his rebellious subordinates, and the priest who guides him along the road to the Tree of Life also dies in the rebellion; while in reality, Tommy, disregarding the drug protocol, tests a formula derived from the mystical tree on a macaque. Both of them encounter all kinds of resistance from those around them, and both rush headlong toward their goals regardless of everything. And the macaque, as a de facto helper, faces the threat of death just like the priest. But the queen in the Spanish story is not constructed by Izzi with herself as the prototype; she is the queen imagined in Tommy’s (Tomás’s) mind — beautiful and noble, yet fragile and helpless, in need of someone to save her. In fact, she is a mental image of Izzi in his eyes, because Tommy always believes that once he accepts that ring representing true love, he has a responsibility to guard her and protect her; and when an external enemy (a virus) invades and threatens her life, finding that Tree of Life that can grant immortality is the only way. Compared with the Spanish plot, the story set deep in the galaxy is even more closely linked to Tommy’s state of mind. Tom always quietly guards the great tree, feeling her life force, and keeps telling her, “Don’t worry, we’ll be all right,” “I’ll stay by your side forever.” The director repeatedly links the scenes of reality and the space world through symbolic continuous montage — for example, through the flickering changes of light and shadow, the gently stroked tree trunk in the frame becomes Izzi’s smooth body; the tree whiskers on the trunk become the fine hairs on her skin; the golden flowing nebula becomes the circular pattern on the hospital floor; and the similar bodily movements of Tommy and Tom — turning the head, looking up, wailing — are also frequently juxtaposed in the transitions between shots. At first, the great tree’s life force is “still very strong”; after Izzi faints in the museum, the tree’s whiskers begin to droop downward; and when Izzi finally dies after resuscitation fails, the great tree also withers and dies. Obviously, the great tree here is a metaphor for Izzi’s physical condition, while the glass-ball-like star body is a metaphor for Tommy’s state of mind and thoughts. Here, Izzi seems always to be by Tom’s side, yet she never truly appears. Tom is afraid to face Izzi’s apparition, afraid that she will repeatedly remind him to finish the novel’s ending; what he has been doing all along is studying the nebula and studying how to keep the great tree alive. After the real Izzi dies, the nebula begins to gather, and the apparition beside Tom becomes Queen Isabella; like Izzi, she tells Tom, “You can free a new Spain from bondage, you can do it.” This time, Tom heeds Izzi’s words — “Let’s finish it” — and he finally leaves the sphere he has guarded for so many years to complete the final ending of his wife’s novel. And Tom vanishes into the cosmos with the great explosion of the nebula. Seen this way, the film begins with the Spanish and space plots as a kind of flashback technique, but it is more than just a narrative device. In fact, the predicaments of Tomás and Tom described at the beginning of the film are exactly the dilemma Tommy faces in reality. After enduring many hardships, Tomás finds the road to the Tree of Life, but he is stabbed by the Mayan warrior guarding the way and is at death’s door. This is the final plot point in Izzi’s novel, and also a riddle-like code she set for her husband: how it ends — whether it stops here, or he continues searching despite his wounds, or something else — is entirely for Tommy to complete. In Tom’s world, there are several voices: one is Tom’s own, saying to the great tree, “You can do it, I don’t want you to die”; another is his wife’s voice from memory, saying, “Come take a walk with me,” “The first snow has fallen”; and the third is the voice of the wife’s apparition hovering around him, saying, “Finish it!” These three voices intertwine, representing Tommy’s painful and conflicted state of mind. He longs for a miracle to happen, longs to find a cure for cancer. Yet he knows how slim that hope is; he “doesn’t know how to finish it.” He is distraught at not being able to accompany his wife to see the snow. “I’m sorry, it’s my fault” — again and again he can only express apology and guilt this way. He also wants to help his wife fulfill that dying wish. He looks at the tattoo on his finger: “All right, I believe you. Take me, guide me.” Unfortunately, Izzi left without leaving any guidance; he still has to figure it all out himself. At the end of the film, Tommy gives up the pursuit of eternity and accepts the death that humanity must inevitably face, and thus finally liberates himself from the fear of death. (2) Themes “So he drove Adam and Eve out of the Garden of Eden, and placed there the cherubim and a flaming sword turning in all directions, to guard the way to the Tree of Life.” This is the passage from Genesis in the Bible quoted at the beginning of the film; while hinting at the plot, it also tells us the main subject the film wants to discuss. From the moment Adam and Eve ate the fruit of the “tree of knowledge” (tree of knowledge, or tree of good and evil), humanity began living in a world of binary opposites: life and death, poverty and wealth, sorrow and joy, good and evil… What exactly is the meaning of life? If they had chosen not the “tree of knowledge” but the “tree of life,” what would things be like? What sets us apart from the Creator, and what makes us special? Perhaps all of this is just a process from the present to eternity. At the end of the film, Tommy finally gains the ability to conceive the novel’s ending. The guardian of the Tree of Life, at the moment he strikes, sees Adam, the “father of mankind,” and lays down the flaming sword in his hand, willing to die for his sins. Tomás gets his wish and sees the Tree of Life, yet he does not become immortal because of it; when he drinks the resin that represents infinite life force, he falls to the ground in agony, and green grass and flowers burst out from his body, burying him beside the great tree. And Tom calmly crosses the nebula to reach the center of Shibalba, turning into a speck of dust in the cosmos as the star body explodes. Judging from the story and its ending, The Fountain mainly seeks to explore views on death, and from there extends to reflections on the meaning of life. Tommy finally breaks out of that glass sphere filled with fear and avoidance, achieving a kind of spiritual transcendence. Accompanied by bright, spectacular images and fast, melodious drum music, the space traveler Tom peacefully explodes and perishes together with the Shibalba nebula; this scene, akin to a religious nirvana, actually expresses the spiritual pleasure of being forever freed from fear. And what helps Tommy achieve this liberation is precisely a renewed understanding of love and the meaning of life. At first, Tommy is fragile and sensitive inside; he doesn’t want Izzi to talk with him about anything involving death — in fact, he is afraid of losing her. So he declares war on fate, wanting to “stop aging, stop death.” He believes that to escape pain, he must conquer death; “death is a disease, and like any other disease, there is a cure,” and he wants to find it. But this defiance, or contempt, is not born of a Sisyphus-like simple perseverance and joy; it comes from subconscious helplessness and despair. As the Mayan guardian says, for him, “death is the road to fear.” Unlike Tommy, Izzi, who has suffered from illness for years, has an aestheticist interpretation of and identification with death. She tells Tommy that the golden nebula is actually a gathering of stars about to die; one day they will explode and perish, giving birth to a new star. And she has found her own place, called Shibalba, a world where dead souls can be reborn. She also tells him that, according to the Mayan creation myth, life was created by the human ancestor Adam with his own body: his body became the trunk of the great tree reaching into the earth, his soul became the branches spreading toward the sky, and Shibalba was created by his children in heaven. Of course, at the time Tommy is obsessed with the treatment and pays no attention to what his wife says. But Izzi keeps using her religious, fantastical way to help Tommy understand that life exists in more than one form, and that we are all just a tiny part of the universe. After Izzi’s condition worsens, she tells Tommy another story that a Mayan tour guide told her: after the guide’s father died, a seed was buried in his grave and grew into a great tree. The guide said his father became part of the tree, and his soul flew far away with the birds foraging for food. The film doesn’t mention the guide’s situation or the source of the story, but it’s clear that Izzi is always trying to enlighten Tommy with a cosmic way of thinking that transcends outward forms, trying to make him understand that death is not an end but a new beginning. In fact, Tommy’s final realization and transcendence come precisely from comprehending this truth. He arranges a death ending for Tomás; Tomás’s body becomes grass and flowers, but in reality he is reborn in another form. And Tom finally reaches the center of Shibalba, the place Izzi said was hers; there the nebula gathers and explodes as described before, transforming into another star, and the Tree of Life is revived. It can be said that Tommy accepts Izzi’s view of life in his mind, and thus Tom — who represents confusion and avoidance — disappears along with the rebirth of Izzi’s soul. Of course, Tommy’s realization is still the result of the true love between him and Izzi. Before Tom finally decides to break out of that glass sphere, his wife’s image keeps appearing, and Queen Isabella, who symbolizes the mirror image of Tommy’s inner self, finally stands together with Izzi’s image. It is her (their) love and trust that give Tommy the courage and strength to “finish it.” And so, when the scene that recurs throughout the film — his wife inviting him out for a walk — appears once again, he doesn’t walk toward the lab; instead he runs toward that snowy field, toward his wife, toward the “heart” of Shibalba. There, he finds the lost wedding ring and puts it on his middle finger, covering the tattooed ring carved there out of pain and out of the longing for eternity. He no longer needs to eat the bark of the great tree to overcome his fear, nor does he need to carve tree rings on his arm to travel through the pain of time, because he knows Izzi has not truly left — she will be with him forever. On the snow-white grave, we see Tommy bury a warm seed, and we believe that before long a lush great tree will surely grow there. “Farewell, Izzi.” “I’ve finished it for you.” “Are you all right?” “Yes, everything is all right.” (3) Visual Language The director conveys the theme of Tommy’s fear of death through the shifting colors of the shots. In the film, we can see the images in the shots constantly shifting between color and black-and-white, darkness and brightness. This color change is tied to the protagonist’s circumstances and state of mind. Among them, the scenes involving Tommy, Tomás, and Tom are basically shot in gloom, only bursting into bright white at the very end. And each time the shot transitions from color to black-and-white, the protagonist is almost always in a state of confusion, anxiety, or pain — for example, when Tommy returns home looking for Izzi; when the priest appears to lead Tomás on his quest for the Tree of Life; when Tommy walks from the hospital to the lab after Izzi faints; when Tom feels the great tree’s vitality declining; when Tom holds the withered tree and weeps bitterly… and so on. In contrast, the scenes involving the queen, Izzi, and her apparitions are mostly shot in fairly saturated light, and each time the male and female protagonists appear on screen together, the character played by Rachel Weisz always occupies the bright part of the frame, and the close-ups of her face are always given a soft, bright glow. Such an arrangement is obviously not arbitrary; it distinguishes two different states — on one side optimism and composure, on the other sorrow and conflict; on one side serenity and peace, on the other bewilderment and helplessness. Finally, when the two together present a dazzling brightness, it actually represents their ultimate transformation from confinement to openness, from dimness to light, from fantasy to reality.

title: Enya has a new album out too — And Winter Came
content: Enya has a new album out too — And Winter Came. Official word is that it drops on the 10th of this month. With Christmas tracks from Sarah Brightman and Enya, this winter is bound to be cozy. Definitely. And Winter Came Album: And Winter Came Artist: Enya Date: 2008.11.10 Region: Europe America Language: English Genre: New Age Album notes: Enya.com has now announced the news of Enya’s latest album. The album is titled And Winter Came and is scheduled for release on November 10, 2008. It’s a new album Enya will release on November 10, 2008, after two years of work. Originally Enya was going to make a Christmas album, but later decided to make a brand-new album instead of limiting herself to covering traditional Christmas carols. “Enya will release her brand new studio album ‘And Winter Came’ on November 10th on Warner Bros. Records. Two years in the making, ‘And Winter Came’ was recorded at Aigle Studios near Dublin and is once again the result of Enya’s longstanding creative team with producerarranger Nicky Ryan and lyricist Roma Ryan. ’I always wanted to do a Christmas album, but as we began recording I didn’t feel it was right to impose a Christmas theme on certain songs,‘ explains Enya. Says Nicky, ’We started out writing for a Christmas album, but it has evolved into more an Enya album based in a winter landscape where Christmas arrives here and there, but it would be wrong to call it an Enya Christmas album.‘ ‘And Winter Came’ is nonetheless rich in delightful festive moments.” ——ENYA.COM “Enya’s brand-new studio album And Winter Came will be released by Warner Bros. Records on November 10. Two years in the making, And Winter Came was recorded at Aigle Studios near Dublin, and it is, of course, another labor of love from Enya’s extraordinarily creative team, which has worked together for so long — besides Enya herself, it includes arrangerproducer Nicky Ryan and lyricistpoet Roma Ryan. ‘I always wanted to make a Christmas album, but when we started recording I felt that some of the songs weren’t suited to being turned into pure Christmas music,’ Enya explains. Nicky says, ‘At first we were making a Christmas album, but it later evolved into an Enya-style record themed around a winter holiday season — though it would be inappropriate to call it an Enya Christmas album.’ Of course, And Winter Came is indeed full of that warm, festive holiday atmosphere.” ——ENYA.COM Full track list: 1. title: A Winter Symphony - Sarah Brightman's New Album
content: Sarah Brightman has a new album out — A Winter Symphony! In November, Sarah releases her second album of the year, A Winter Symphony, pouring her formidable vocal technique and originality into these well-loved classics: 〈Silent Night〉, 〈Happy Christmas (War Is Over)〉 written by John Lennon and Yoko Ono, and Neil Diamond’s classic 〈I`ve Been This Way Before〉 and 〈In The Bleak Midwinter〉; plus ABBA’s rare instrumental 〈Arrival〉, for which Sarah had lyrics specially written, making it a song for the first time. The album also features two duets: one is 〈Ave Maria〉 with tenor Fernando Lima, the other is 〈Carpe Diem〉 with Greek tenor Mario Frangoulis. On top of that, Sarah also teams up with the London Symphony Orchestra and the Royal Symphony Orchestra, plus a 46-voice choir, for a lavish display of her soprano artistry. Along with the release of A Winter Symphony, Sarah is also hitting the road for a world tour — her first in four years — kicking off in Monterrey, Mexico. She’ll also play 18 shows in the US, ten in Canada and four in Mexico. These concerts carry on the grand, spectacular stage-production style of her past shows, and audiences everywhere will see brand-new, breathtaking technology along with all kinds of virtual and 360-degree stage design, giving the fans who come out a spectacle unlike anything before. The new technology used in the stage setup for this tour is extremely intricate and packed with special effects, creating a fairyland, heaven-like feeling: you see an ornate ballroom blended with a fairy-tale garden on stage, and a giant aquarium appearing right there on stage — and alongside Sarah’s beautiful singing, it satisfies the audience’s visual appetite too. In the first week after A Winter Symphony‘s release, besides immediately setting off on her world tour, Sarah will also make her big-screen debut, starring in the rock-opera film “Repo! The Genetic Opera,” alongside Paris Hilton, Paul Sorvino and others. It’s a horror musical, directed by Darren Lynn Bousman — the director of the hit thriller Saw I through III. Sarah Brightman, always one of the most creative and pioneering artists of our time, has effortlessly bridged the gap between rock, pop, Broadway and opera, captivating audiences around the world with both sound and vision, and bringing every fan under the spell of her voice and stage charisma. A limited-edition CD+DVD goes on sale November 4: CD Tracklist 1. Arrival — the title instrumental from ABBA’s 1976 album Arrival, which topped the charts in 10 countries; Sarah wrote the lyrics herself and reinterprets it 2. Colder Than Winter — US country superstar Vince Gill’s timeless 1984 classic; a heartbreaking song of lost love 3. Ave Maria (Deut with Fernando Lima) — a second tender duet with Spanish bel canto tenor Lima; flawless, pure light shining in the depths of winter 4. Silent Night — Sarah’s rendition of a well-loved classic; an unforgettable, wonderful moment 5. In The Bleak Midwinter — English composer Holst’s most moving melody; Sarah turns it into a warm blessing of true love 6. I`ve Been This Way Before — Neil Diamond’s 1974 hit; a stirring, universal sigh 7. Jesu, Joy of Man`s Desiring — Sarah’s sweet, gorgeous voice brings a new, sacred light to Bach’s classic 8. Child in a Manger — a beautiful setting of the lyrical classic 〈Morning Has Broken〉; poetry that gives hope and dawn back to the disappointed 9. I Wish It Could Be Christmas Everyday — Sarah’s joyful, upbeat performance; the perfect companion to get any party going 10. Amazing Grace — the conscience-anthem of The White Tower; Sarah delivers the ultimate, majestic version 11. Ave Maria — Sarah’s pure soprano soaring through a soothing, tender melody 12. I Believe In Father Christmas — progressive rock band Emerson, Lake Palmer’s hit single; peace and joy are everywhere for the taking 13. When A Child Is Born — a tiny star lights the way in the sky; Sarah sings the joy of new birth 14. Carpe Diem (Duet with Mario Frangoulis) — Sarah and Greek crossover bel canto tenor Mario in a heartfelt duet 15. Happy Christmas (War Is Over) — John Lennon’s 1971 anti-war classic; turning hate into love, war into peace DVD contents: ◎Sarah Brightman performing 〈Fleurs du Mal〉, 〈Symphony〉, 〈Let It Rain〉 and 〈Running〉 live in Atlanta ◎A three-minute preview of the Live in Vienna concert DVD, coming in 2009 ◎Behind-the-scenes footage from the making of A Winter Symphony ◎A collection of the latest gorgeous photos of Sarah Brightman Official page with the latest album info and samples Purchase page Note: LIMITED TIME CD PROMO: For a limited time, anyone who purchases this CD (prior to November 30, 2008) will be entered to win an autographed “Harem” photo. Promotion is exclusive to this Official Store. Anyone who buys it on this official page before November 30 will have a chance to win an autographed Harem photo! title: Jay - Capricorn Album Download Link Sharing
content: Introduction from verycd: Jay Chou’s latest 2008 magic masterpiece “Capricorn” — the ultimate showdown between magician and clown. Jay Chou makes his grand entrance in a stylish “smoky clown makeup.” Pre-orders start 924. 12 designs of the “Capricorn desk calendar” welcome 2009. The “Capricorn Cube” and more await fans’ challenge. Having recently been diving deeper and deeper into magic, Jay Chou already predicted that his new album would have something to do with magic. On October 9 he’ll release his ninth solo album, “Capricorn”! A Capricorn himself, Jay Chou conjures a new constellation in the starry sky out of notes and creativity — “Capricorn,” a mysterious sign that leaves astrologers baffled: sometimes it’s shaped like the knight on a playing card, sometimes it turns into the joker on a joker card, shifting form and musical style. The pre-order poster design for the new album uses the concept of playing cards to present the ultimate showdown between magician and clown! As soon as this poster, designed around the Jack of Spades playing card, was revealed, it struck everyone as quite fun. It symbolizes the infinite possibilities in Jay Chou’s music: sometimes, like a magician, he strives for perfection in his own music and gives off an air of mystery, and sometimes his songwriting is wildly imaginative, as playful and witty as a clown. And “playing cards” as the design theme is exactly the card magic Jay Chou is proudest of and best at lately. As for the magician-and-clown design, he said: “In movies it’s always magician versus magician. This time the poster’s theme is magician versus clown — very cool!” In fact, the new album will include a song written specifically about “magic” and another written specifically about “the clown,” and the lyrics of the two even reveal a lively back-and-forth between magician and clown. The pre-order poster already expresses that sense of a head-to-head duel. Fans have been waiting eagerly for Jay Chou’s one-album-a-year release, and even in the downturn, record store channels remain full of confidence in his new album, gearing up to welcome the pre-order campaign starting September 24. For the pre-order gifts, the label has thoughtfully rolled out two: a Rubik’s Cube and a 2009 desk calendar. Major record store channels give away the “Capricorn Cube”; 7-Eleven convenience stores give away the “Capricorn desk calendar.” Of the six faces of the “Capricorn Cube,” four feature photos of Jay Chou and two feature totem designs. The funny part is that it was originally going to be a single full face pieced together from a photo of Jay Chou’s face in a 3x3 grid, but because they worried that everyone’s Rubik’s Cube skills might not be up to it and Jay Chou’s face would end up scattered across all sides, each face’s 3x3 grid was made using nine copies of the same photo. Rubik’s Cubes have become quite popular among students lately — many students play with them on the MRT and buses, drawing everyone’s attention, which shows the cube is on a rising trend. And although Jay Chou’s magic skills have grown a lot recently, when it comes to the Rubik’s Cube he still has room to improve. Playing with the “Capricorn Cube,” he said: “This can train everyone’s IQ and reflexes. You think you can get it to the same side really fast…” And as he talked, he realized he couldn’t turn it back to the same face, so he promptly added: “Turns out it’s impossible — at times like this you just have to quickly swap in another one.” He hurriedly asked a staff member to bring a new Rubik’s Cube. He said: “‘The Capricorn Cube’ has four faces that are me. Maybe we could even hold a ‘Capricorn Cube’ speed-solving contest next — that should be a lot of fun!” On the other gift, the “Capricorn desk calendar,” you can see the 12 photos Jay Chou shot for this pre-order design, the whole thing giving off a gorgeous yet retro vibe! Dressed as a magician and a clown, he got completely carried away playing. For the magician portion, all sorts of magic props were brought in — steel rings, doves, a magic wand, coins… even a large human-sized box made an appearance. Jay Chou was like a master magician: with every object under the play of his nimble hands, every transformation was easy as pie! And to become the clown, Jay Chou truly made a grand entrance, putting on a fashion-forward version of “smoky clown makeup.” His mother, watching from the side and finding it amusing, couldn’t resist coming over during a break in the shoot to take a photo with her clown-faced son. Jay Chou mischievously put on a terrifying grimace, and his mother obligingly played along with a look of utter shock, delighted in the fright. The new album’s title, “Capricorn,” represents a constellation of music and magic. “Capricorn” carries meaning on several levels: besides the fact that Jay Chou is a Capricorn to begin with, he works magic to make his music endlessly variable. Along with one song built around the theme of “magic,” the rest of the album’s content is extremely rich, with such a variety of styles it’s dazzling! And these brand-new “masterpieces” that go beyond moving — every one of them is a brilliant “masterpiece” of his! It also lets people who love Jay Chou’s music reclassify their own star sign. The “Capricorn” album coming out October 9 will be released in two packaging versions: a “Cool Tin Box Edition” and a “Collector’s Paper Box Edition.” The “Cool Tin Box Edition” comes with a bonus Knight card sticker (usable on cards the size of an EasyCard, etc.), giving fans different collector’s options. Time Machine 10. Uncle Joker 11. title: Not Fighting Alone — the Battle for SNS in China Keeps Getting Bigger
content: Funny things keep happening. Not long ago, Qianxiang Group successfully bought Kaixin.com from 9158.com, and then quietly launched the group’s first vertical SNS community aimed specifically at white-collar workers, “Kaixin.com” (note: it’s http://www.kaixin.com/, not http://www.kaixin001.com/). In the post An SNS Bloodbath Triggered by a Single Domain Name: Qianxiang’s Version of Kaixin.com Officially Goes Live!, it says: From Facebook to Kaixin001, Qianxiang has once again copied their biggest potential competitor from top to bottom, and this time they even carried the borrow-ism mindset over to the competitor’s name and initial marketing strategy. As everyone knows, Xiaonei copied FACEBOOK and has already become the most powerful SNS in China today. That copy gave Qianxiang a taste for it. What do you do when there’s a domestic competitor? Keep copying — just copy the whole thing through and through, and don’t even spare the name. Now the world has two Kaixin.coms, and the latecomer even has the better domain name… Think about it — Qianxiang’s move is nasty and formidable at the same time… Even better: someone is now striking while the iron is hot, and along comes xiaonei001.com……. Also, I came across this article recently, and it’s well written: “A Review of Domestic SNS Sites: It’s All One Big Pot of Porridge“. Give it a read if you’re interested (original post).
