title: Starting to watch the epic fantasy: Merlin
content: Recently I started pulling down season 1 of Merlin from eMule to watch. Ugh, SGA5 is getting less and less interesting, so I just dropped it and switched to a fantasy-themed show to pass the time. Merlin is good, it’s currently airing, lots of people are downloading it, so it’ll come fast. So far I’ve found 3 versions on verycd. As for good-looking subtitles, I think the ones from YYeTs are relatively better. But I watched the first two episodes with Fengruan’s subs, so I’ll just stick with that all the way through. Introduction provided by the YYeTs review team: - O great king, the gods have granted you extraordinary wisdom and courage, raising you to heights no king of England has ever reached, letting you see the splendor and purity of this world, and letting you lead your people out of the darkness. - O great king, the goddess of the fairy realm is won over by your courage and wit; the sword is granted to you, and wherever you swing it you are invincible. - O great king, Excalibur is unstoppable, cutting through gold and jade wherever it goes. But you must remember: even a divine sword that slices iron like mud has its weakness — its scabbard, which you must never lose. In a dark cave, the young magic-bearer holds a torch, facing off against a pensive dragon; inside a castle built by the water, the physician in his chamber knits his brows; a princess in a magnificent blue dress leans against an ornate four-poster bed, consumed with worry; before the castle, a golden-haired prince in a red cloak and silver armor swings his sword, and the bearing of a king is there for all to see; in the gloomy palace, the old king’s brutality grows ever more fierce — the kingdom’s peaceful forests, clear lakes, magnificent castles, everything, dissolves into emptiness within his furrowed brow… Yes, this is the fantasy blockbuster Merlin, a fantasy drama series produced in Britain. Who says the British are stodgy? They have never lacked for wild imagination. That stammering, refined gentleman in a tall hat appears before the Queen, smiling shyly over his witty, humorous [Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland]; he bows his head and presents his new work, A Detailed Explanation of the Four Arithmetic Operations, only to find that the Queen understands nothing of the complex calculations of mathematics, so he just keeps smiling, blushing even harder. This is a much-told tale in the history of fantasy and fairy tales. Two old professors in their sixties, in a pub by the university, each scribbling on a blank sheet of paper, talking about the ideas in their heads — those two sheets of paper later raised the curtain on a new chapter of fantasy in the literary history of Britain and of the world. One of the two old professors was named Tolkien, who wrote the Lord of the Rings trilogy; the other was named Lewis, who wrote the Chronicles of Narnia. The sheets of paper filled with ideas in that pub became a scene worth remembering in literary history. Rings, halflings, elves, princes, and lions and witches — all have become part of the magical adventures Britain has given the world. And now Arthur, the king with the strongest mystico-religious aura, has been brought to the screen as well. Aided by a sorcerer, helped by the fairy goddess, wielding a divine sword, he makes enemies flee at the mere rumor of his coming. Only this time, we’re not just watching the king; we also get to see that spirited young magic-bearer — it is his hand that changes the fate of the young prince. Because of him, the fate of the whole kingdom is transformed; you could say the sorcerer Merlin is the lever that pries up the kingdom. On screen, the young sorcerer Merlin finally makes his entrance: red collar, blue robe, deep gaze, arms outstretched toward the distance. At this point in his youth, he is driven only by his own ideals — because his ideals are bound up with the prince’s ideals, and with the kingdom’s. He is an indispensable arm in a golden age. Merlin, the greatest sorcerer of Arthur’s time, now comes to the small screen this autumn to spend the most memorable morning hours with each and every one of you at your computer. So let’s look through the sorcerer’s eyes at the great age inaugurated by England’s wise king; in these turbulent times, you will see unforgettable people and events. On September 21, 2008, we all look forward to Merlin’s magical journey together! Introduction provided by 星辰, 晓贝紫, 却舞, Radio4, and 雨潇@FRNEWS: This series is adapted from the story of King Arthur and the sorcerer Merlin. Unlike the legend, Merlin in this series is no longer a white-haired old man but a fledgling youth; the story focuses on how the young Merlin comes to understand his mission, turns an enemy into a friend in Prince Arthur, and saves the world of magic. As the plot unfolds, legendary figures such as the Knights of the Round Table and the Lady of the Lake will appear one by one. In March 2008, Merlin began filming in Wales and France. Co-produced by BBC Wales and the production company Shine, its executive producer Julie Gardner previously worked on the classic BBC sci-fi series Doctor Who. The series has 13 episodes, premieres in the UK on September 21, 2008, and will air on NBC in the US next year. A few other introductions: =This introduction comes from 破烂熊 These old stories are etched in our minds: King Arthur, the Sword in the Stone, the Knights of the Round Table… And how was each of these legends forged? The key figure is the famous sorcerer and prophet — Merlin. This time there is no white-haired, long-bearded sage; BBC Wales, the team behind such fine productions as Doctor Who and Life on Mars, takes us back to the little-known youth of the legendary sorcerer Merlin. This thirteen-episode fantasy production sets its story in the ancient city of Camelot, a world of magic where the tyrant Uther forbids people to practice sorcery. Young Merlin, though he has already mastered magic, can only keep it hidden as a secret. Hot-blooded, he comes to Camelot to temper himself, and there he meets Arthur, still a prince. Merlin could never imagine that this is the master he will one day help become king; the two young men go from stumbling friction to inseparability, fighting side by side against their enemies, walking their fated path and forging a legend of medieval myth. =The following introduction comes from 天涯小筑 NBC has decided to pick up the historical-mythological legend “Merlin the Great Sorcerer” adapted by the British BBC — how surprising and delightful. Many people must have heard of “Merlin”, along with “King Arthur”, “Lancelot”, “the Knights of the Round Table”, “Camelot”, “Avalon”, “the Lady of the Lake” and “Morgan le Fay” — famous figures from English historical legend. This new Merlin will interpret the traditional story from a distinctly modern perspective. It is set in the legendary holy city of Camelot (Camelot, the fabled site of King Arthur’s court), and the story takes place before Merlin and Arthur became legendary figures. At that time they were just ambitious young men, eager to explore the wider world, eager to win their families’ recognition, eager for beautiful romance, eager to realize their ideals, eager to explore their future destiny. They were green and inexperienced, and they stumbled over many things. The young, hot-headed Merlin does not treat Arthur as a supreme master, and the two often clash. According to NBC’s description, this is an “innovative”, “groundbreaking”, “gripping” action drama. It depicts something TV audiences are familiar with but have never seen before — the early lives of Merlin and Arthur. BBC’s ability to adapt and remake historical drama is plain for all to see; in recent years it has successively remade Jane Eyre, Oliver Twist, Pride and Prejudice and Robin Hood, and adapted Bleak House, Sense and Sensibility and many other series. But these are mostly faithful to the original works, or to the traditional stories people generally accept. Merlin is the exception — it has almost nothing to do with the white-bearded old sage in our heads. Is this change a good thing or a bad thing? Time will tell. = Yesterday’s Bionic Woman, Today’s Evil Sorceress — Merlin Begins Filming ◆ Author donatino ◆ Category Important US TV News, TV Series Merlin ◆ Date 2008-07-23 After lying low for quite a while, Michelle Ryan, formerly the star of “Bionic Woman”, has taken a role in the much-watched BBC mythological drama — Merlin. Unlike her “righteous through and through” image in Bionic Woman, this time her character is the evil sorceress Nimueh. Fate works in strange ways: after Bionic Woman was cancelled by NBC, a heartbroken, frustrated Michelle Ryan (related report) went all the way around in a big circle and ended up back in NBC’s arms — NBC had announced as early as last summer that it had picked up this BBC One series, and would air it at a suitable time next spring. The production has kept things fairly well under wraps — this is the first news about the series in months. Besides Michelle Ryan, the latest additions to the cast are John Hurt and Santiago Cabrera. John Hurt will voice Merlin’s mentor, the “Great Dragon”, while Santiago Cabrera, who played Isaac Mendez in Heroes, will play the famous leader of the Knights of the Round Table, Lancelot. Another cast member is Katie McGrath (“The Tudors”), whose role is unknown. Earlier this year the production announced that Northern Irish screen newcomer and 22-year-old Colin Morgan (“Doctor Who”, “Catherine Tate Show”) would play the lead, Merlin; Bradley James would play Arthur; Anthony Head (“Buffy the Vampire Slayer”) would play Arthur’s father, King Uther (Uther Pendragon); Richard Wilson (“A Passage to India”, “One Foot in the Grave”) would play the court physician Gaius; and Angel Coulby would play Guinevere, the queen who comes between Arthur and Lancelot. This 13-episode series tells of the early friendship between the great sorcerer Merlin and Arthur (as a prince). If you’re unfamiliar with the show, you can check out the earlier introduction: http://donatino.skygate.cn/post/21/2441. The series will first air on BBC One this September, in the Saturday-night slot — that is, Doctor Who’s slot. One can predict that the show, like Doctor Who, will suit all ages and won’t have too much adult material. The visual effects are handled by The Mill, the studio behind Doctor Who and the film Gladiator, which has won the Oscar for Best Visual Effects. title: Spore! Spore!
content: The game I’ve been waiting for — one that breaks the mold — has finally been discovered! Wow — simulationcreature-raising + first-person role-playing + strategy + management + sci-fi! From a single-celled organism all the way up to galactic overlord! Whenever I play a strategy game, I never get to enjoy the harmonious economic growth that comes after world peace in the late game; when I play a management sim, there’s no military element; and a first-person RPG lacks the big-picture feel. Once you get bored with a few things, you discover that combining them creates something else entirely — something fresh and exciting. It’s so thrilling — I no longer have to fool myself into building cities in RN or Generals, and I don’t have to scheme about building military bases to expand in SimCity… By pure chance I came across EA’s Spore, and it was love at first sight — I only wish I’d found it sooner. From a first look at the intro, this game blends elements from a lot of games. In it, your little creature goes through 6 stages (if you don’t like subjective takes, feel free to scroll past). The first two stages are a bit more primitive, mostly RPG and action elements. The tribal stage kicks off clan communes… then comes the city stage, which maybe feels a bit like Beautiful Genesis… then the civilization stage, where you’re basically playing Rise of Nations… and finally the space stage: Homeworld + Sins of a Solar Empire… Awesome. A game where you can free-form it from so many angles — hehe, that’s enough to keep me hooked for quite a while. Hey, Raccoon, Old Ox, all of you — come give it a try already. The trailer music is actually from SimCity 4… This game does have its flaws: by today’s standards the visuals really aren’t much, and some online critics say it’s not as perfect as you’d imagine… Whatever — everyone forms their own opinion once they play it. I’m off to download the demo. Official screenshots: http://www.ea.com.cn/zh-cn/games/pc/spore/spore/screenshots/ Official description of the game’s features: Fully control your creature’s fate and guide it through six stages of evolution: Ocean stage: Compete with other creatures and absorb them to adjust your creature’s form. This is the period of fighting for survival under the microscope. Creature stage: Venture onto land and teach your creature how to survive and develop in a world beyond your safe haven. Herbivore or carnivore? Social or solitary? The choice is yours. Tribal stage: You no longer control a single creature, but an entire tribe made up of creatures you’ve created. You can hand them tools and guide their interactions, gradually letting them develop and evolve. City stage: Lead your species into a golden age, develop technology for them, build, and complete their cities. Civilization stage: Once your cities are established, your creatures will start looking for opportunities to make contact with other civilizations. You can have them do so through war or peace; the ultimate goal is for your species to rule the planet. Space stage: It’s time to move to other bodies in your star system. Make quick contact, colonize, or relocate entirely, then head further out into the vast universe in search of other star systems. A new “mission” mode will accompany your expansion and development across the cosmos. A set of flexible, intuitive tools to spark the player’s creative imagination. Creating a universe full of animals, plants, buildings, vehicles, and planets will be incredibly simple and fun. From the very start, the game is full of endless design possibilities. The worlds you explore are full of life, plants, buildings, and vehicles, all created by other players and downloaded through a central database. The server selects the creatures and civilizations that suit you best based on the environment you choose, your experience level, and your creature’s abilities. At the same time, your creatures will be uploaded to the server to share with others. In the game, your creatures and vehicles are generated based on your designs, and their actions and interactions depend on your designs and your encounters in-game. That means the game doesn’t set a fixed path of development for you. Imagine the attitude other players have when they create creatures and evolve them. Discover the original, primitive information of various creatures in the Sporepedia, and learn about that creature’s evolutionary journey in Spore in another way. Sept 25 update: I spent 3 hours playing today and got to the tribal stage. Seeing an ocean creature gradually become an intelligent land creature does give you a certain sense of achievement ^_^ This game’s concept is excellent and its subject matter is grand — it tells the evolutionary history of a species in some star system. Too bad the visuals are so childish (I can’t think of a more fitting word for it), and just like SimCity Societies, playing it makes me dizzy… Found an interesting detail: in the second stage, at night you might see a high-tech alien spaceship come visit your planet, so be careful it doesn’t suck you up… PS: If only MS had developed a game with this kind of subject matter.

title: Hadron Collider Starts Today — Intel Gathering
content: Modern Express: Hadron Collider Starts at 15:30 Today, Unraveling the Mystery of the Universe’s Birth: According to PhysOrg, the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiment is the most complex scientific experiment ever conducted, and its main purpose is to unravel the mystery of the universe’s birth. With the goal of filling in the gaps in our understanding of the universe, subatomic particles will be accelerated to near the speed of light and then made to collide. Beyond that, the collision experiment may also verify some novel theories about space-time and answer the question of whether another dimension exists. After nearly 20 years of effort and 6 billion Swiss francs, 5,000 scientists, engineers and technicians from dozens of countries are turning this enormous project into reality. At 7:30 GMT on the 10th (15:30 Beijing time on the 10th), the first protons will be injected into a 27-kilometer ring-shaped tunnel spanning the Swiss-French border. CERN (the European Organization for Nuclear Research) headquarters is also located on the Swiss-French border. As the first step in a long-term experiment, the beam of subatomic particles will be accelerated to near the speed of light and then collide, with the impact producing, in a tiny space, a brief temperature 100,000 times that of the sun. Analysts will closely monitor the entire collision process in search of fundamental particles. “We are entering a whole new realm of physics,” said Peter Jenni, spokesperson for ATLAS (short for A Toroidal LHC ApparatuS). “The 10th is a very important milestone.” ATLAS is one of four huge laboratories installed on the ring tunnel. Detectors attached around the tunnel will monitor the collision process. In an experiment lasting 10 hours, the particle beams may travel more than 10 billion kilometers, enough for a round trip between Earth and Neptune. At maximum intensity, each beam carries energy equivalent to that of a car traveling at 1,600 kilometers per hour. The Large Hadron Collider will consume 120 megawatts of electricity, equivalent to the power consumption of every household in Geneva. Two Hypotheses The Doomsday Nightmare Some scientists worry that great caution is warranted when it comes to starting the hadron collider. In fact, ever since the multinational construction of the Large Hadron Collider began in 1994, some doomsayers have alarmingly claimed that “reproducing” the universe’s initial state after the Big Bang some 13.7 billion years ago would lead to a catastrophe. Not long ago, a small group of dissenting scientists filed a lawsuit with the European Court of Human Rights. They argue that while the probability of the Large Hadron Collider experiment producing a mini black hole is very small, that possibility does not equal zero. Once a black hole forms, Earth would face being swallowed. Others go further, claiming that the consequences would be far more than just a black hole — the collision experiment could trigger a catastrophic chain reaction in the structure of space-time, tearing the entire universe to shreds. To that end, they put forward two terrifying hypotheses. First hypothesis: We would see no warning at all; within perhaps less than a month, all life on Earth would suddenly come to an end. After that, terrifying earthquakes would erupt suddenly, sea levels would rise rapidly, and super tsunamis would strike coastlines around the world. In the end, the apocalypse described in the Bible would descend upon humanity, and the entire Earth would be destroyed. The second doomsday hypothesis is even more terrifying: without any warning whatsoever, in roughly one-twelfth of a second the entire Earth would vanish into space. In less than two seconds, the Moon would follow Earth. Eight minutes later, the Sun would be split in two. After that, the same fate would befall the other planets in the solar system. More seriously, the massive destruction caused by cracks in the fabric of space would spread outward at the speed of light, and every world beyond Earth would meet its end. Four Reasons It Won’t Destroy Earth “The Large Hadron Collider experiment could destroy Earth” — headlines like that may help sell newspapers, but the media has paid no attention to the truth, and has even deliberately ignored important details. The scientists in charge of the collision experiment explain: first, nature can produce subatomic particles with even higher energies than those the Large Hadron Collider generates in the form of cosmic rays. For billions of years, they have rained down on Earth in huge numbers — and yet here we still are on Earth, still writing stories about them? Second, these mini black holes aren’t just small black holes — they are actually only subatomic in size, roughly the size of an electron or a proton. If the Large Hadron Collider ran for a hundred years, all the energy these particles produce still wouldn’t be enough to light a single light bulb. Although the subatomic particles produced by the Large Hadron Collider can reach trillions of electron volts, the maximum rate at which it could produce mini black holes might be one per second, and such a tiny rate couldn’t cause any perceptible harm to anyone. Third, these mini black holes are extremely unstable and would collapse very quickly. In fact, these black holes go in the opposite direction — they emit radiation, so they ultimately disappear without a trace, rather than continuously swallowing matter, growing larger and larger, and finally devouring Earth. Fourth, according to Werner Heisenberg’s “uncertainty principle,” anything has some tiny possibility of happening — it’s just that the probability of such a thing happening is extremely small, perhaps so small that it won’t happen in the entire lifetime of the universe. Of course, some experts also argue that if something is so extremely rare that it might never happen in the entire lifetime of the universe, physicists should tell the media that such a thing won’t happen. Related Producing a Host of Valuable Byproducts This grand scientific experiment will also yield some amazing byproducts, such as improved cancer treatment, ways to destroy nuclear waste, and help for scientists studying climate change. Over the course of a year, the two proton beams in this machine will collide at high speed, generating enough data to fill 5.6 million CDs. That means physicists have to develop a complex, sophisticated system for processing information quickly. What they call the Grid may become a model for many other systems used to handle massive amounts of data. The findings of another project suggest that new ways of dealing with nuclear waste could be found in these collisions. Scientists at the European Organization for Nuclear Research have discovered that firing a proton beam (one kind of subatomic particle) into a lead plate produces a large number of neutrons (another kind of subatomic particle), and these neutrons can break radioactive waste down into harmless, stable elements. In addition, the European Organization for Nuclear Research has also contributed to medical research, because they discovered that beams of charged particles such as protons, carbon ions and even antimatter can be used to treat cancer. Cloud formation is a crucial factor for climate and weather, and this research could put the European Organization for Nuclear Research at the center of a debate over whether factors other than greenhouse gases are linked to climate change. Researchers will use a proton beam from the Proton Synchrotron to simulate cosmic rays, firing them into a so-called “cloud chamber” to see whether small patches of cloud form. Starting today, scientists will find out whether the enormous sums spent building the Large Hadron Collider were really worth it. Sidelights The Experiment Was Turned Into a Rap Song The Large Hadron Collider experiment may be making some people fear for the world’s future, but what nobody expected is that someone actually turned the collision experiment into a rap song, making the seemingly impossible marriage of a physics experiment and music a reality. This rap song was written and performed by 23-year-old Kate McAlpine. McAlpine works in the press office of the CERN laboratory. Rap songs often deal with themes like violence and crime, and rarely have anything to do with high-energy particle physics. In that sense, McAlpine’s act is quite unconventional. One verse of the rap goes like this: “Two protons spinning through the ring until they reach the detector’s heart and then collide all the energy gathered in that tiny space becomes mass and creates particles in the vacuum.” CERN spokesperson James Gillies said: “We love this rap song. Physics can also find its place in the music world.” McAlpine was given permission to film herself and her friends dancing in the huge cavern and tunnels where the collision experiment will take place. Simulation animation of the Hadron Collider’s Big Bang experiment: The rap mentioned above — staff rap to showcase the European Hadron Collider: Physicists from various countries predict the outcome of the Large Hadron Collider experiment: Hawking bets $100: the collider will not find the God particle According to foreign media reports, the Large Hadron Collider was designed to unlock the mystery of the universe’s birth by launching the largest-scale research in human history. But can it reveal why most subatomic particles have mass — which may signal the existence of the Higgs particle? Can this massive experiment uncover why the Creator favored matter and slighted antimatter? Can it overturn our current understanding of fundamental particles and forces? The Daily Telegraph interviewed several of the world’s leading theoretical physicists, asking them to lay out their predictions for the collider’s results. Prediction of Nima Arkani-Hamed of the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, USA I’m betting a year’s salary that they will find the Higgs particle. They are also quite likely to observe the particles that make up the mysterious dark matter in the universe. This kind of dark matter may or may not be related to supersymmetry. I think there is a fairly high probability that the Large Hadron Collider will reveal supersymmetry. It would explain beautifully why gravity appears so weak compared with the other fundamental forces. The Large Hadron Collider experiments may also tell us that our existing ideas about what nature is made of are simply incorrect. Prediction of Nobel laureate Martinus Veltman of Utrecht University, the Netherlands I won’t be surprised if this experiment finds no Higgs particle, because I don’t believe in Higgs theory. But if a Higgs particle is found, it will be crucial to test whether it matches theoretical predictions. I would be surprised if supersymmetry is found. I was very supportive when the theory was first proposed, but now I’ve gradually lost faith in it — perhaps I’m wrong. Of course, if the Large Hadron Collider finds no evidence supporting supersymmetry, its supporters will still make excuses and keep clinging to the theory. As for string theory, that’s meaningless talk with no connection to experiment. Prediction of Eva Silverstein of Stanford University, USA I would be very surprised if no Higgs particle is found, but if they don’t find evidence of supersymmetry, that’s fine too. Some of my views come from string theory, which holds great promise as a theory unifying the forces of nature. According to many — or most — string theories, supersymmetry is not operative at the energies the Large Hadron Collider explores. So its discovery might require further explanation of this view. On the other hand, supersymmetry fits very well with some existing observations. The final revelation of whether it exists will be something to look forward to. Prediction of John March-Russell of Oxford University Unlike the general predictions about the Large Hadron Collider’s results, some possible discoveries could even lead to technological change. For example, the answer to the question of where favorable climate energy comes from may be related to the formation of unstable but fairly long-lived exotic charged particles. Like the biochemical enzymes in the body that promote chemical reactions, these exotic particles could efficiently catalyze nuclear fusion without the extremely high temperatures that plasma fusion reactors and stars normally require. The results might also reveal that the number of space-time dimensions is ambiguous, resembling more an ordinary hologram in which two and three dimensions coexist. Prediction of Chris Llewellyn Smith, director of the UK Atomic Energy Authority at Culham and director-general of CERN from 1994 to 1999 I think both the Higgs boson and supersymmetry will be found — the former with 95% probability, the latter with 60%. As for new discoveries of exotic particles, I’d put the probability at only 5%. If the Large Hadron Collider produces no new discoveries (which I think has a 5% probability), I’ll feel a little embarrassed, since I spent years of my life on it. Finding nothing would also be surprising and would force people to rethink, but if the collider can lead to further new discoveries, that would be the most exciting outcome of all. Prediction of Garrett Lisi, the physicist who proposed a new superstring theory and is known as the “surfing fanatic” The most likely result of the Large Hadron Collider is the discovery of a Higgs particle. The Higgs particle has to break the unified symmetry of the electroweak force, leading to the separated electromagnetic and weak forces we see. Many physicists also think this experiment may find supersymmetry, strings or new dimensions, but I don’t think so. If the Large Hadron Collider really does find many new particles, my guess is that they are just several different kinds of Higgs particles. Whatever the result, it’s exciting that nature’s beauty can be revealed at such a tiny scale.” Related topics: http://news.xinhuanet.com/tech/2008-09/09/content_9867754.htm

title: GTA's recent nonsense. Are crime games good or bad?
content: Ever since GTA took the world by storm, plenty of teenagers have drawn some pretty unbelievable criminal inspiration from it. Juvenile crime has clearly been giving the authorities a headache in recent years, and last month Thailand’s Ministry of Public Health put it on its list of dangerous goods. -_-! The list of the 10 most dangerous games: GTA (Grand Theft Auto) Man Hunt (Manhunt) Scarface 50 Cent - Bulletproof 300 The Godfather Killer 7 Resident Evil 4 God of War Hitman So it seems that in some people’s eyes, playing crime games means you’re highly likely to go out and commit crimes. Only a few days after I read those reports about Thailand banning GTA, I came across another report saying the exact opposite. According to a recent story in the Ottawa Times Weekly, an 11-year-old GTA4 player helped her family escape a car explosion in a crash — and she says the know-how came from playing GTA4. When the Jeep carrying the five members of the Norris family was in a crash on the highway, it spun out of control, hit the guardrail and rolled over four times before it finally came to a stop. The vehicle was badly wrecked, and the Norris couple in the front seats were seriously injured in the impact. Their 11-year-old daughter, Audrey Plique, bravely climbed out of the window and helped her parents and siblings escape the car, which could have exploded at any moment… Afterwards she told reporters that her bravery and clearheadedness were thanks to Grand Theft Auto. “She knew exactly what to do, from playing Grand Theft Auto,” Plique’s mother, Karen Norris, told reporters. “She’d seen (in the game) cars crash and roll over and then explode, so she knew exactly what danger we were facing.” This almost unbelievable story was quickly picked up and reported by major US media outlets. Clearly, while the Grand Theft Auto series is easily tied to all kinds of crime, it can also awaken heroic qualities in an 11-year-old girl. Of course, it’s not hard to imagine that many staunch opponents of violent video games would still rather believe in the vicious-circle theory that “violent games create violent teenagers who breed violent crime.” But at least this time, Plique’s heroism can remind us that, used well, video games can benefit us too. -— http://cn.gamers.com/_newsforwardShowNewsArticle.php?newsid6394 See? No matter what kind of game it is, if you can learn a lot from it, it isn’t necessarily a bad thing. These games are a double-edged sword. In real life, those who mean well take the good and leave the bad; those who mean ill, being of unsound mind, get led astray. The key lies in the individual, not the game. An outright ban doesn’t seem very meaningful to me — why not guide people properly instead? Playing GTA is more like watching a big-budget cops-and-robbers movie; there’s no need to copy the protagonist and go commit crimes.

title: Q4, waiting for GTA4
content: According to official news: the PC version of Grand Theft Auto IV will go on sale in North America on November 18, while the European release date is November 21. Back in the SA era, the whole Grand Theft Auto experience leveled up a notch. Tons of hardcore, offbeat playstyles popped up. I remember watching “Grand Theft Auto Multiplayer Blockbuster Series: Deadly Flight” — haha, the plot rips off Con Air. I am very very very very very very very very very very much looking forward to the new GTA — GTA4. Oh yeah — my rig can barely keep up… The fourth game is way more realistic: Hand-to-hand combat is genuinely hard. Don’t go picking fights in the street if you don’t have a gun. One time I attacked a woman and three guys came to her rescue and beat me to death. 2. I’ve been flung out through the windshield on impact in a crash more than once. 3. Maybe it’s because I’m not used to the gamepad, but the cars are harder to drive this time — more realistic. 4. Motorcycles are seriously dangerous. One time I crashed and NIKO flew a whole street’s length, then hit the ground and splattered blood everywhere… 5. Always watch for cars when you cross the road! Otherwise 8 out of 10 will hit you — they just can’t brake in time. Once, during a mission, I ran out onto the road to find a car and an NPC following me got hit and killed by a car. Mission failed. 6. Getting a hooker works the same as in the previous games, but this time there are three services at different prices, and you can see the actual action inside the car! 7. The cops are seriously persistent. One mission ended with me having to break out of a building while at 3 stars. Total headache. 8. Once I got into a fight on the street and jumped into a car to run. I floored it just as the guy was opening my door, and he ended up hanging onto the door handle, getting dragged along. Thinking fast, I swerved past an oncoming car — there was a bang, a cloud of blood, and the guy was gone… 9. After you shoot a driver dead from outside the car, the windshield gets covered in blood and the driver’s head presses down on the horn, which blares on and on… 10. This time, when a car is badly damaged it usually just stalls, but once my car shot flames out from both sides of the rear wheels and then exploded… 11. The explosion effects for grenades and rocket launchers are gorgeous. Once my rocket exploded behind an enemy and he flew toward me, sailed right past me, with chunks of brick and stone landing behind me. 12. When you drive across the big bridge you have to queue up and pay at the toll booth. Run through it and you get 1 star… 13. After stealing a police car, logging into the police database from the onboard computer is a really creative touch. 14. Gunfights this time really do feel like a Hollywood blockbuster. The motion blur when you switch targets is great. Once NIKO pulled off a slick slide when switching cover. 15. Characters in the game sometimes ask NIKO out for a drink. He gets drunk every single time — staggering all over the place when walking, and driving? Don’t even mention it. ——http://www.kpsky.cn/show/197.html Not only did they put plenty of work into the graphics and greatly improve the realism, GTA4 also has multiplayer! See the official site. Hehe, there are several modes: Team play: everyone on your own team is a comrade. Go to war with the other gangs! Mode name Team Deathmatch — team deathmatch. Player count: 2-8 teams allowed. Victory condition: the team of players with the most money when the game ends wins. Rules: Players form teams and fight other teams. You get money for killing opponents — and whatever you do, don’t forget to pick up the money they drop when they die. Mode name Team Mafiya Work — team gang jobs. Player count: 2-8 teams allowed. Victory condition: the team of players with the most money when the game ends wins. Rules: In the game, Kenny Petrovic calls everyone to tell them the objective (unlike single player, you don’t pull out a phone and slow-walk here — so it’s more like a broadcast). Teams cooperate to complete gang jobs. These cover all kinds of conditions: killing people, stealing cars, delivering goods, etc. Cooperation is crucial! Several teams may go after the same target at the same time, and when that happens you have to try to kill the key target or ultimately accomplish the objective. Mode name Team Car Jack City — team car jacking. Player count: 2-8 teams allowed. Victory condition: the team of players with the most money when the game ends wins. Rules: Target cars respawn at several fixed locations on the map. Players need to work as a team: steal the car and drive it to the drop-off point (DROP-OFF POINT). The parking spots are usually guarded by a few NPCs, who are easy to take out. The amount of money players get for delivering a car depends on how damaged it is. If it’s badly wrecked, you get very little. There are also special vehicles in the game, and these cars are carrying drugs (DRUGS). Handing over a car with drugs gets you $1500, regardless of how damaged the car is. Green square: ordinary car Green square with an arrow: car carrying drugs (all green squares show an arrow before they enter the player’s field of view; you only find out whether one really has drugs once you get close) Yellow square: drop-off point PS: Besides team modes, Deathmatch, Mafiya Work and Car Jack City also have solo modes with basically the same rules, except each player is their own team and has no teammates. Mode name Cops n’ Crooks — cops and robbers. Player count: only 2 teams allowed. Rules: one team plays the gang, one team plays the cops. The cops can see the gang’s position on the GPS map, while the gang can’t see the cops. And the cops start the game riding in police cars. There are two sub-modes: ALL FOR ONE: When the game starts, one random member of the gang becomes the BOSS, marked with a star above his head, while everyone else is a circle. The team has to work together to protect the BOSS, and the cops’ goal is to kill the gang’s BOSS. The gang has to protect the BOSS until he reaches the designated spot and escapes by car. Everyone except the BOSS can respawn. ONE FOR ALL: There’s no BOSS. The cops win by killing all the crooks or destroying the getaway vehicles. (Of course, only the dead can get into these two escape vehicles.) Players can’t respawn in this mode. Mode name Turf War — turf war. Player count: 2-8 teams allowed. Victory condition: the team of players with the most money when the game ends wins. Rules: Basically the same as the capture-the-turf modes in other games. There are several bases in different locations, and players need to go stand inside the ring for a certain amount of time; once the capture meter hits 100%, the turf is successfully captured (the more people, the less time it takes). A team that holds turf starts gaining money as time passes (the more turf you hold, the faster it adds up). Players can take back turf that the other side has captured. You can’t capture turf while an opponent is near its ring — you have to kill the enemy first. Co-op mode: all players in the game are on the same side … Solo competition — win the match through your own efforts … Racing — saves you from having to install Need for Speed … PARTY mode: this mode is basically just going in and letting the host switch to any other mode at any time. Reading the intro to multiplayer battles, I really can’t wait～

June 7, 2008, Taipei Arena, 12,067 seats — not a single one empty Before that night, it was the first half of your life and the first half of mine After that night, it was the whole life of the two of us… Fish Leong [Today Is Valentine’s Day] New Songs + LIVE CD If we can be together, I will remember that today is Valentine’s Day. [I Love You] LOVE CD x1 Five brand-new love songs + twelve deeply remembered ones 17 volumes, our diary from now on, recording each other’s soul and breath 〈2008.6.7 Fish Leong [Today Is Valentine’s Day] @Taipei Arena〉 A Valentine’s night exclusively for [Leong-style love songs] The day Fish Leong stands on stage and sings is the Today Is Valentine’s Day that belongs exclusively to all lovers. On June 7, 2008, Fish Leong stepped onto the stage of Taipei Arena for the first time, and all 12,067 seats were filled. The concert ran for more than three hours, and the rich set list was so good nobody wanted it to end; in the end, at fans’ insistent demands, the on-the-spot request segment was extended without limit, with more than 40 songs performed, and both the performers and the audience were thoroughly delighted. That night, amid the sweet, soft lilt of Leong-style love songs, countless pairs of hands in the audience were clasped tight, holding fast to each other’s love and warmth; pairs of eyes gazing up with deep affection shone with the light of happiness in the darkness; every kiss that couples couldn’t help but share was dotted through the concert’s shifting, kaleidoscopic moods. 〈Courage〉〈If One Day〉〈Unconditionally for You〉〈Happy Breaking Up〉〈Grown Up Overnight〉〈Warm〉〈Ningxia〉〈Too Bad It’s Not You〉〈Worship〉〈The Pain That Breathes〉〈Silk Road〉〈I Like〉〈Swallowtail Butterfly〉〈Little Hand in Big Hand〉〈Kiss Kiss〉〈The World I Most Want to Travel Around〉 Snuggling up with the one you love beside you and taking in a Fish Leong concert can always become an unforgettable memory in the course of a romance. No other voice can give us so much courage to love; No other blessing can compare to the truth and purity in Fish Leong’s singing. In response to the strong demands of tens of thousands of fans, B’in Music is releasing a complete live recording of the whole concert as a LIVE CD, capturing nearly the entire show 100% unadulterated, and sincerely adding 5 brand-new songs that portray the “five stages of love,” as a thank-you to fans for their love of Leong-style love songs. Fish Leong’s Taipei Arena debut had a total production cost of 20 million. B’in Music painstakingly built a stage worthy of the aura of the queen of love songs: 36 dazzling crystal ornaments, luxurious and glittering; an extra-large white lift screen in front of the stage, 25 meters long and 13 meters tall, projecting images with a special H25 high-magnification projector; at the opening, Fish Leong stood on a high platform as it rose, and a single song, 〈Worship〉, captured the audience’s hearts. The concert was full of ingenious touches, including a stunning aerial “duo red silk” dance, Chaplin-style mime performances matched to the mood of the songs, and Fish Leong riding a little steam train around the whole Taipei Arena — all worth savoring again and again. Musically, besides the excellent Malaysian musicians led by veteran musician Mac Chew, there was also a majestic live string orchestra surrounding her, with musicality that knows no bounds and flows at ease. As for the set list, in addition to more than 30 well-known love songs from Fish Leong’s own ten years since debuting and nine albums, she also performed live many songs by the kings and queens of pop that she admires, including Jody Chiang’s 〈Silent Flower〉, Faye Wong’s 〈Red Bean〉, A-Mei’s 〈Remember〉, Jacky Cheung’s 〈Love Letter〉, David Tao’s 〈Love Is Simple〉, Karen Mok’s 〈Let’s Fall in Love〉, Mayday’s 〈Contentment〉 and more. Fish Leong’s good friend Tanya Chua, who had just won Best Female Vocalist at this year’s Golden Melody Awards, also came to sing 〈Premonition of Happiness〉 with her. All of these will be included in full on the [Today Is Valentine’s Day] LIVE CD, sealing in one perfect memory. This is an era short on eternal songs, an era that needs Fish Leong’s voice. Whether they are other people’s songs or her own, Fish Leong’s wonderful voice leaves us forever the best songs of this era. We seem to live in an era lacking “eternal songs,” and we often feel that old songs are still the most enduring and the best at conveying deep feelings. Fish Leong’s singing is natural and effortless, blending sweet and sour emotions, and it can always bring people warmth and clarity. To have good songs sung for us by such a voice, and to leave the sound of classic songs behind in a concert — that must be happiness. The [Today Is Valentine’s Day] LIVE CD places special emphasis on the songs by beloved kings and queens of pop that Fish Leong performed (〈Silent Flower〉, 〈Red Bean〉, 〈Love Letter〉, 〈Love Is Simple〉, and more). Each one is a classic love song, and each has brought countless people the beauty and courage of love. Fish Leong sang these songs at her concert not only because hers is a concert that performs love, singing the best love songs for her fans, but also because her wonderful voice can give the classics a different kind of emotion. Five brand-new songs sincerely included, portraying the five stages of love — secret crush, first love, passionate love, bitter love, broken heart Besides the songs performed live at Taipei Arena, as a thank-you to fans, the [Today Is Valentine’s Day] LIVE CD also sincerely includes five brand-new Fish Leong songs, ingeniously portraying the five stages of love — secret crush, first love, passionate love, bitter love, broken heart. In order, they are: 〈If We Could Be Together〉, 〈Today Is Valentine’s Day〉, 〈Full of Love〉, 〈I Decide〉, 〈Let’s Stop Here〉. Every feeling of love — sweet and sour, bitter and spicy, and the bitterness and sweetness known to no one else — is gathered in these five songs, worth savoring slowly. Among them, 〈Today Is Valentine’s Day〉 is the 1,000th lyric by the famous lyricist Yao Ruolong, the “god of love poems,” and we are extremely honored to include it on this Fish Leong album; having the queen of love songs, Fish Leong, deliver this deeply meaningful work with true feeling could not be more fitting.

title: Recommended: Beijing 2008 Olympic Games Songs Album
content: I’ve been listening to this Beijing 2008 Olympic songs album lately — it’s well worth keeping. Album track list: CD 1 Beijing Welcomes You - Various Artists 02. One World One Dream - Wang Leehom 05. One World One Dream - Liu Huan Na Ying 06. Our Dream - Wang Feng 07. Glory - Guo Rong 08. Fly Together - Tan Jing Yan Weiwen 09. The Beijing 2008 Olympic Songs Album first hit the market as a two-disc set, containing 24 outstanding songs, all of which can be called the most popular and widely loved works from the five years of Olympic song solicitation campaigns. The one-year countdown theme song We are ready, performed by a hundred stars, and the 100-day countdown theme song Beijing Welcomes You head up the two discs respectively. Andy Lau’s Everyone is No.1, Liu Huan and Na Ying’s duet One World One Dream, Sun Nan, A-Mei and CoCo Lee’s Forever Friends, Wakin Chau’s Olympic volunteer theme song I Am a Star, Jay Chou’s A Thousand Miles of Mountains and Rivers, Wang Leehom’s One World One Dream, Wei Wei and Dai Yuqiang’s Mankind Is One Family, Han Hong and Yu Quan’s Cheers for Life, and Joey Yung and Nicholas Tse’s On the Same Blue Planet, among other famous works, are all included. And the creators of these tracks bring together outstanding songwriters such as Giorgio Moroder, Kong Xiangdong, Lin Xi, Xiaoke, Leung Kin-cheung, Peter Kam, Chan Siu-kei, Vincent Fang, and others. According to Zhao Dongming, director of the Cultural Activities Department of the Beijing Organizing Committee for the Olympic Games (BOCOG), every Olympic Games has released its own official music or song album, using the unique charm of music to spread the concept of that edition of the Games and to provide the global public with a unique channel for enjoying and understanding the Olympics. What sets the Beijing Olympic official song album apart from those of previous editions is that it is not a closed-off, in-house creation, but rather the crystallization of an open call for submissions. As the fruit of five years of Olympic song solicitation and creation, this album embodies the painstaking effort and wisdom of numerous music creators at home and abroad. Zhao Dongming also believes that the release of this album will allow Olympic songs to enter people’s daily lives more conveniently, and the dissemination and promotion of Olympic songs will thereby become more convenient and truly ubiquitous. This simply designed album has a rather extraordinary technological dimension. In addition to offering normal CD audio playback, this album also provides full-track downloads and ringtone downloads through China Mobile’s wireless music club, with strong support from China Mobile. Moreover, though it looks no different from an ordinary record on the outside, this album also comes preloaded with aigo Miaobi listening and sing-along functions. Users need only tap a certain mark on the inner pages with the aigo Miaobi to conveniently preview any song in full or learn to sing it karaoke-style — truly full of delightful novelty. On the occasion of the grand ceremony marking 100 days to the Olympics, the Beijing 2008 Olympic Songs Album was grandly released. This highly commemorative 2CD album contains 24 award-winning works that stood out in the Olympic song solicitation campaign, bringing together many well-known musicians from the mainland, Hong Kong and Taiwan as well as a hundred singing stars. The album carries the expectations of all Chinese people for the Olympics, expresses in music the pride and glory of all Chinese people, and highlights the power of the Olympics and the magnificence of China. Inspired by “One World, One Dream” and the Olympic spirit, let us join hands and together put into practice the Olympic ideals of “dream, friendship and peace,” and let one immortal Olympic anthem after another resound throughout the world. This album records the love and passion of China’s outstanding musicians for the grand Olympic occasion, including the one-year countdown theme song We are ready; the 100-day countdown theme song Beijing Welcomes You, performed by 100 stars; the Beijing 2008 Olympic torch relay theme song Light the Passion, Share the Dream; and the volunteer song I Am a Star. It also includes One World One Dream, written, composed and performed by Wang Leehom; Forever Friends (Chinese version), performed together by Sun Nan and A-Mei; A Thousand Miles of Mountains and Rivers, composed by the powerhouse duo of Jay Chou and Vincent Fang; Joey Yung and Nicholas Tse’s heartfelt rendition of On the Same Blue Planet; Liu Huan and Na Ying’s duet One World One Dream; Han Hong and Yu Quan’s Cheers for Life; Everyone is No.1, written, composed and performed by Andy Lau; and Wei Wei and Dai Yuqiang’s Mankind Is One Family — 28 outstanding Olympic songs in all. The creative team also brings together an all-star lineup of top-tier Mandarin pop and world-class songwriters and composers, including Xiaoke (blog), Moroder, Kong Xiangdong (blog), Leung Kin-cheung, Peter Kam, Chris Babida, Giorgio Moroder, Huang Xiaomao, Lin Xi, Chan Siu-kei, Vincent Fang and Han Bao, weaving the Olympic spirit of friendship and peace into this album. On the occasion of 100 days to the Olympics, the 100-day countdown theme song Beijing Welcomes You, performed by 100 singing stars, once again brought the celebration of welcoming the Olympics to a climax. This was yet another theme song performed jointly by many stars released by BOCOG, following the one-year countdown theme song We are ready, which had set off a wave of Olympic song singing. This star-studded song was composed by the famous mainland musician Xiaoke, with lyrics by Hong Kong lyricist Lin Xi, and performed jointly by 100 singers including Jackie Chan, Wakin Chau, Wang Leehom, Liu Huan, Stefanie Sun, Eason Chan and Richie Jen. From the idea being proposed in early March to the completion of production, the song took a month and a half in total, of which just 5 days were spent completing the demo of the lyrics and music, two weeks were spent recording all 100 singers, and 6 days were spent completing all post-production; the documentary footage alone ran to more than 7,000 minutes — a testament to the enormous and fervent Olympic “centripetal force” of the entertainment world. As the sonic symbol of the 100-day countdown to the Beijing Olympics, a hundred of the biggest and most talented singers in the Mandarin music world greet and invite the world with a thoroughly Beijing-flavored tune — “Beijing Welcomes You” — embracing Beijing’s Olympic guests with musical warmth, cheering on the Olympics, and greeting the arrival of the Beijing Olympics with a confident bearing. With the lighting of the Beijing 2008 Olympic flame in Athens, the Beijing Olympics that captured the world’s attention thus raised its curtain. Over more than a hundred days of torch relay across five continents, more than 20,000 torchbearers from around the world carried the Olympic torch bearing countless dreams, and with it the world’s beautiful pursuit of peace and friendship and the Olympic ideal. The song Light the Passion, Share the Dream accompanied the Beijing Olympic torch all the way, as the blazing “Lucky Cloud” torch shone together with the Olympic spirit and sang of the powerful cohesion of the Chinese nation. Besides the four-person version of Light the Passion, Share the Dream performed by Wang Leehom, Stefanie Sun, Wang Feng and Jane Zhang, the English version recorded with the participation of 106 international beauties from the 57th Miss World finals is also a dazzling highlight of this album. Since the official launch of registration for Beijing Olympic city volunteers, the public’s enthusiasm for paying attention to and supporting city volunteer work has reached unprecedented heights. The number of applicants for Beijing Olympic city volunteers has exceeded 1.36 million, and becoming one of the Olympic volunteers has become a matter of immense pride and honor. Every volunteer is a bright star in the sky, adorning the splendid firmament of the Beijing Olympics. I Am a Star, the Beijing Olympic volunteer song with lyrics by the famous lyricist Lin Xi and composed and performed by the Taiwan powerhouse singer Wakin Chau, depicts our most lovable volunteers in warm and moving words. The song was jointly created by Lin Xi and Wakin Chau over two weeks. Lin Xi’s creative prowess is fully displayed in this song, with every word and phrase expressing his original creative intent of boundless love. At the same time, the melody of the whole song is gentle yet powerful, and its grand orchestral style blends with a typically Chinese flavor — very distinctive indeed. Forever Friends, a song created for the Beijing Olympics by the Italian musician Giorgio Moroder, is also a major highlight of this album. The song has both Chinese and English versions, performed respectively by Sun Nan and A-Mei, and by Sun Nan and CoCo Lee. The lead creator of the song, the world-renowned Giorgio Moroder, is a famous Italian music master. Having composed many Olympic theme songs, he has a deep attachment to China, and even made a special trip to Beijing to gather inspiration for this song. The song combines the charm of Eastern music with the characteristics of Western music. Through the theme of “forever friends,” it expresses a beautiful wish that transcends racial and national boundaries, and the power and appeal contained within it will make everyone who hears it want to hold the hand of the person beside them, so that everyone becomes friends and shares in the joy. Thousands of Miles of Mountains and Rivers, the work of Jay Chou and his longtime partner Vincent Fang, has drawn even more attention. The song blends rock with Chinese-style melodies, and even adds a passage of “Peking opera” vocals, fully showing the true colors of the Chinese style. Dreams in Sight, jointly created by the famous Hong Kong musicians Lin Xi and Leung Kin-cheung and sung by Bibi Zhou (blog), tells of the Olympic spirit that crosses national borders and the humanistic values of Chinese civilization, and became a hit Olympic song as soon as it was released. The well-known Hong Kong singers Nicholas Tse and Joey Yung sang their hearts out for On the Same Blue Planet, personally performing an Olympic song and showing extremely high enthusiasm for participation. The two also separately expressed their hope for the success of the Beijing Olympics, and felt even more honored to be able to contribute to it. Hero, composed by the Taiwan singer Chris Yu with lyrics by Wang Pingjiu, director of the Olympic Cultural Activities Division of the Cultural Activities Department of BOCOG, is dedicated to the heroes who strive for their dreams on the Olympic field and never give up the Olympic spirit. Another song performed by a hundred stars, We are ready, as the theme song of the one-year countdown to the Beijing 2008 Olympics, let the whole world feel Beijing’s rich Olympic atmosphere and enthusiasm. The famous musicians from Hong Kong, Peter Kam and Chan Siu-kei, used a melody and lyrics full of vitality and rhythm to meticulously portray the heroic spirit, confidence, joy and anticipation of Beijing and China on the eve of the Olympics. Its repeatedly chanted “We are ready” is not only unforgettable as the song’s main melody, but also became the strongest voice of anticipation for the arrival of the Beijing Olympics. And the moving lyrics and pleasant melody of Everyone Is NO.1, created by Andy Lau, vividly portray the spiritual world of athletes with disabilities, depicting both the hardships and bitterness they face and their striving and struggle. As the pride of the Chinese people, Wang Leehom, as one of the first torchbearers to carry the sacred flame, completed the major mission of Olympic torch relay. He brought a song, One World One Dream, for which he wrote the lyrics, composed the music and sang himself, expressing with its majestic music and beautiful lyrics his full support for and boundless hopes for the Olympics. One World One Dream, a song by the famous singers Liu Huan and Na Ying, conveys to the whole world the deep feelings of the sons and daughters of China toward the 2008 Olympics. “One World One Dream,” as the slogan of the Beijing 2008 Olympics, accurately expresses the spirit of the Olympic Games, and this perfect pairing of a king and a queen of song inspires in Chinese people a sense of glory, responsibility and mission. Our Dream, a song created by Wang Feng, has maintained consistently high click rates since it entered the selection process; this Olympic song full of rock flavor is also the Chinese rock scene’s way of expressing its sense of Olympic glory. Cheers for Life, performed jointly by Yu Quan and Han Hong, is a song that embodies para-sports. As friends who have known each other in the industry for many years and equally top-tier powerhouse singers in China, the three of them nonetheless sang a song together for the first time — and singing for the Olympics, especially joining forces for para-sports, made all three particularly committed. Stand Up, the theme song of the Olympic film The One Man Olympics, has lyrics by Wang Pingjiu, director of the Olympic Cultural Activities Division of the Cultural Activities Department of BOCOG, and music by Shu Nan, winner of the Golden Rooster Award for Best Music. It is performed jointly by Jackie Chan, Wang Leehom, Stefanie Sun and Han Hong, with the four representing the mainland, Hong Kong, Taiwan and overseas Chinese respectively. The song expresses the Olympic spirit of never giving up and striving tenaciously. Mankind Is One Family, brought by Wei Wei and Dai Yuqiang, hopes to convey the core of the Olympic spirit — peace, harmony, open-mindedness, friendship, transcendence and passion — to everyone, hoping that it can represent every Chinese person and awaken in all humankind enthusiasm for and resonance with the 2008 Beijing Olympics and the ideal of universal harmony. As an international sports gala of extraordinary significance, the Beijing 2008 Olympics will become a richly colored and infinitely glorious stroke in history. Everyone is, in their own way, singing the praises of, celebrating and giving voice to their expectations and yearnings for the Olympics. Music knows no borders, and music can never be fully expressed in words. As a sonic-version commemoration of a grand occasion of the century, the Beijing 2008 Olympic Songs Album carries the passion of Chinese people around the world in watching over, blessing and supporting the Olympics, carries the world’s pursuit of and ideals for the Olympic spirit, and allows the humanistic spirit to leap forward and be sublimated in the perfect fusion of the Olympic spirit and music.

title: I've watched a few movies recently
content: Evening of 08-8-16: finished Wall-e (the TS version, no other option). A robot’s innocent love… Evening of 8-22: finished Déjà Vu. The film’s logic is absolutely brilliant — you rarely come across a movie like this! Genuinely excellent; mulling it over carefully, it still holds plenty of meaning, and you can piece together the hidden plot. My head was mush for a long while; someone on Douban described it as being possessed, which is spot on… Evening of 8-23: Hellboy II. What you’re in it for is the sci-fi and the imagination, but in the end it’s still about love… Once it was over I’d thought too much: chaos - clarity - chaos. I can’t even be bothered to articulate any thoughts or feelings… Want to watch them? Wall-E I got from a BT download, forgot the link; Déjà Vu is on eMule, and there’s also Hellboy II.
