title: Getting to Know "Otaku" Culture — We're Not Otaku Boys and Girls?
content: I joined the “We’re Not Otaku Boys or Girls” group on Douban. Ugh, there’s actually a Jiongxing community, and even Jiongjiong TV… http://orzStar.com “Jiongxing - The Most Lovable Otaku Planet in the Entire Universe”… Unbeatable! I’m not really an otaku, but I’ve got potential… I’ll go study abroad on this planet for a while first. After reading the group’s intro posts on Douban and wandering around Jiongxing, I discovered that otaku culture is not as simple as I imagined — hating going out, loving to stay at home, using the computer and internet to reach the whole world without stepping outside, SOHO. Based on the somewhat parodic professional explanation, the term “otaku” was originally pejorative. The word originated in Japan, that perverted country where “lust is the worst of all evils,” so you can imagine it comes packed with shocking elements — Introduction to Otaku The original name was the Want-to-be-Stepped-on Tribe — as the name suggests, a tribe that likes to be stepped on. They even like to scream when stepped on; the old-fashioned term for this was “queen.” Later, politicians abused the term and it went bad too, so it was changed to “freedom of speech,” fighting for the autonomy to make crappy drawings, and protesting against Taiwan’s big shots depriving them of their right to watch uncensored crappy drawings. Finally they protested that the name “Want-to-be-Stepped-on Tribe” carried sexist connotations, so it was changed to “otaku” — but that’s not much better either. Otaku are the dregs of society, the shame of humanity, potential criminals — desperate outlaws who will do anything, from upskirt photography and underwear theft to kidnapping. Otaku are caused by a computer virus spread through electronic signals; once infected, there is no cure. All otaku are driven to act by the power of moe, forming a transnational network across the globe and engaging in cross-border crimes such as child pornography, kidnapping, model-kit collecting, and premium-goods theft. In Japan, the earliest birthplace of otaku, because their burning motivation cannot support a work ethic, the country has fallen into long-term recession, and the Japanese government has established a Fetishism Eradication Organization to block the spread of the otaku virus. The otaku virus is an ancient computer virus discovered by Japanese scientist Dr. Otaku Nen beneath the Antarctic ice. It may be the main cause of the destruction of the highly advanced civilization of Atlantis mentioned in ancient texts. After discovering the virus, Dr. Otaku disappeared for unknown reasons, possibly connected to the Men in Black. Types Otaku King A high-ranking otaku who never leaves home, wielding a giant life-size animemanga character body pillow (female or male) and living in an impregnable fortress materialized from delusionslewd fantasies. The Otaku Kings of the world are linking up in a conspiracy to overthrow all nations founded on the language of God, and attempting to spread their faith through internet, TV, and manga. There was once a rumor that Tedi Bill was an Otaku King, but he solemnly denied it. The latest report from Road-Blast News Agency claims that the lust demon Kili is the real Otaku King — pending verification… Collector Maniac A faithful servant of Fetishism, one of those who abandon almost all material needs and survive on moe alone. They nearly ignore everything about reality, but will always scrape together money to buy the premium goods they love. Legend has it that on a full-moon night after eating instant noodles for over a month straight, a collector who offers up the last remaining shred of humanity in reality will become a disembodied Collector Lich. Fujoshi Conglomerate Ambitious schemers attempting to conquer the world with homosexual pornographic images, deluding themselves at every moment. Upon seeing ambiguity between people of the same sex, they immediately sort out the top and the bottom (you must determine this within one second to have any chance of promotion), and this is not limited to humans. In order to promote their cause they resort to extreme measures — a group known as the “Wolves of Tanbi,” operating in groups distinguished by flower names (such as lily, rose, etc.), specifically attacking children who are alone to strengthen their organization. The subgroup made up of women is also called “doujin women.” Stay-at-Home Deadbeats Strictly speaking, they shouldn’t count as otaku, because they are almost entirely non-aggressive — commonly known as NEETs, useless people who have passed school age but still refuse to work and just leech off their families at home. Otaku Religions Generally speaking, otaku religious preferences differ from those of ordinary people, and can be roughly divided into the following types: Zeon Founding Principle Only those who have migrated to space, the Spacenoids, represent human innovation. Toward the ghosts bound by gravity, the moderates believe in gradually enlightening them, while the radicals believe in dropping colonies to purge and accelerate evolution. They have now formed the Zeon Remnants to realize their ideals. Nazism Hitler was the last Otaku King to hold political power; only superior otaku can lead the world and eliminate the masses of ignorant fools who cannot accept the correct path. Also, Hitler had an abnormal hatred of “juice.” Indescribable Elder God Worship The great beings beyond humanity recorded in the Book of the Dead, written by the Arab madman H. P. Love Generator, whose true names cannot be pronounced by ordinary human vocal organs, and who transcend the true essence of the universe as comprehensible by human reason. Worshipping them grants powerful magic, the assistance of ubiquitous agents, and the most wonderful tentacle-wrapping violation of nude beautiful girls. Lolicon Supremacy Believes that women past their appreciation period have only the residual value of producing more lolis, and dreams of creating a perfect society where all women have the appearance of a twelve-year-old and either huge breasts or flat chests. In fact, disputes over breasts have always been a reason for their internal strife. The famous Char is a representative figure of this faction Feminization Promotion Alliance Believes that only yuri is the true path of the service genre, and that all male characters in anime and manga should be cut off and rerolled. Bubble Dog Indiscriminate Heaven-Defying Imperial Army An existence even deeper than the Feminization Promotion Alliance, rejecting physiological differences between men and women. Not only do they support pushing down young beautiful girls — as long as they’re moe enough, even shotas and Mizuho types can be pushed. Since launching the Roaming Heaven-Defying Weekly in 2006, they have swept the Chinese otaku world with lightning speed. Big Ships, Big Guns Doctrine Firepower and caliber are the only true path — a type whose life is filled with guns and military terminology. Their leader is GIRORO of Planet Keron. This Is My Path A group of people whose ultimate goal is the ultimate otaku lifestyle, who ignore others and carry out the lifestyle they want, with the potential to become Otaku Kings. Gundam Fundamentalists Researchers dedicated to researching all Gundam setting materials. They argue over the orthodoxy of materials on Gundam forums and enjoy exposing and attacking non-orthodox heretics. They are further divided into Tomino Fundamentalists and Realist Militarists. For a very long time the two factions attacked each other, but after the Pink Enchantress Cult appeared, both factions recognized its horror and decided to join forces against it — historically known as the Military–Tomino Alliance. Otaku Gatherings Normally otaku will not leave their castles with TVs and internet, but certain activities can make them suppress their inherent territoriality, such as: Doujinshi Conventions Gatherings packed with pornographic publications and outlandish costumes. You might have to line up for hours just to enter, only to sweat profusely in the crowd and fail to grab a boring pornographic doujinshi of no more than a hundred pages. Video Game Expos No need to explain this one! Mainly H-games, H-manga, and anime. With OGC on-site, everyone has a healthy LP. Megane Girl Church A religious group that holds gatherings every week. You must absolutely never take off your glasses in front of them. They are dedicated to promoting the beauty of glasses-wearing girls and to increasing women’s glasses prescription. National Dara Alliance That is, the National Doll Lovers (Doller) Alliance, abbreviated as the National Dara Alliance. This organization is also the base camp of Rozen Maiden supporters. Regular Pilgrimages to Limited-Edition Premium Goods at Boutiques Burn for the premium goods! Otaku Industries: For an otaku, no matter how much he wants to overthrow or escape the real world, he still has to raise funds to satisfy his wicked desires, so otaku often work in these industries: Education Workers Or simply, teachers. Which teaching position they take depends on their guarding range and ability, and it’s usually a choice other than a university post. Being a moral example is a good cover for hiding their abnormal desires. Perhaps their cover is too good, because the teachers usually caught preying on students are normal-minded heterosexuals. Entertainment Industry Combining interest and entertainment is a nice idea. Besides that, working in related industries can also promote their extreme devil worship. From manga artists and voice actors to anime-industry workers, this is a good choice for social parasites who like to play video games to death while claiming to be seeking inspiration. But after becoming famous, you’ll have less time to entertain yourself than to entertain others — unless you’re a serial-delinquent manga artist who married someone in the same industry and no longer has to worry about the rest of your life. Rich Family Scions The type who can coast through life without having to struggle — in other words, second-generation heirs, spendthrift brats, worthless types, a minority within a minority. Terrorists Relying on fundraising, they can get enough funds to buy several lifetimes’ worth of premium goods, then spend their downtime frantically devouring the bizarre anime and military hardware they could never normally obtain. If it weren’t for the need to periodically express their existence through actions (violating otaku territoriality) and the risk of losing their lives, this would actually suit the freeloading type of otaku quite well. If all the world’s terrorists were otaku, counter-terrorism would only need to increase investment in the anime and manga industry to paralyze terrorist organizations. Measures by Various Governments Regarding the Otaku Phenomenon: Because of the great harm caused by otaku, governments around the world have taken measures to crack down on and eliminate their spread. Japan Japan is the birthplace of otaku, the Mecca of Fetishism. But under the threat of sex crimes caused by otaku and the harm to Japanese values, the Japanese government gathered former spies and girls who had been hurt by otaku, subjected them to physical enhancement and mind control, and secretly established the Fetishism Eradication Organization under the cover of the social welfare budget. They carry out total physical and spiritual annihilation of otaku friends lurking among the populace like terrorists. On a certain small island in Japan, there exists a facility for brainwashing, torture, and forced labor to eliminate harmful otaku ideology. Taiwan A regime that has always persecuted otaku faith through various soft or coercive means. Long, long ago it wiped out up to eighty percent of local manga artists with decrees that were “guidance” in name but prohibition in reality. But ACG will not be extinguished by this; relying on smuggled resources, the manga-reading community can still find comfort, and in private settings student groups still hide large quantities of manga. In recent years, thanks to the intervention of business conglomerates, the treatment of the ACG community has improved somewhat. But to brain-dead legislators, ACG is merely a synonym for moral corruption, and they are always ready to use the media to deliver another Seven Days of Fire. Fellow enthusiasts should emulate the spirit of their predecessors and make those jerks unable to hold onto their seats. Wikipedia Someone has said: Otaku generally refers to people who are enthusiastic about subcultures such as anime, manga, and computer games, but it is now widely used by people from all walks of life in Japan and has trended toward neutrality, with some even proud of being otaku. For Japanese anime fans in Europe and America, the word’s positive or negative connotation varies from person to person. At present, in Japanese, the term otaku has a tendency to extend to those who are enthusiastic about mainstream cultural interests, or even those with deep expertise in professional fields. One of the founders of GAINAX, Toshio Okada, who calls himself “Otaking” (Otaku King), defined otaku as follows: in this 21st century known as the “full-scale explosion of visual information,” a new type of human race has emerged to adapt to this world of visual information. In other words, a race whose sensitivity to visuals has evolved to an extreme. However, this is Okada’s personal interpretation beautifying otaku, not an objective definition. As for the three things regarded as markers of otaku — anime, manga, and computer games — although they are essentially inseparable, there is no special collective term for them in Japan (their content is often referred to as “2D” (nijigen), since they are mainly 2D images. Even now, in the era of highly advanced 3D modeling technology, the representativeness of this term remains unshaken). In the Chinese-speaking world, the term “ACG” (Animation, Comic, Game), coined by the senior “AIplus” of the “Sha Hu Lu Alliance” — a mangaanime-related group founded in Taiwan long ago and still active today ([1] The group’s name comes from a transliteration of the Shuffle Alliance (シャッフル同盟, also translated as Xiaru Alliance or Shuffle Alliance) from the Japanese anime “Mobile Fighter G Gundam”) — is the most common way of referring to it, and it has continued to spread and be used to this day. Evaluation of Otaku Because of their excessive enthusiasm for subcultural products, they are easily regarded by the general public as a group that produces nothing. In addition, collecting certain subcultural products, such as firearms or pornographic content, may cause them to be seen as potential criminals. For example, in the famous case that once occurred in Japan — the “TokyoSaitama Serial Girl Kidnapping and Murder Case” (also known as the Tsutomu Miyazaki Incident, 1988–1989) — because a large quantity of pornographic anime videotapes was found in the home of the perpetrator, Tsutomu Miyazaki, the reputation of the OTAKU community was called into question by society. Moreover, because they are excessively enthusiastic about specific fields, many of them are relatively worse than ordinary people in interpersonal relationships and social skills, so Japanese society’s overall impression of this group is generally not good. This situation improved slightly after the 2004 movie Densha Otoko aired (see below). The 2004 internet story “Densha Otoko,” which caused a sensation in Japan, portrayed a typical otaku image: unconcerned with appearance, no luck with women, afraid to talk to women, good with computers, good with subcultures, and collecting all kinds of models. But being unconcerned with appearance, having no luck with women, and being afraid to talk to women are not traits that otaku necessarily possess. Many otaku also have the trait of being “hikikomori” (stay-at-home); and “hikikomori” shares certain traits similar to the above. For this part, one may refer to “hidden youth.” It must be especially noted that otaku are not equivalent to hikikomori, and there is no necessary relationship between the two. In present-day Japan, the situation in this regard has begun to change. Since Japan is a country where capitalism reigns supreme, “economic value” has become the ultimate indicator of everything. Japan’s famous socio-economic research group, the “Nomura Research Institute (野村総合研究所),” proposed the “Otaku Market Report” in 2004, stating that this market has a scale of 2.3 trillion yen, but because the original research direction was considered not broad enough, the actual market size may be even larger. In addition, at the “9th International Architecture Exhibition of the Venice Biennale” (La Biennale di Venezia) hosted by Italy, the Japanese pavilion’s exhibition project was themed on moe, and some specific 2D beautiful-girl illustrations were even adopted by internationally renowned design brands, causing their value to begin to be reaffirmed by the world. The Term “Zhainan” in Taiwan The term “zhainan” in Taiwan already differs from the otaku as understood in Japan. Tracing the popularity of the term “zhainan” in Taiwan back to August 2005, when boards on Taiwan’s PTT (such as Hate and JapanDrama) were into watching the Japanese short drama “Densha Otoko.” Since the story is about an unkempt Japanese otaku encountering a tall beauty, Taiwanese PTT netizens began to enjoy jokingly saying on the Hate board that they stay at home all the time and are very “zhai,” or that people who are online all day are simply “zhainan.” From this period onward, the term “zhainan” began to spread wildly in Taiwan. At first, some people criticized that the “zhainan” recognized by Taiwanese differs from the Japanese otaku, sparking numerous online flame wars. But in the end, the terms “otaku” and “zhainan” in Taiwan have already come to differ from Japan. And due to Taiwan’s internet KUSO culture, anyone who often stays home and doesn’t go out, loves playing online games, has no girlfriend, dresses sloppily, or speaks slowly is considered a “zhainan.” On the show “Guess, Guess, Guess” hosted by Jacky Wu, the term “social parasite” was used to insult otaku, arousing public dissatisfaction. Starting in 2007, “zhainan” not only appeared in the subculture’s online world; many media news outlets also began using the term. For example, a news report on July 7, 2007 read, “23-year-old zhainan suffers stroke from being online,” when in fact, looking carefully at the news content, it was merely a graduate student who had to use a computer frequently, leading to illness. The CTi Variety show “Quanmin Damenguo” on July 19, 2007 used “High university admission rates, high unemployment rates after graduation, a bunch of zhainan who are lazy as hell — what will we do about our next generation?” as its main topic, and the host also made erroneous statements such as “Fujoshi means corrupt women with no future” and “Zhainan are already all connected — go find a job, would you?” — further vilifying otaku and fujoshi. This later triggered an outpouring of criticism online, and even a movement to boycott “Quanmin Damenguo” appeared. The term “zhainan” has already begun to be used widely but incorrectly. In the same year, the headline on page 3 of the United Evening News on August 2, 2007 also used “Is there a zhainan in your house?” as its title, describing zhainan as a kind of disease, over-citing scholars and experts to stigmatize zhainan, and categorizing almost all men and women who simply don’t interact with society or don’t want to talk to others as “zhainan” or “fujoshi,” considering it a disease requiring medication or psychiatric treatment. At the same time, the report interviewed too few representative zhainan, who did not represent the whole, resulting in overgeneralization and a failure to report the truth in full. Most of the content defining zhainan was determined by scholars and experts and given in interviews with reporters. Strangely enough, on certain large anime and game websites in Taiwan, as soon as “zhai” is mentioned, a whole crowd of angry internet users will explain and defend the word “zhai.” Common Subcultures Manga Anime Games Tokusatsu Doujinshi Cosplay Movies Books Models Military Science Computers Occultism Bus fans (common in Hong Kong) Railway fans (common in Japan and Taiwan) Forget it, they’re too professional — I can’t compare, I’m a good person… If “zhai” still means this in mainland China, then I’m not “zhai”…

title: Sins of a Solar Empire: Beginner Tips & Screenshots
content: Last night I played Sins of a Solar Empire (hereafter Solar) until midnight. I’ve finally got the hang of it. Three takeaways: You absolutely can’t do without resources — be aggressive about colonizing and grabbing mines. In Solar you never have enough resources: the enormous research tree eats a lot of them, and you need plenty of bases to build enough labs. To fix that, you have to colonize fast and grab several planets. Once you get a planet, build population, logistics, metal mines and crystal mines first. When crystal is short you can buy it on the black market at a high price — otherwise you fall into a vicious cycle: no crystal - can’t build tech labs - tech can’t level up - can’t build new products - can’t beat the enemy - lose planets - the economy collapses even harder, and so on. Sometimes spending a bit of cash on crystal helps you take more crystal-rich planets faster. Watch the fire from across the river — fund the underworld and terrorism. Besides the fixed wandering mobs you can MF (like the creeps in WAR3), the neutral factions in the game include pirates who have formed their own independent nation. Unlike those mobs, the pirates have their own bases, with lots of logistics facilities, firepower installations and big fleets. Every dozen minutes or so they set out on a sweep, and for a beginner that sweep is usually devastating. In the early game, funding pirate operations and putting a bounty on your opponent is a very wise move. If you don’t, the consequence is this: someone puts a bounty on you, then you get swept by pirates, and while you’re busy yelling “you bastard” and fighting them off, that sneaky opponent takes the opportunity to harass your economy… Nechayev wrote: “For the victory of the revolution, the revolutionary may break with every moral law accepted by society… If an alliance with bandits can hasten the victory of the revolution, then by all means form the alliance…” In Solar, the most terrifying thing isn’t the AI players, it’s the pirate fleets. My god, the firepower on a pirate planet had me drenched in sweat — see the screenshots below. When you don’t have the strength early on, you absolutely must fund the pirates. Remember, remember. For just a few hundred credits, an advanced pirate fleet will launch a full-scale assault on your opponent, leaving them in total chaos and wailing — I guarantee you’ll be pleased. Truly a must-have product for playing Solar at home! Turn swords into plowshares — Solar’s diplomacy system. Have you ever been playing another strategy game and thought that you and some hostile faction might sometimes share common interests? Maybe even enemies can reach certain agreements with each other. Like in SGA, where the Wraith and the humans wipe out a Replicator planet together. Heh, in Solar’s diplomacy system, AI players give you missions (asking you for support), which may be economic or military. For example, they ask you to provide 1000 crystal, or they want you to help destroy 7 cruisers from another faction. If you finish the mission within a set time, the friendship between your two nations goes up; otherwise it goes down (this friendship value is in some ways similar to reputation in WOW). In Solar the friendship value ranges from 0 to 100. As it climbs past 50, that faction will propose negotiations such as a “truce agreement”, “shared planet vision”, “shared ship vision” and “economic cooperation”. When it reaches 100, you can choose whether to ally! Of course, after allying you can break the alliance again. With a diplomacy system this innovative, how could you not make good use of it? In the game I lean toward allying with AI players who are far away. First, their missions usually have you destroy player units near you, which is convenient to march out on. Second, you can form an encirclement with that AI and control the course of the battle. Third, if you ally with a nearby faction, where are you going to colonize? Screenshots below: [caption id”attachment_157” align”aligncenter” width”300” caption”The blue guy is so unlucky — tormented by pirates from the very start, and still fighting them off when I sailed over to invade…”][caption] [caption id”attachment_161” align”aligncenter” width”300” caption”Storming the pirate planet, only to find ourselves outnumbered”][caption] [caption id”attachment_162” align”aligncenter” width”300” caption”Outnumbered — full retreat”][caption] [caption id”attachment_163” align”aligncenter” width”300” caption”Pirates attack; fighters locked in battle with the pirates”][caption] [caption id”attachment_164” align”aligncenter” width”300” caption”The invading pirates are nearly wiped out”][caption] [caption id”attachment_165” align”aligncenter” width”300” caption”To save Li Ka-shing, planning to relieve the siege by striking elsewhere, passing the pirate planet again”][caption] [caption id”attachment_166” align”aligncenter” width”300” caption”Honorable pirates, I’m just passing through…”][caption] [caption id”attachment_167” align”aligncenter” width”300” caption”Open the gate and run, fast”][caption]

title: Watched *The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe*
content: Bad movie. The premise of The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe was created by the British writer C.S. Lewis, who wrote seven fantasy novels set in the magical kingdom of Narnia. The novel this film adapts, The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, was the first book in the series that C.S. Lewis published, though in story order it is the second. The protagonists are four London children — Lucy, Peter, Susan and Edmund. Because London was under constant air-raid threat during World War II, children were evacuated to country estates, and the four Pevensie children were sent to the country home of an old professor, Digory Kirke. There they discover a magical wardrobe that turns out to lead into a magical kingdom — Narnia. It is a wondrous world where animals talk, but the evil White Witch Jadis has laid her hands on everything, and the children must join the side of the righteous spiritual leader, the lion Aslan, uniting all the forces opposed to the Witch to bring peace back to Narnia. I rather liked this story as a kid, and it’s one of the most common setups in the genre: there’s another world parallel to our three-dimensional space-time (Narnia), and that world is shrouded in darkness and ice and snow. The four protagonists stumble into it, only to discover that they are the prophesied saviors of that world. Four humans will end Narnia’s age of ice and darkness, save its people, and usher in Narnia’s rebirth. Hmm, the setup itself is actually a good one, but what bugs me is this: what special abilities do these four legendary figures actually have? Take, for example, “the legendary figures possess the power of love, which has all but vanished from this world,” or “the legendary figures have extraordinary magic and wisdom,” or “the legendary figures have exceptional courage and fighting spirit.” At the very least you have to give the prophecy a reasonable explanation before the audience will buy it. Maybe my eyes are just bad. In this film I don’t see anything indispensable about these four “prophesied saviors of everyone.” In other words, as far as I can tell, Aslan would win without them anyway. Just look: the rebel army Aslan recruits is no worse than the White Witch’s in attack, defense, numbers, morale, equipment, RP — you name it. Can’t Aslan fight a war himself? Do a few war-weary kids, traumatized by WWII, have to lead the troops into battle? Otherwise there’s no victory? What’s even more unbelievable is that these kids actually get six “artifacts.” Peter gets a “melee greatsword” and a “holy shield”; Susan gets a “never-miss bow set” and a “battle horn”; little sister Lucy gets “soul-restoring water” and a “fine dagger.” The “artifacts” are given out by Narnia’s Santa Claus. I’m dumbfounded — why does Santa Claus have artifacts like these, and why is he so certain they should go to these four? Where does anyone see in them the potential for war, the talent, or the ability to run a country after winning? (PS: The only explanation that feels reasonable to me: having the four of them on board gives the army special attributes: [+morale, +luck], so it’s destiny — the good guys have to recruit them.) Good movie.Oh, right — I get it, it’s a fairy tale. Plot holes aside, this movie is really about the four children growing up. Like Alvin and the Chipmunks, which I saw the day before yesterday, it’s once again the story of someone drawn in by immediate gain (Edmund, for Turkish delight and a throne), going astray, and finally coming back for a happy ending. In this film, little sister Lucy giving her handkerchief to the faun Tumnus, Edmund’s awakening after he sees the White Witch’s cruelty, Aslan willingly dying to redeem the traitor Edmund, Edmund telling his brother “I believe in you too” before the battle, and, in the big battle, the spectacular fight scene of one of Aslan’s lieutenants, a bull — these are all good moments. Edmund’s betrayal caused trouble for countless people. A lie woven out of candy ultimately cannot withstand the ever-changing world. But his later awakening and courage let you feel the power of growing up. Peter, a child who always seems to have to put on an adult’s air, indecisive, always seeming to just protect his small self, to hole up in his own world — until the final battle with the White Witch, when he sees the subjects who follow him bravely throw themselves at the Witch and die on the battlefield, and sees his own brother stabbed by the Witch, he seems to grow up overnight. Susan, who seems willing to play the mother role, always hunting for the so-called best way through clever little tricks, but often ends up outsmarting herself. In Narnia, playing in the water with her sister — that’s her true self. Lucy, my favorite of the children, full of imagination, friendly and warm. After meeting the faun, she quickly bonds with him, and when he’s in trouble she insists they can’t just walk away. Young as she is, she’s strong and has a mind of her own. That white handkerchief makes even me want to give it a shout-out. ——Uncle Bunny This film also carries everyone’s childhood dreams. Inside everyone there’s a corner for fairy tales; everyone has a magic wardrobe in their heart, and when you open it, a kindly lion and a faun smile at us. Warm and simple. The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe isn’t a movie everyone takes to, because it isn’t good enough, even though Disney did its best. Those who fell asleep watching it aren’t necessarily lacking a child’s heart — it’s just that everyone’s childhood is different. Some people’s childhoods had mice that flew planes and drove tanks, some had drawers that pop out blue round robots, some had purple gourds that could suck in everything. And my childhood happened to have a wardrobe. Maybe from the moment I read Secret Room 309 and started running my hands over all four corners of every cabinet at home, looking for that inconspicuous bump, it was destined that I would be just as unable to forget another wardrobe. ——LiliMarleen Also, I really like the music in this film. Kids’ movieI love the ending of this film; the professor is very kind and amiable. In one final sentence: this is a fantasy film that enlightens the mind, suitable for children.

title: The Ultimate Fix for Garbled Text When Flash Fetches PHP-Generated XML
content: I’m never one to back down from wrestling with the most bizarre problems—let’s see who comes out on top. It’s been ages since I hit an obstacle while coding, yet today I ran into a little snag—XML generated by PHP came out as garbled text when fetched with FLASH. After some digging I finally solved it. Recording it here, and also jotting down the general solution. If you also run into XML - FLASH garbled text, here’s a quick reference: 1. When you’re certain the XML is absolutely fine:First, FLASH reading XML and getting garbled text involves the static property System.useCodepage. Official description: “A Boolean value that tells Flash Player which code page to use to interpret external text files.” Defaults to false. If we’re using UTF-8 encoded external text files, we don’t need to worry about it. But if we use a non-UTF-8 encoded text file with Chinese characters in it, we need to set it to true for FLASH to read the characters without garbling. In AS3 you can first import flash.system.System; then set System.useCodePage=true; 2. Wanting PHP to generate UTF-8 encoded XML:To have Chinese characters in the XML, it’s best to use UTF-8 encoding. Before creating the XML with DOM, declare it as $dom\_XML = new DomDocument(1.0,UTF-8);—the second parameter corresponds to the encoding value in the XML document’s declaration section. But note: this is only the declared encoding. When you finally use $dom\_XML-saveXML();, the actual generated XML file has the same encoding as the PHP script source file, i.e. “whatever encoding your PHP is, that’s the encoding of the generated file.” (see http://www.phpchina.com/bbs/viewthread.php?tid=11450) 3. The XML file declares UTF-8 encoding, but in FLASH it’s still garbled no matter what value useCodepage is set toThis situation comes up often, usually because: although the declaration part is UTF-8, the file itself isn’t UTF-8 (mine was ANSI encoded, ugh). That leads to a serious problem: Firefox can parse the XML fine, but IE (including IE-based browsers like TT) reports invalid characters, and Flash shows garbled text too! There are two ways to handle this: Change the XML declaration part to a non-UTF-8 encoding, such as GB2312, then set FLASH’s useCodepagetrue; Open the XML in Notepad, use “Save As” to save it as UTF-8. In other words, make the encoding declaration match the file’s actual encoding—no false advertising. 4. The PHP source file isn’t UTF-8 encoded—how do you generate XML that lets FLASH support Chinese characters? This is the case I ran into:The PHP is saved as ANSI, so the XML generated with DOM is naturally ANSI too. If an XML file in this encoding contains Chinese characters, it can’t be read correctly even if the declared encoding is UTF-8. Given this, for FLASH to read the XML correctly without garbled text, you must set encoding to GB2312. Yet PHP’s DOM apparently can’t write Chinese characters with GB2312 (no idea why—gurus, please enlighten me). If you do new DomDocument(1.0,GB2312);, saving the XML throws an error like: “output conversion failed due to conv error, bytes 0xCE 0xD2 0x5D 0x5D”. That is to say, my ANSI PHP can only generate an XML file that declares UTF-8 but is actually ANSI—and of course FLASH reads that as garbled text (see item 3). My solution: after PHP generated the XML with the UTF-8 declaration, I added one extra step: open the XML file, rewrite the header declaration, and replace UTF-8 with GB2312. Hehe—now FLASH, IE, and FF all work without errors!

title: Enjoyed *Alvin and the Chipmunks*
content: In the afternoon I watched Alvin and the Chipmunks. Mm, an immortal theme — family. The male lead, Dave Seville, loves music but can’t catch a break at work — a talented guy nobody recognizes, broke, and unemployed. Then there are three chipmunks who bounce around and talk like humans: Alvin, in red, is the leader of the trio — handsome, brash, and fond of pulling pranks; Simon, in blue, is the brainy one; Theodore, in green (well, he doesn’t wear anything) is round and chubby, a lively, lovable little glutton who’d rather lie around than move. The three chipmunks can not only talk, they’re also seriously musically gifted — they sing and dance, and before long their special talent has taken over Dave’s house and his career. Thanks to them, Dave’s career takes off too. But the three little chipmunks are naive about the world and easily dazzled by short-term gain, so they run away from home… yeah, that plot is pretty educational… The story follows them going from strangers to colleagues, then to friends, and finally to family. Like Stuart Little, it’s a kids’ movie about animals and humans living together in harmony as one family… Watching it, I found the plot a bit dull, and the music, which should have been the big highlight, just wasn’t my taste. What the story mainly shows is the power of family. The climax in one sentence: a bunch of clueless kids want treats and fun and won’t listen to their parent, get lured away from home by the bad guy, and in the end the prodigals come home for a happy ending. At the start Dave thinks he doesn’t like kids, and at the end he declares they’re a family — which reminded me of The Mask 2. Ugh, so similar. Most American kids’ movies use this kind of comedy to get children to value family, love the people around them, and cherish what they have. Watch enough of them and it gets boring — it’s all the same formula. Just like Japanese anime is forever preaching and dispensing motivation; these days the moment I hear “gambatte” in Japanese I get goosebumps. Tomorrow I’ll watch The Chronicles of Narnia (1). Hopefully it won’t be too disappointing.

title: Embarking on the Path of Cosmic War - Sins of a Solar Empire
content: I’ve trekked over high mountains and lakes, visited orcs and the undead, commanded angels and demons, studied science and religion, crossed the ancient past and the distant future, savored the instant and the eternal, lived through the epic and the immortal. I’ve been a commander, a general, a strategist; a warrior, a mage, a wizard, a sage; a ranger, a rogue; a mayor, a tyrant, a CEO, a comrade… I thought I had already experienced everything the world had to offer. But just now I finally realized there’s still one level up to aim for — space! Sure, in WOW I went with my companions to Draenor, the orcs’ homeland, that extraordinarily beautiful alien planet, but I’ve never commanded a war in space. Now the opportunity is here: out in the Western world there’s a creator organization called Ironclad Games, and in the universe they finished building earlier this year, one breathtaking epic space battle after another is about to unfold! For now we call this universe “Sins of a Solar Empire”. At the start of the year, that world still had no Chinese characters — only a language of 26 letters, writing with so little depth to it, plus Arabic numerals. Now Chinese characters have been born! I truly can’t wait to get into that Western space. Brave commanders, imperial monarchs, join the sacred war and step onto the epic battlefield together. In the game, players control swarms of ships to explore and conquer nearby planets and distant solar systems. You can achieve your goals through military force, cunning strategy, refined diplomacy, economic control, technological research and more. You’ll use your capital ships to direct the rest of your fleet, improve your offensive and defensive systems, and unlock unique new capabilities. From research machinery to weapons platforms, from structures on a planet’s surface to installations in satellite orbit, everything must be folded into the planet’s strategic and economic system. This title uses the Iron engine and Forge tool suite developed by Ironclad Games; through them it can render the game’s captivating starfields, powerful ships, giant planets and more. The link below can show you and me the door into that universe: legitimate-version supporters can go to the official site:http://www.sinsofasolarempire.com/store.aspxto buy it. Destitute pirates, head to:http://www.verycd.com/topics/233235/fire up eMule to download, then apply the 1.4 patch the 1.4 Chinese patch. To put it bluntly, yesterday I got bored of Heroes of Might and Magic V again. Sigh. Life is like a game, and a game is like life — I’ve seen through the mundane world the way I’ve seen through a game… Life goes on; as long as there’s life, there’s gaming. Keep sinking into boredom — there are still so many years left to get through. Enjoy The Moment. Live well in the here and now.

title: Grumbling after finishing The Lord of the Rings
content: *Ranting below:*** At this stage (representing only what I knew as of this season, July 11, 2008 CE), a grand declaration (Note: if you disagree with any of the following declarations, please stop reading the “ranting” section, because to you it’s all nonsense): 1.The essential pursuit of life is love — for a related film, see The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy2.Ruthless, infinite life is a process of suffering — see The Mermaid Legend3.Mortals’ souls do not die after death; memories are wiped clean at reincarnation4.To attain the Way and become a sage, one must slay the Three Corpses I finally finished watching the entire Lord of the Rings trilogy, and I came to understand Sargeras’s fall. An extended thought: mortal or not, no one can escape their own suffering. Heaven and earth are ruthless; they treat all things as straw dogs. The ultimate meaning of life is that there is no meaning. It’s probably listening to Keren Ann’s sad songs lately and seeing how nothing in my hometown is the same anymore that has left me feeling so negative. The essential pursuit of life is love — at birth, human nature is good. People are born with a yearning for beautiful things. When a small child sees an adult who is sad, he’ll want to try giving the adult his toy to cheer them up. Human nature is fundamentally a force of love, and that’s why human civilization has been able to develop to where it is today. Not long ago, during the 512 disaster, the whole nation came together as one to pull through, fully showing that true human love endures. Even when reality buries it, that’s only temporary. Arwen — the elven princess, willing to give up the elves’ eternal life to marry Aragorn, king of Men. To abandon everything she has for the love of a mortal takes immense courage; I hope Aragorn cherishes that feeling. It reminds me of the Chinese story of the Seventh Fairy descending to the mortal world. Hmm, in a human life, love is the noblest pursuit… Personally, I think Arwen’s was probably an unwise choice — both a blessing and a tragedy. What she gave up was not just her own eternal life, but also her family, her people, her country, her glory… Does anyone realize what a huge blow this was to her father? This, this is selfishness. Ah, love is selfish — what does a country matter? What do the people matter? If it were me, I’d choose selfishness too. Selfishness can only satisfy you for a moment, never forever; the bitter fruit of that selfishness is still to come. A lifetime of happiness will eventually fade; one day, life reaches its end, and true love goes with the wind… Pick up, put down; gain, lose; rebirth, reincarnation — never ending. This is the legendary moth drawn to the flame. Exactly — love is a moth to a flame, and life is a moth to a flame. How many people under heaven can stay together through life after life without parting? Don’t believe what the books say: “Love, one knows not where it begins, yet it goes deep. The living may die for it, and the dead may live again. If the living cannot die for it, and the dead cannot live again, then it is not love at its utmost.” Mortals have no way to grasp eternity! I hate the universe’s design — mortals can’t obtain eternity, while those who attain the Way gain only heartlessness. The reason a mortal can become a sage and circulate the heavenly circuit is that it’s premised on comprehending the creation of all things and reaching sufficient energy. One who becomes a sage merges with the universe, lives and dies with it (seen as eternity), creates a living environment for all things in the world, and maintains the natural order at a macro level. That is, it’s the Buddha’s Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, God’s eternal kingdom — the ultimate of all things, perfection, the whole, emptiness, nothingness. But I don’t like it! Heaven and earth are ruthless; they treat all things as straw dogs. The ultimate meaning of life is that there is no meaning — no matter how splendid a life is, it’s no more than smoke before the eyes, as if we’re all just objects in the universe’s grand program. When your mission is done, your memory is freed and you turn into a soul; when the time comes, your memory block is used to create another object, and the new object has instance attributes almost entirely different from the earlier one. You’ll have a new life, with joy and sorrow, birth and death, aging and illness. And so we reincarnate; we have no meaning of our own, and we never get anything in the end. And what can heaven and earth do? Heaven and earth are the same — utterly meaningless. Heaven, earth, and humans play this cyclical game together, playing with themselves, fooling around with themselves — and what comes of it? Nothing at all, and it amounts to nothing. In fact, the universe is just like an online game — nothing but a vast system and a bunch of objects amusing and tormenting themselves. (In this online-game analogy, mortals are the players, and a sage who has attained the Way isn’t a GM but the game’s program logic!) So what if you’re mortal or not? Isn’t the universe itself just something being played with? Sargeras really is a wise one! The meaning of the universe’s existence is destruction — but after the Burning Legion annihilates all things, what then? Even though I’m still living freely and pushing forward positively in life, I’m utterly disappointed in the universe. Peter Pan once said: “Life is a big adventure.” Enjoy the moment. Live the present well. *****Rant over******

title: Watch the entire Lord of the Rings trilogy
content: Yesterday at 2 p.m. I sat down to watch and finished at midnight — nine hours of the trilogy in one go. I took in a bunch of epic battles, witnessed friendship, family, love, and saw both the ugly and the beautiful sides of human nature. Having watched The Lord of the Rings trilogy, it felt like playing one epic game of Heroes of Might and Magic V. Here are a few things I found fun in The Lord of the Rings: At around the 11:47 mark of The Two Towers, the orc leader makes a clenched-fist “stop” gesture… ugh, so orcs use the same hand signals as modern armies… What exactly does Frodo base his deduction about Gollum’s past on? I couldn’t figure it out. He seems to be as sensitive as Lyra in The Golden Compass — Lyra can see the truth through the alethiometer, and Frodo can see the truth through magic possession and near-drowning? In the final siege in The Two Towers, Legolas (the elf archer) uses his shield as a skateboard, shooting while on the move… The army of the dead really is huge — I’d say they alone could wipe out the whole orc host. Watching them come ashore from the ships with scythes and axes raised reminded me of that WOW comic about downing Onyxia, where a horde of humans shouts “damn you” and steamrolls the raid… This army of the dead is like a giant swarm of termites, chewing through everything in its path. They charge up the elephants’ bodies shouting “Damn you——“ and the giant elephants go down immediately… Hmm, “Legendary characters all get a chance to turn back, but they don’t. They press on without hesitation, because their beliefs are unwavering.” That line is a classic. Both are NewLine films, so why did The Golden Compass get so much bad press? I think plot-wise, The Golden Compass leans too heavily on individual heroism — it’s mostly Lyra and her group doing role-play and adventuring — whereas The Lord of the Rings is a massive, multi-thread, multiplayer PvP. As for what the films are getting at, The Golden Compass stresses free will, while The Lord of the Rings packs in a great deal more, using characters from many kingdoms to show the many sides of human nature — the true, the good, the beautiful, and the false, the evil, the ugly. On those two points alone, I think The Lord of the Rings is better than The Golden Compass. That said, it doesn’t mean The Golden Compass isn’t worth watching — I’m really looking forward to the last two films of the His Dark Materials trilogy! title: Stargate Atlantis (SGA) Season 5 has already premiered
content: I only got into the SGA series this year—at the start of the year I binge-watched the first four seasons in one sitting. Privately, I stubbornly maintain that this series’ worldbuilding is a bit absurd. The Ancients’ technology, the birth of the Wrath. Practically every planet’s species is identical to Earth humans, and they all speak English too…. Let’s just chalk that up to the inevitable course of civilizational development—from the classical Dark Ages to the modern era, to a world government, to artificial intelligence, to galaxy-wide prosperity, and then to a whole horde of bug-swarming Wrath who want to devour all the food yet somehow never thought to farm humans… It really doesn’t add up. We humans eat chickens and ducks, so we build farms, help them breed, and only by keeping the natural balance can we keep dominating Earth. But from what the show depicts, the Wrath just wait around for people to breed naturally (and this “waiting” isn’t even an active strategy—most of the time it’s simply that they haven’t found a given human planet -_-), then wipe them out completely. They evolved from bugs, so of course they have no clue what sustainable development is?! I used to complain a lot about this show—probably because I was so obsessed with The X-Files, obsessed to the point of getting lost in that kind of sci-fi masterpiece where you can hardly find a single BUG. No matter how absurd or illogical the worldbuildingcosmology is, this show is still well worth watching and worth looking forward to. The most watchable part is exactly each episode’s plot. Setting the backstory aside and just watching it as a cops-and-robbers or military action show, every episode is full of strategy, a battle of wits and courage. The scientist’s mind and the tactician’s skill work in perfect sync, turning every crisis around and saving the day. Hoho, I really love their combo—unstoppable. Every character is vividly drawn: McKay, Zelenka, Sheppard, Teyla, Ronon, Carter, Weir, Caldwell, and Ford, and so on. Hehe, every smiling face that once stood far away… Now, they’re back! SGA5 premieres in July 2008! Brothers back home, hurry up and subscribe to the updates: http://www.verycd.com/topics/300648/feed! You can already download the first episode on VERYCD! title: SimCity 4 - Reliving a Classic
content: No matter how much of a force I am in strategy games, I’d still rather play simulation-style development games — which is exactly why I like Rise of Nations. Even in CC-General (Command Conquer: Generals), I like to pick the terrorist organization and grow a thriving little Arab town. By comparison, CC3 Tiberium Wars gives you no room to play for development. I’m crazy about CC3, but in the end I found that aside from the absolutely gorgeous battle scenes and a pace so fast your fingers cramp, it never gave me the feeling I was looking for — and the game is so damn huge. At the end of 2007 I played SimCity Societies for a bit (some people translate it as “City of Dreams” — great translation, whoever came up with it must have grasped the essence of this version of the game!). It really does no longer suit the mayors who were devoted to the earlier SimCity games — we mayors took the most pride in macro-level control: zoning land, demolition, rebuilding, improving the city’s traffic layout, adjusting taxes at the macro level, promoting the industries we needed, and eventually watching the city grow bigger and bigger until it became an international metropolis. Every single problem we solved along the way — education traffic fire crime healthcare pollution power and water supply development of agriculture, industry and commerce budget deficits — gave us a huge sense of accomplishment. In “City of Dreams” all of that becomes so simple, so comfortable — maybe the designers thought the earlier SimCity games cost players too many brain cells, that they were too tired and needed a rest, so they gave us a beautiful, fairy-tale, utopian heaven. From then on, mayors could sit back and relax. Or maybe the designers were thinking more about newcomers and completely overturned the SimCity style, building a simulation masterpiece tailor-made for brothers and sisters who have never played SimCity but still have a child’s heart! Why do I say that? Because back when I first played SimCity, I used to fantasize about putting up houses one by one, setting up all kinds of residential public workplace buildings, then building roads to connect them and creating a cozy little town. Heh, and now that naive dream can come true in SimCity! Thanks to the “City of Dreams” development team, thanks to EA. And thanks to all those brothers and sisters who put so much effort into the translation — a lot of the Americanized jokes in SimCity were translated in a thoroughly localized way! I once played “City of Dreams” like a maniac for several all-nighters, because a game like that is just too beautiful, too fairy-tale. But later I chose to give it up. Three reasons: 1. After playing for a while, the screen would freeze for no reason — not a crash; I could click or move the mouse and still hear the game’s sound, but the screen was frozen. Bizarre. Once I switch machines I might keep playing. 2. Playing this game makes me dizzy… 3. Even though I really like that Platonic kind of city development, I’m better suited to the highly strategic SimCity 4. Anyway, a few days ago Wenjun was designing his personal avatar, and the big V inevitably made me think of skyscrapers… which stirred up my desire to be a mayor again. So, unable to resist the powerful urge inside me… there was one more game on my machine: the long-lost SimCity 4 - Formosa. Sorry, I’m not using a legit copy — I’m so poor I can barely cover “food and clothing,” guess I’ll go sell blood… I’m using the http://www.verycd.com/topics/93139/ version. Excited to death. Playing SC4 again now, I already feel completely at home with it — guess I’ve matured a fair bit ^_^ First, let me post a screenshot from last year’s playthrough. This one screenshot alone has plenty of planning problems: The problems: 1. The few high-rise buildings in the upper left of the center definitely have seriously inconvenient traffic access — it’s just a road, and there’s no subway. 2. It’s only year 35; there’s no need to build a highway yet, and budget deficits are bound to show up. Better to build light rail or invest in planning more industrial zones. 3. The location where the school was built — the surrounding residential area doesn’t make sense. Just one street to the north is a tech park, which wastes the community environment. Actually, high-tech parks should go where there are lots of parks green space; those places have location value too. I’ll grab a few more screenshots next time I have time to play.

title: Forum thread about 《仙剑江湖OL》, still very orz
content: This online game is seriously strong — it might just make it big. After all, all kinds of wild, offbeat ideas can be openly explored and built out here. And the dev team’s bold exploration and fearless attitude will make this game grow fast. I browsed the official forum for a bit and found some very entertaining discussions, including this one: Facepalm — the banner up there boldly proclaims “the first large-scale mythological wuxia online game”…. There’s also this thread, “Discussion about the baby-making feature”: Improving in step with the times like this, tagging along right behind God — the player — seeking truth from facts and keeping pace with the times, is bound to succeed. All in all, though, this game really is good. Looks like it was made by Xianjian fans — go in with an appreciative attitude instead of nitpicking and you’ll get a lot of fun out of it. There are quite a few genuinely appealing features: The Six Spirit Orbs return to the jianghu; Shushan, Shaolin, Mingjiao… nine great sects rise together across the jianghu, brawling through the greenwood, blood and slaughter ready to erupt at any moment. Invent your own martial arts and forge your own Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms; found your own sect, carve out your own turf, open a school and become a grandmaster, spreading your heroic name across a hundred li of jianghu. The rich run escort jobs for extra cash — pull it off and be remembered forever; the broke team up to rob the escort wagons — blow it and lose everything. Running escorts through the jianghu: a cautious sailor sails ten thousand years; one wrong step becomes eternal regret. Main quests, side quests. Storylines, daily quests. Special quests, all kinds of quest combinations, setting the jianghu abuzz. It overturns the dull grind of killing mobs to level up, and shakes off the lonely plight of nobody caring about you. Green bosses, gold bosses, purple bosses — the martial heroes rise to fame. Li Xiaoyao, Zhao Ling’er, Yun Tianhe, Han Lingsha; a flawless companion-raising system lets you build your own dream team and bring classic wuxia characters back to life. But I did spot one serious problem: the ICP filing number posted on the homepage of 仙剑江湖OL is fake, and this online game has no business license… I hope it gets fixed quickly. Even if grassroots players carve out their own kingdom, you still have to do things by the law.

title: Just finished watching "Jumper"
content: Finally saw Jumper, which I’d been looking forward to. Disappointed — the plot is a mess, zero logic. Then again, it was always going to be a surreal movie. The female lead is always scowling, like she’s up to her ears in debt. Does the male lead have even a shred of shame? He runs away from home because he’s useless, uses teleportation to rob banks, and even slaps on a note saying “I’ll pay it back someday” — yet never once shows the slightest intention of returning the money. No class whatsoever. With that kind of ability, in his situation, using teleportation to land a delivery job would’ve beaten robbing banks any day! Early on, after he falls into the icy river and teleports his way out, he doesn’t even bother to immediately tell the people there — people who thought he was dead and may even have been trying to rescue him. Talk about self-centered; it makes no sense at all! No sense of responsibility, no social conscience — just a clueless little kid. The female lead starts off with sharp observational skills, but then her view of him flips so abruptly, as if he’d saved her — when really he’s the one who ruined her perfectly good life! Actually, this movie teaches us something too: superpowers must be used sensibly! Abuse them and you’ll get yourself killed. The only thing I liked was the film’s premise: teleportation. From i.Ksharp on Douban: This movie is just perfect for otaku~ Who wouldn’t want to leap past the constraints of distance and time, the pressure of money and work, and live that carefree, godlike life — one second you’re on top of the Sphinx’s head, sipping coffee and soaking up the sun; the next you’re surfing in the Maldives; then you’re off to the Louvre to see da Vinci; and after that, you swing by an NBA game. And if you’re broke, just drop into a bank vault for a quick stroll. Greed is good. It’s an intoxicating, impossible dream, yet it satisfies human desire enormously. If you ever got that ability, how could you not do whatever you pleased?

title: Why so many 囧s?《仙剑江湖OL》
content: Check out the hilarious online games - http://www.i397.com/html/wangyouxinwen/20080706/517.html The most embarrassing knockoff online game in history: “Xianjian Jianghu OL” The knockoff crowd has really infiltrated every corner of our lives. Knockoff phones, knockoff MP3 players, knockoff PSPs, knockoff Wiis are all the rage, and now knockoff online games have even appeared—of course, they must be made by Chinese developers. This game, called “Xianjian Jianghu OL”, uses the Xianjian logo, and the background music on its homepage is also from Xianjian. In the most prominent spot, there’s a slogan: “The first large-scale mythological wuxia online game masterpiece.” Add to that a “permanently free” icon that we couldn’t be more familiar with, and from every angle, it looks absolutely like a standard domestic free-to-play online game. Could this really be an online game version of Xianjian? But starting from the recharge page, there are problems. This game actually accepts recharges from all game point cards, even Q coins! The method is also strange: instead of recharging on the official website, you contact customer service, tell them your password, and they complete the recharge for you. The game appears to have four servers, but actually, no matter which one you choose, you end up on the same server. In other words, the server selection is just there to fool people. If you don’t believe me, look at the server settings: “Mobile Server”. OMG, so this game can be played on a phone? After entering the game, the first thing you see is Sister Shen Qishuang, but why is Sister Qishuang’s character model so chibi? That’s the character design from Cross Gate. Okay, let’s ignore these details for now. But this house looks so familiar, so familiar—where have I seen it before? Cross Gate’s character design Remember now? In Legend of Mir, houses like this are everywhere. “Xianjian Jianghu” took the background and character settings from Xianjian, and also “borrowed” the house models from the world of Legend of Mir. A house from Legend of Mir Then we see Sister Liu Mengli. Besides the same Cross Gate character design, Sister Liu’s avatar just stunned me beyond belief—this, this, this is the default avatar from many forums… I’m gradually feeling the power of this knockoff game—_—! Sister Liu Mengli Next we see Wang Xiaohu. Brother Xiaohu has a middle-aged man avatar here. (According to a tip, these avatars are all selectable avatars from Koei’s Romance of the Three Kingdoms series.) Finally, we meet Ling’er MM, but why is she a maid with a headscarf? And she also looks very familiar, but I really can’t remember whether I’ve seen such a character in Cross Gate or RO. Any sharp-eyed classmate want to fill us in? A maid? We also see Su Mei. Although she has the same avatar as Ling’er, her character model is actually “Dae Jang Geum”! The power of this knockoff game is truly beyond our imagination. Dae Jang Geum? There’s another powerful presence in the game… Alas, this could easily corrupt kids. ………..There are many more awkward moments, especially on the last page. Hurry over to http://www.i397.com/html/wangyouxinwen/20080706/517.html and take a look.

title: Good book
content: I’ve been reading 《大话设计模式》 lately. It really is a great entry-level book on design patterns—plain and accessible, explaining deep ideas in simple terms. You get a feel for the great wisdom embedded in the evolution of design, and for the scenes in the joys and frustrations of a programmer’s life that are worth reliving again and again. The whole book is built around scenario-based dialogue, using a series of short stories or programming examples to explain the 23 design patterns summarized by GoF (the authors of the classic design patterns text—Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software, whose Chinese edition is titled 《设计模式——可复用面向对象软件的基础》: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson and John Vlissides, who are often called the Gang of Four, i.e. the four-person group, GoF for short). The book is divided into 29 chapters. Chapters 1, 3, 4 and 5 focus on what object orientation means, why it’s valuable, and several important design principles; chapter 2, along with chapters 6 through 28, walks through the 23 design patterns in detail; chapter 29 is a comprehensive summary of design patterns. The appendix introduces the basic concepts of object orientation to beginners through the evolution of a single example. What sets the book apart is its playful QA between Xiaocai and Daniao: by walking through the continuous refactoring and evolution of a program, it lowers the barrier to learning design patterns, making it easier for beginners to understand—why is this design the good one? How did anyone arrive at this design? The aim is not only to give readers a “fish” but also to teach them how to fish, guiding them to appreciate the great wisdom contained in the evolution of design. This book is suitable for programming beginners or developers who want to improve their object-oriented programming skills.

title: How to fix session_start() errors in PHP
content: I’m not doing .net for now — I’ve gotten interested in PHP, so I’m learning PHP while working on it. There are a shocking number of baffling things in the beginner stage; good thing I was mentally prepared. Last night I ran into a problem: in PHP, session_start() always threw an error: Warning: session_start() [function.session-start]: Cannot send session cache limiter - headers already sent (output started at D:wwwrootEZineTest.php:1) in D:wwwrootEZineTest.php on line 1 I searched all over the web and found three explanations and fixes for it: There can be no other output before the session_start(); statement (this is mostly the case that reports: Cannot send session cache limiter headers already sent) The session save path isn’t set; you need to change session.save_path “C:phpsession” in php.ini [set the path after it yourself, and make sure it exists. The php.ini file is generally located in the system driveWindows directory] Change session.auto_start 0 in php.ini to session.auto_start 1 I was so frustrated. Point one: my session_start(); statement is on the first line. Point two: it is set. Point three: I don’t want to set it to auto. I was really annoyed. Since I was testing on the server machine at home, I suspected it was a config problem, so I compared its PHP.INI against the config at the data center and found nothing suspicious. In the end I grabbed another PHP file I’d written that used sessions and tested it — and it worked! That proved it wasn’t a config problem. Finally I went ahead and deleted the problem file down to a single line and tested it — it still errored. Heh heh, with the scope narrowed down to that, it suddenly hit me: could this be a file gene problem?! I checked, and sure enough — a UTF-8-encoded PHP source file can’t session_start(); an ANSI one can. Heh, so the problem can be solved: Method 1. Encode all files as non-UTF8; Method 2. Make the PHP engine support UTF-8-encoded source files (the following material is quoted from: http://phorum.study-area.org/index.php/topic,36484.html) ****** Fully adopt UTF-8 across the site. ****** 1. Use vi etchttpdconfhttpd.conf to set the charset in Apache to: (remember to restart) AddDefaultCharset UTF-8 2. Use vi etcphp.ini to set the charset in php to: (remember to restart) default_charset “utf-8” 3. Use vi etcmy.cnf to set the charset in MySQL to: (remember to restart) [mysqld] init_connect’SET NAMES utf8’ default-character-setutf8 [client] default-character-set utf8 4. When creating the database, choose the charset: (remember to clear the DB cache) DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS `aa`; CREATE DATABASE `aa` DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8 COLLATE utf8_unicode_ci; USE `aa`; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `aat` ( `id` char(1) NOT NULL default ‘1’, `myStr` varchar(200) default NULL, PRIMARY KEY (`id`) ) ENGINEMyISAM DEFAULT CHARSETutf8 COLLATEutf8_unicode_ci; 5. Use UltraEdit (v11.20a) to convert all ANSI-format php files to UTF-8 format: File – Conversions – ASCII to UTF-8 (Unicoding Editing) (in UltraEdit press Advanced – configuration – File Handling – UnicodeUTF-8 Detection – check Auto detect utf-8 files). If needed, you can run Remove BOM.php. When you use WinXP’s Notepad to convert a php file from ANSI to UTF-8, the BOM at the head of the file causes layout problems, so it must be removed — running Remove BOM.php removes it automatically. Remove BOM.php can be downloaded from: http://www.hoyo.idv.tw/hoyoweb/document/view.php?sid=13author=hoyostatus=view 6. In the php file you must add: 7. In the file that connects to the DB, you must add 3 lines of mysql_query for it to work: $host”localhost”; $DBname”aa”; $user “root”; $passwd “”; $link mysql_connect($host,$user,$passwd) or die (“Fail”); $db mysql_select_db($DBname, $link) or die (“Fail”); Before you actually query the DB to fetch data, add the following 3 lines mysql_query(“SET NAMES ‘utf8’”); mysql_query(“SET CHARACTER_SET_CLIENTutf8”); mysql_query(“SET CHARACTER_SET_RESULTSutf8”); $sql “select * from aat where crid’1’”; $rows mysql_query($sql); 8. In php files, note this if needed: [Optional] When using htmlentities and htmlspecialchars, do it like this: $chars htmlentities($chars,ENT_QUOTES,”UTF-8”); $chars htmlspecialchars($chars,ENT_QUOTES,”UTF-8”); And before displaying, use $chars html_entity_decode($chars,ENT_QUOTES,”UTF8”); If you’ve used addslashes() or mysql_real_escape_string(), remember to use the following: $chars stripslashes($chars); If needed, you can use the following function to convert between encodings: $chars iconv(‘Big5’,’UTF-8’,$chars); convert from Big5 to UTF-8 Postscript: If you use Notepad to edit a UTF-8 file, saving it automatically adds a BOM header, and this BOM header is 3 bytes of invisible characters that cause PHP to output content too early when executing. Solution: delete the BOM header — you can use the UE text editor to save as UTF-8 text without a BOM header, or you can create a PHP script specifically for stripping BOM headers, put it in the site root directory, and run it once: if (isset($_GET[‘dir’])){ config the basedir$basedir$_GET[‘dir’];}else{$basedir ‘.’;} $auto 1; checkdir($basedir); function checkdir($basedir){if ($dh opendir($basedir)) { while (($file readdir($dh)) ! false) { if ($file ! ‘.’ $file ! ‘..’){ if (!is_dir($basedir.”“.$file)) { echo “filename: $basedir$file “.checkBOM(“$basedir$file”).”“; }else{ $dirname $basedir.”“.$file; checkdir($dirname); } } }closedir($dh);}} function checkBOM ($filename) {global $auto;$contents file_get_contents($filename);$charset[1] substr($contents, 0, 1);$charset[2] substr($contents, 1, 1);$charset[3] substr($contents, 2, 1);if (ord($charset[1]) 239 ord($charset[2]) 187 ord($charset[3]) 191) { if ($auto 1) { $rest substr($contents, 3); rewrite ($filename, $rest); return (“BOM found,automatically removed.”); } else { return (“BOM found. “); }}else return (“BOM Not Found.”);} function rewrite ($filename, $data) {$filenum fopen($filename, “w”);flock($filenum, LOCK_EX);fwrite($filenum, $data);fclose($filenum);}?

title: Come on, brother computer, do us proud!
content: After getting home, I finished putting together the computer I use at school. The day before yesterday I was using it at home when the mouse suddenly died — the scroll wheel lost its scrolling function for no reason and turned into a free-spinning wheel… I swapped in the old mouse from home, and it worked. ^_^ Yesterday morning, the mouse pad was so dusty that the optical sensor couldn’t track properly, so I tossed the mouse pad off to the side to cool down. Yesterday evening, the replacement mouse died too — the wheel rolled, the left and right buttons clicked, but it wouldn’t move. Looked like it had been hit with a paralysis spell… No choice — I went out that night and bought a new mouse… After swapping it in, it worked. ^_^ At noon today it suddenly quit again — movement, scrolling, left and right buttons, all functions gone. It had turned into a statue… I started to suspect the mouse wasn’t the problem. Unplugged and plugged it back in, fixed ^_^ Sweat. Ten minutes later, crippled again… Unplugged and plugged it back in, fixed ^_^ Sweat. Five minutes later, crippled again… Unplugged and plugged it back in, fixed －—－ Sweat. Two minutes later, crippled again… Unplugged and plugged it back in, fixed －.－ Sweat. One minute later, crippled again… Unplugged and plugged it back in, fixed －_－ Sweat. A few seconds later, crippled again… Unplugged and plugged it back in, fixed -_- Sweat. A while later, unplugging and plugging it back in did nothing at all… O_o Plug, unplug, plug, unplug, plug, unplug, plug, unplug — and finally it worked again. To this day I still don’t understand what was going on. Later I got to wondering whether it was just too hot, whether the machine couldn’t take it and the mouse went on strike first as a protest. So I got ready to turn on the air conditioner. Shit… not enough outlets. Number of usable sockets in this area − (tower ×2 + monitor ×2 + switch + ADSLM + audio + TV + air conditioner) required one three-prong outlet short! Sweat! Major sweat!! Genghis Khan!!! No choice — I had to kill one monitor (the one on the old machine at home) for the greater good. The air conditioner finally came on. To keep that computer usable after its monitor was killed, I enabled Remote Desktop on it. And then another problem showed up: too many viruses, interfering with process execution. So I had to reinstall the antivirus again… I downloaded the latest Rising from the machine I was currently using, and it wouldn’t even install! Memory error. Damn viruses. The machine is beyond cure, infected to the bone. Antivirus can’t fix it, so I might as well just reinstall the OS… It mostly just sits there idle anyway, so why not install it as a 2003 server… What? The optical drive is broken?! Sweat! Major sweat!! Genghis Khan!!! I’d say you’re ruthless -_- Come on, computer buddy, show some fight!

title: Fixing the Fanfou AIR Client "Acting Up" Issue
content: Ever since I added the minimize-to-tray feature last time, I’ve been hearing about one “freak-out” paranormal event after another — you type in your own username and password, and the login info that comes up is someone else’s; someone else logs in and your status shows up… This whole freaking-out thing reminds me of Crazy Train, which was all the rage back in the day: “his phlegm can land on your face, your phlegm can land in his mouth… which makes for better protein absorption…” Alright, to fix the protein-absorption problem, I’ve made some more changes. Other people’s phlegm won’t land in your mouth anymore. And if you still get spit on, come find me and settle the score — I’ll let you spit too… While I was at it, I also fixed the cache issue where refreshing sometimes didn’t show the latest status. But this Fanfou AIR is, after all, the first thing I ever built back when I first touched AIR last year, and looking at it now, it has plenty of design flaws. To really fix it, I’d probably have to tear the whole thing down and rewrite it. Forget it — time is tight, so let’s carry on the revolutionary spirit: new Fanfou, old Fanfou, smash the pot and sell the iron, Fanfou again.
